extraction_notes.note: Remark 3.7 asserts an if-and-only-if characterization of good strategies without proof; kept as remark (rigor semi_formal) rather than retyped as claim.

Theorem 9.4 is titled a restatement of Theorem 6.2 but differs (G is a measurement, the strategy hypothesis sentence is dropped), so both are kept with a uses edge 9.4 -> 6.2; Theorem 12.1 is verbatim Theorem 6.3 and was merged into it via also_stated_at.

Section 9.2 proves Lemma 9.1 as a prose construction of H followed by four separate item proofs; the construction is a prose proof node and each item is a claim nested in the lemma, proved by its own proof.

The prose opening Section 12 (WLOG on parameters and derived consistency relations, equations 121-124) is effectively part of the proof of the pasting theorem; emitted as one remark containing those equations.

Section 12 lemmas cite the hypothesis items of the pasting theorem (item:ld-pasting-*), which would make ref edges from the theorem into its own proof chain; these edges are marked mention since they use the hypotheses, not the theorem.
The test itself is only stated inside a boxed figure float; extracted as an algorithm node from the figure body, which the finishing step flags as starting mid-sentence.
The first pasting construction is analysed only by an explicit sketch for constant d; the claim carries rigor semi_formal and the sketch is a proof node.

Informal technical-overview material (BFL induction loop, informal self-improvement statement, Magic Square discussion), the prior-work table, and the toy-model motivation of the second pasting construction were not extracted; the symbol g_ell flagged in the overview is unrelated to its later use.
Propositions 4.26 and 4.29 are attributed to NW19 (Facts 4.20 and 4.29) and marked external even though the paper gives its own proofs.

nodes.name: Raz-Safra theorem
nodes.statement: Suppose Provers~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ pass the $k = 2$ surface-versus-point low-degree test with probability~$1-\epsilon$. Then there exists a degree-$d$ polynomial $g:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf Pr\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = \boldsymbol{a}] \geq 1 - \epsilon - \mathrm{poly}(m) \cdot \mathrm{poly}(d/q). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Passing the plane-versus-point test with probability 1-eps implies agreement 1-eps-poly(m)poly(d/q) with a global degree-d polynomial.
assumptions: Suppose Provers~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ pass the $k = 2$ surface-versus-point low-degree test with probability~$1-\epsilon$.
conclusions: Then there exists a degree-$d$ polynomial $g:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ such that

nodes.name: Polishchuk-Spielman theorem (classical soundness of the low individual degree test)
nodes.statement: Suppose Provers~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ pass the low individual degree test with probability~$1-\epsilon$. Then there exists a polynomial $g:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ with individual degree~$d$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf Pr\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = \boldsymbol{a}] \geq 1 - \mathrm{poly}(m) \cdot (\mathrm{poly}(\epsilon) + \mathrm{poly}(d/q)). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Classical soundness of the low individual degree test with error poly(m)(poly(eps)+poly(d/q)).
assumptions: Suppose Provers~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ pass the low individual degree test with probability~$1-\epsilon$.
conclusions: Then there exists a polynomial $g:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ with individual degree~$d$ such that
nodes.label: thm:classical-test-soundness

nodes.name: Main theorem (informal): quantum soundness of the low individual degree test
nodes.statement: Suppose Provers~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ pass the two-prover. degree-$d$ low individual degree test with probability $1-\epsilon$. Let $A = \{A^u_a\}$ be the measurement the provers perform when they are given the point $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$ to produce a value $a \in \mathbb F_q$. Then there exists a projective measurement $G = \{G_g\}$ whose outcomes~$g$ are polynomials of individual degree~$d$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}\sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \sum_{g:g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes G_g \ket{\psi} \geq 1 - \mathrm{poly}(m) \cdot (\mathrm{poly}(\epsilon) + \mathrm{poly}(d/q)). \end{equation*} In other words, if Prover~$\mathrm{A}$ measures according to~$A^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ to produce $\boldsymbol{a}$ and Prover~$\mathrm{B}$ measures according to~$G$ to produce~$\boldsymbol{g}$, then $\boldsymbol{g}(\boldsymbol{u}) = \boldsymbol{a}$ except with probability $\mathrm{poly}(m) \cdot (\mathrm{poly}(\epsilon) + \mathrm{poly}(d/q))$.

nodes.statement_short: Two entangled provers passing the low individual degree test w.p. 1-eps admit a projective measurement over individual-degree-d polynomials consistent with the points measurement.

Let $A = \{A^u_a\}$ be the measurement the provers perform when they are given the point $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$ to produce a value $a \in \mathbb F_q$.
conclusions: Then there exists a projective measurement $G = \{G_g\}$ whose outcomes~$g$ are polynomials of individual degree~$d$ such that

nodes.name: Bad strategy for the low individual degree test
nodes.statement: Consider the degree-$(d+1)$ polynomial $h(x_1, \ldots, x_m) = x_1^{d+1}$, and suppose that Players~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ play according to the following classical strategy. \begin{itemize} \item[$\circ$] (Player~$\mathrm{A}$): given $\boldsymbol{u} \in \mathbb F_q^m$, return the value $\boldsymbol{a} = h(\boldsymbol{u})$. \item[$\circ$] (Player~$\mathrm{B}$): given the axis parallel line~$\boldsymbol{\ell} = \{\boldsymbol{u} + x \cdot e_{\boldsymbol{i}} \mid x \in \mathbb F_q\}$, act as follows. If $\boldsymbol{i} > 1$, then $h$ is a constant function along~$\boldsymbol{\ell}$, and so return $\boldsymbol{f} = h|_{\boldsymbol{\ell}}$. Otherwise, if $\boldsymbol{i} = 1$, then $h$ is a degree-$(d+1)$ polynomial along~$\boldsymbol{\ell}$. As the verifier expects a degree-$d$ polynomial, simply give up and return $\boldsymbol{f} \equiv 0$. \end{itemize} Using this strategy, $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{u}) = h|_{\boldsymbol{\ell}}(\boldsymbol{u}) = h(\boldsymbol{u}) = \boldsymbol{a}$ whenever $\boldsymbol{i} \neq 1$, which occurs with probability $1- \frac{1}{m}$. Hence, the players pass the degree-$d$ low individual degree test with probability at least $1 -\epsilon$ for $\epsilon = \frac{1}{m}$. However, Player~$\mathrm{A}$ is responding to their questions using the polynomial~$h$ which is degree-$(d+1)$ but not degree-$d$, and so by the aforementioned Schwartz-Zippel lemma, any degree-$d$ polynomial~$g$ will agree with~$h$ on at most a $\frac{d+1}{q}$ fraction of all inputs. This means that the agreement between Player~$\mathrm{A}$'s strategy and any degree-$d$ polynomial~$g$ is at most \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf Pr\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = \boldsymbol{a}] \leq 1 - m \cdot \epsilon + \frac{d+1}{q}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The strategy answering with x_1^{d+1} passes w.p. 1-1/m but is far from every degree-d polynomial, so the poly(m)poly(eps) dependence is necessary.
nodes.label: ex:bad-individual-degree-example

nodes.name: Roles
nodes.statement: The low individual degree test will be played between two provers and a verifier. The two provers are named Player~$\mathrm{A}$ and Player~$\mathrm{B}$. A \emph{role} $r$ is an element of the set $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$. Given a role~$r$, we write $\overline{r}$ for the other element of the set $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$.

nodes.name: Low individual degree test
nodes.statement: Let~$m$ and~$d$ be nonnegative integers. Let $q$ be a prime power. Then the \emph{$(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test} is stated in \Cref{fig:test}.

nodes.name: Symmetric, projective strategy
nodes.statement: A \emph{symmetric, projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test is a tuple $(\psi, A, B, L)$ defined as follows. \begin{itemize} \item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H} \otimes \mathcal{H}$ is a bipartite, permutation-invariant state. \item[$\circ$] $A = \{A^u_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$ and $a \in \mathbb F_q$. For each $u$, $A^u$ is a projective measurement on~$\mathcal{H}$. \item[$\circ$] $B = \{B^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\mathbb F_q^m$ and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \mathbb F_q$. For each $\ell$, $B^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\mathcal{H}$. \item[$\circ$] $L = \{L^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\mathbb F_q^m$ and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \mathbb F_q$. For each $\ell$, $L^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\mathcal{H}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: A permutation-invariant shared state with projective points, axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines measurements used by both players.

nodes.name: General projective strategy
nodes.statement: A \emph{projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test is a tuple $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ defined as follows. \begin{itemize} \item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{B}}$ is a bipartite state. \end{itemize} Furthermore, for each~$w \in \{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$: \begin{itemize} \item[$\circ$] $A^{w} = \{A^{w,u}_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$ and $a \in \mathbb F_q$. For each $u$, $A^{w,u}$ is a projective measurement on~$\mathcal{H}_{w}$. \item[$\circ$] $B^{w} = \{B^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\mathbb F_q^m$ and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \mathbb F_q$. For each $\ell$, $B^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\mathcal{H}_{w}$. \item[$\circ$] $L^w = \{L^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\mathbb F_q^m$ and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \mathbb F_q$. For each $\ell$, $L^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\mathcal{H}_{w}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: A bipartite state with separate projective points, axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines measurements for each player.

nodes.name: Only projective strategies are considered
nodes.statement: Throughout this work, we will only consider projective strategies. So we will henceforth use the terms ``strategy" and ``symmetric strategy'' to refer exclusively to projective strategies and symmetric, projective strategies, respectively. In addition, we will spend the vast majority of this work dealing solely with symmetric strategies, as they are notationally simpler to work with. Much of this work will focus on proving~\Cref{thm:main-induction}, a variant of our main theorem for symmetric strategies. Our main theorem for general strategies, \Cref{thm:main-formal} below, will be proven in \Cref{sec:induction} by a standard reduction to the symmetric case. We will only see these more cumbersome-to-write general strategies in this section, where we state \Cref{thm:main-formal}, and in \Cref{sec:induction}, where we carry out the reduction.

nodes.name: Good strategy
nodes.statement: A strategy is $(\epsilon, \delta, \gamma)$-good if it passes the axis-parallel lines test with probability at least $1-\epsilon$, the self consistency test with probability at least~$1-\delta$, and the diagonal lines test with probability at least~$1-\gamma$.

nodes.name: Characterization of good strategies via consistency
nodes.statement: Using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:comparing-measurements} below, a symmetric strategy is $(\epsilon, \delta, \gamma)$-good if and only if it satisfies the following three conditions. For $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ and $\boldsymbol{u}$ as in the axis-parallel lines test, \begin{equation*} A^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\epsilon} I \otimes B^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}, \quad \text{and} \quad A^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes A^u_a. \end{equation*} And for $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ and $\boldsymbol{u}$ as in the diagonal lines test, \begin{equation*} A^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\gamma} I \otimes L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: A symmetric strategy is good iff points are consistent with axis-parallel lines, with themselves, and with diagonal lines.
nodes.label: rem:good-strat-characterization

nodes.name: Lines measurement in the last direction
nodes.statement: Our proof will be via induction, i.e.\ proving soundness of the $(m+1,q,d)$-low individual degree test using the soundness of the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test. To do this, we will frequently use the axis-parallel line test in the specific case of $i = m+1$. Thus, it will be convenient to introduce the following notation. Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1, q, d)$-low individual degree test, Then for each $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$ we will write $B^u_f$ as shorthand for $B^{\ell}_f$, where $\ell = \{(u, x) \mid x \in \mathbb F_q\}$. For a function $f:\ell \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$, we will also sometimes write $f(x)$ as shorthand for $f(u,x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Shorthand B^u_f for the axis-parallel lines measurement on the line through u in direction m+1.
nodes.label: not:conditioned-on-last-direction

nodes.name: j-restricted diagonal lines test
nodes.statement: Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test. For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$, we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test} as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\boldsymbol{i} = j$. For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test, the line $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\mathbb F_q^m$.

nodes.name: Main theorem: quantum soundness of the low individual degree test
nodes.statement_short: A projective strategy passing w.p. 1-eps yields projective individual-degree-d polynomial measurements for both players, nu-consistent with the points measurements and with each other.
assumptions: Consider a projective strategy
which passes the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\epsilon$.
Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
conclusions: Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
nodes.label: thm:main-formal

nodes.name: Triangle inequality for numbers
nodes.statement: \text{if $\alpha \approx_{\epsilon} \beta$ and $\beta \approx_{\delta} \gamma$, then $\alpha \approx_{\epsilon+\delta}\gamma$.}
assumptions: if $\alpha \approx_{\epsilon} \beta$ and $\beta \approx_{\delta} \gamma$
nodes.label: eq:triangle-inequality-for-numbers

nodes.name: Finite field trace
nodes.statement: The \emph{finite field trace} is the function $\mathrm{tr}:\mathbb F_q \rightarrow \mathbb F_p$ defined as \begin{equation*} \mathrm{tr}[x] = \sum_{\ell=0}^{t-1} x^{p^{\ell}}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Character sum over F_q
nodes.statement: Let $a \in \mathbb F_q$. Then \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot a]} = \left\{\begin{array}{rl} 1 & \text{if $a = 0$},\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array}\right. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The average of omega^{tr[xa]} over x in F_q is 1 if a=0 and 0 otherwise.
assumptions: Let $a \in \mathbb F_q$.
nodes.label: prop:fourier-fact-scalar

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
If $a = 0$, then $\mathrm{tr}[x \cdot a] = 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb F_q$. As a result,  egin{equation*} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[{ oldsymbol{x}} \cdot a]} = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q} \omega^{0} = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q} 1 = 1. \end{equation*} On the other hand, if $a 
eq 0$, then there exists a $y \in \mathbb F_q$ such that $\mathrm{tr}[a \cdot y] 
eq 0$. As a result,  egin{equation*} C := \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[{ oldsymbol{x}} \cdot a]} = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[({ oldsymbol{x}}+y) \cdot a]} = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q} (\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[{ oldsymbol{x}} \cdot a]} \cdot \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[y \cdot a]}) = C \cdot \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[y\cdot a]}. \end{equation*} But because $\mathrm{tr}[y \cdot a] 
eq 0$, $\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[y\cdot a]} 
eq 1$. This implies that $C = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Case split on a=0 versus a nonzero; in the latter case shift x by y to show the average C satisfies C = C omega^{tr[ya]}.

nodes.name: Character sum over F_q^m
nodes.statement: Let $v \in \mathbb F_q^m$. Then \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[\boldsymbol{u} \cdot v]} = \left\{\begin{array}{rl} 1 & \text{if $v = 0$},\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array}\right. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The average of omega^{tr[u.v]} over u in F_q^m is 1 if v=0 and 0 otherwise.
assumptions: Let $v \in \mathbb F_q^m$.
nodes.label: prop:fourier-fact-vector

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: By the linearity of the trace, \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[\boldsymbol{u} \cdot v]} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} (\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[\boldsymbol{u}_1 \cdot v_1]} \cdots \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[\boldsymbol{u}_m \cdot v_m]}) = \prod_{i=1}^m (\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[\boldsymbol{u}_i \cdot v_i]}), \end{equation*} which by \Cref{prop:fourier-fact-scalar} is $1$ if $v_i = 0$ for all $i$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.statement_short: Factor the character over coordinates by linearity of the trace and apply the scalar case.

nodes.name: Polynomials of low individual degree
nodes.statement: Let $q$ be a prime power, and let $m$ and $d$ be nonnegative integers. We define $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ to be the set of polynomials in $\mathbb F_q^m$ with individual degree~$d$.

nodes.name: Individual degree means at most d
nodes.statement: Note that as defined in \Cref{sec:intro}, in this work a polynomial with individual degree~$d$ is one in which the degree~$d_i$ of each coordinate~$i$ is \emph{at most~$d$}. This allows us to say ``individual degree~$d$'' rather than the wordier ``individual degree at most~$d$''. For example, under this definition, $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ is contained in $\polyfunc{m}{q}{d+1}$ for each~$d$.

nodes.name: Schwartz-Zippel lemma
nodes.statement: Let $g, h:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ be two distinct polynomials of total degree~$d$. Then \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf Pr\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}[g({\boldsymbol{x}}) = h({\boldsymbol{x}})] \leq \frac{d}{q}. \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let $g, h:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ be two distinct polynomials of total degree~$d$.
nodes.label: lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree

nodes.name: Schwartz-Zippel for individual degree
nodes.statement: Let $g, h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ be distinct. Then \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf Pr\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}[g({\boldsymbol{x}}) = h({\boldsymbol{x}})] \leq \frac{md}{q}. \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let $g, h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ be distinct.

nodes.name: Measurements and sub-measurements
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a Hilbert space and $\mathcal{A}$ be a set of outcomes. A \emph{sub-measurement} is a set of Hermitian, positive-semidefinite matrices $A = \{A_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ acting on~$\mathcal{H}$ such that $\sum_a A_a \leq I$. The sub-measurement is \emph{projective} if $(A_a)^2 = A_a$ for each~$a$. It is a \emph{measurement} if it satisfies the stronger condition $\sum_a A_a = I$.
nodes.statement_short: Sub-measurements are PSD families summing to at most I; measurements sum to I; projective means each element is a projector.

nodes.name: Low-degree polynomial measurements
nodes.statement: We write $\polysub{m}{q}{d}$ for the set of sub-measurements $G=\{G_g\}$ with outcomes $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$. We write $\polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ for the subset of $\polysub{m}{q}{d}$ containing only those $G = \{G_g\}$ which are measurements.

nodes.name: Post-processing measurements
nodes.statement: Let $A = \{A_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a set of matrices, and let $f:\mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathcal{B}$ be a function. Then for each $b \in \mathcal{B}$, we define the matrix \begin{equation*} A_{[f(a)=b]} = \sum_{a:f(a)=b} A_a. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: def:post-processing

nodes.name: Post-processing notation compared with prior work
nodes.statement: We note that \Cref{def:post-processing} agrees with the notation for post-processing measurements used in \cite{NW19}, but it disagrees with the notation used in \cite{JNV+20}. That work uses the notation ``$A_{[f(\cdot)=b]}$'' rather than the notation ``$A_{[f(a)=b]}$'' that we use in this work.

nodes.name: Post-processing preserves (sub-)measurements
nodes.statement: Let $A = \{A_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a set of matrices, and let $f:\mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathcal{B}$ be a function. Then \begin{equation*} \sum_a A_a = \sum_b A_{[f(a)=b]}. \end{equation*} Thus, if~$\{A_a\}$ is a sub-measurement (respectively, measurement), then~$\{A_{[f(a)=b]}\}$ is also a sub-measurement (respectively, measurement).
assumptions: Let $A = \{A_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a set of matrices,
let $f:\mathcal{A} \rightarrow \mathcal{B}$ be a function.
conclusions: then~$\{A_{[f(a)=b]}\}$ is also a sub-measurement (respectively, measurement).

nodes.name: Ambiguity of post-processing notation
nodes.statement: We note that there is some ambiguity in the notation $A_{[f(a)=b]}$ because it requires one to know which of~$f$ or~$a$ is the measurement outcome and which is the function applied to it. For example, given a sub-measurement $G = \{G_g\} \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$, we will often consider evaluating its outputs at a point $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$. This entails looking at the sub-measurement \begin{equation*} \{G_{[g(u)=a]}\}_{a \in \mathbb F_q}, \quad \text{where} \quad G_{[g(u)=a]} = \sum_{g:g(u) = a} G_g. \end{equation*} Here, $g$ is the measurement outcome of~$G$, and the function being applied maps it to its evaluation on the point~$u$, i.e.\ $g(u)$. In general, it should always be clear from context what the measurement outcome and the function being applied to it are.
nodes.statement_short: In G_{[g(u)=a]}, g is the outcome and evaluation at u is the post-processing function.

nodes.name: Measurements indexed by questions
nodes.statement: We will frequently encounter sets of sub-measurements $A^x= \{A^x_{a}\}$ indexed by elements~$x$ from a set of ``questions" $\mathcal{X}$. We will write $A = \{A^x_a\}$ for this set. We will typically refer to this set~$A$ as a sub-measurement, and we will refer to it as a measurement if each~$A^x$ is a measurement. In addition, we will refer to it as projective if each~$A^x$ is projective.

nodes.name: Complete part of sub-measurement
nodes.statement: Given a sub-measurement~$A = \{A_a\}$, we will write $A = \sum_a A_a$. Similarly, given a sub-measurement~$A = \{A^x_a\}$, we will write $A^x = \sum_a A^x_a$ and $A = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}$.

nodes.name: Completion of a sub-measurement
nodes.statement: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a sub-measurement. We define the \emph{completion of~$A$}, denoted $\mathrm{completion}(A)$, to be the measurement $\widehat{A} = \{\widehat{A}^x_a\}$ with outcome set $\widehat{\mathcal{A}} = \mathcal{A} \cup \{\bot\}$ such that for each $a \in \widehat{\mathcal{A}}$, \begin{equation*} A^x_a = \left\{\begin{array}{cl} A^x_a & \text{if $a \in \mathcal{A}$,}\\ I - A^x & \text{if $a = \bot$}. \end{array}\right. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Add the incomplete part I - A^x as an extra outcome bot to turn a sub-measurement into a measurement.
nodes.label: def:measurement-completion

nodes.name: Consistency
nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state in $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{B}}$. Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{B}}$. Finally, let $\mathcal{D}$ be a distribution on the question set~$\mathcal{X}$. Then we say that \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a \end{equation*} on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mathcal{D}$ if \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathcal{D}} \sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi} \leq \delta. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A is delta-consistent with B if the probability of distinct outcomes, averaged over questions, is at most delta.
nodes.label: def:simeq

nodes.name: Equation (2)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathcal{D}} \sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi} \leq \delta.
nodes.label: eq:no-big-Oh

nodes.name: Simplifying notation for consistency
nodes.statement: Because the state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mathcal{D}$ are typically clear from context, we will often write ``$ A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a$" as shorthand for ``$ A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a$ on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mathcal{D}$". In the case when $\mathcal{D}$ is not clear by context, we might specify it implicitly in terms of a random variable~${\boldsymbol{x}}$ distributed according to~$\mathcal{D}$. For example, suppose the distribution~$\mathcal{D}$ is supposed to be uniform on the question set $\mathbb F_q$. Then we might say ``on average over ${\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q$, \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a" \end{equation*} as shorthand for ``$ A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a$ on distribution $\mathcal{D}$".

nodes.name: Consistency for measurements
nodes.statement: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be two measurements. Then \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a \end{equation*} if and only if \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \geq 1 - \delta. \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be two measurements.
conclusions: A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a \end{equation*} if and only if
nodes.label: prop:simeq-for-measurements

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We compute \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a \neq b}\bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b \bra{\psi} \Big(\sum_{a \neq b} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a\Big) \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b\ket{\psi}\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b \bra{\psi} (I - A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b) \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b\ket{\psi} \tag{because~$A$ is a measurement}\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b \bra{\psi} I \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b\ket{\psi} - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b\ket{\psi}\\ =~&1 - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b\ket{\psi}. \tag{because~$B$ is a measurement} \end{align*} Hence, the first expression is at most~$\delta$ if and only if the last one is as well, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation using that A and B are measurements to rewrite the disagreement as 1 minus the agreement.

nodes.name: Equation (3)
nodes.statement: B^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\epsilon} I \otimes C^x_a?
nodes.label: eq:can-we-use-approx-delta-to-derive-this

nodes.name: The state-dependent distance
nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state in $\mathcal{H}$. Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be sets of matrices acting on $\mathcal{H}$. Finally, let $\mathcal{D}$ be a distribution on the question set~$\mathcal{X}$. Then we say that \begin{equation*} A^x_a \approx_{\delta} B^x_a \end{equation*} on state $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mathcal{D}$ if \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathcal{D}} \sum_{a} \Vert (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 \leq \delta. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: A and B are delta-close if the average over questions of sum_a ||(A_a - B_a)psi||^2 is at most delta.
nodes.label: def:approx_delta

nodes.name: Transferring consistency using the state-dependent distance
nodes.statement: Let $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ be measurements, and let $\{C^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement. Suppose that $A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes C^x_a$ and $A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{\epsilon} B^x_a \otimes I$. Then $B^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta + \sqrt{\epsilon}} I \otimes C^x_a$.
assumptions: Let $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ be measurements,
let $\{C^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement.
Suppose that $A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes C^x_a$ and $A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{\epsilon} B^x_a \otimes I$.
nodes.label: prop:triangle-sub

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
First, we can rewrite the consistency between $A$ and $C$ as  egin{align*} \delta \geq \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a 
eq b}  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi} & = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a}  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes (C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}} - C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} \ & = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a}  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \ket{\psi} - \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a}  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \ & = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}}  ra{\psi} I \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \ket{\psi} - \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a}  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} 	ag{because~$A$ is a measurement}\ & =  ra{\psi} I \otimes C \ket{\psi} - \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}. \end{align*} Likewise, we can rewrite the inconsistency between $B$ and $C$ as  egin{align*} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a 
eq b}  ra{\psi} B^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi} &=  ra{\psi} I \otimes C \ket{\psi} - \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a  ra{\psi} B^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}. \end{align*} We want to show that the inconsistency between~$B$ and~$C$ is close to the inconsistency between $A$ and $B$. In particular, we claim that  egin{equation*} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a 
eq b}  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\epsilon}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a 
eq b}  ra{\psi} B^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi}. \end{equation*} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference using Cauchy-Schwarz.  egin{align*} & \Big| \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a }  ra{\psi} (A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a) \otimes C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a\ket{\psi} \Big| 
onumber \ \leq~& \sqrt{ \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a}  ra{\psi} (A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a}  ra{\psi} I \otimes (C^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}} \ \leq~& \sqrt{\epsilon} \cdot 1. 	ag{because~$C$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*} This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite both inconsistencies in terms of the agreement with C and bound their difference by Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Consistency implies state-dependent closeness for measurements
nodes.statement: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be two measurements such that \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a. \end{equation*} Then \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{2\delta} I \otimes B^x_a. \end{equation*} This is an ``if and only if'' if~$A$ and~$B$ are both projective measurements.
assumptions: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be two measurements such that
A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a.
conclusions: This is an ``if and only if'' if~$A$ and~$B$ are both projective measurements.
also_stated_at: As just one example among many, when $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ are projective measurements, the ``$\approx_\delta$" and ``$\simeq_\delta$" distances are equivalent.
nodes.label: prop:simeq-to-approx

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Our goal is to bound \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a\Vert (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi} +\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} I \otimes (B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi} - 2 \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} +\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} I \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} - 2 \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}\\ =~&2 - 2 \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$A$ and~$B$ are measurements}\\ \leq~& 2 - 2 \cdot(1-\delta) \tag{by~\Cref{prop:simeq-for-measurements} and the fact that~$A$ and~$B$ are measurements}\\ =~&2 \delta. \end{align*} This completes the proof. When $A$ and~$B$ are projective, ``if and only if'' follows from the first inequality becoming an equality.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the squared norm, use that measurement elements are at most their squares, and apply the consistency-for-measurements characterization.

nodes.name: Consistency does not imply closeness for sub-measurements
nodes.statement: We note that \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx} certainly does \emph{not} hold for sub-measurements. For example, if $A^x_a = 0$ for all~$a$, then $A_a^x \otimes I \simeq_{0} I \otimes B_a^x$, but \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \Vert (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)\ket{\psi} \Vert^2 = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \Vert (I \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)\ket{\psi} \Vert^2, \end{equation*} which is nonzero unless $(I \otimes B^x_a) \ket{\psi} = 0$ for all~$x$ and~$a$.
nodes.statement_short: The zero sub-measurement is 0-consistent with any B but far from it in state-dependent distance.

nodes.name: Closeness of inner products
nodes.statement: Let $\{A^x_a\}$, $\{B^x_a\}$, and $\{C^x_{a,b} \}$ be matrices. Suppose that $A^x_a \approx_\gamma B^x_a$ and that for all~$x$, $\sum_a (\sum_b C^x_{a,b}) (\sum_b C^x_{a,b})^\dagger \leq I$. Then \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\gamma}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \,. \end{equation} Similarly, suppose that $(A^x_a)^\dagger \approx_\gamma (B^x_a)^\dagger$ and that for all~$x$, $\sum_a (\sum_b C^x_{a,b})^\dagger (\sum_b C^x_{a,b}) \leq I$. Then \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\gamma}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} \ket{\psi} \,. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.4.3 Deriving consistency relations from the state-dependent distance
nodes.statement_short: If A is gamma-close to B and the C-matrices are suitably bounded, the inner products with A and B differ by at most sqrt(gamma).
assumptions: Let $\{A^x_a\}$, $\{B^x_a\}$, and $\{C^x_{a,b} \}$ be matrices.
Suppose that $A^x_a \approx_\gamma B^x_a$ and that for all~$x$, $\sum_a (\sum_b C^x_{a,b}) (\sum_b C^x_{a,b})^\dagger \leq I$.
nodes.label: prop:closeness-of-ip

nodes.name: Equation (4)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\gamma}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \,.
nodes.section: 4.4.3 Deriving consistency relations from the state-dependent distance
nodes.label: eq:closeness3

nodes.name: Equation (5)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\gamma}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} \ket{\psi} \,.
nodes.section: 4.4.3 Deriving consistency relations from the state-dependent distance
nodes.label: eq:closeness4

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We begin by showing~\Cref{eq:closeness3}. \begin{align*} &\Big | \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} \Big | \\ &= \Big | \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} \Big ( \sum_b C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} \Big ) \cdot (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} \Big |\\ &\leq \Big ( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Big(\sum_b C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b}\Big) \Big(\sum_b C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b}\Big)^\dagger \ket{\psi} \Big )^{1/2} \cdot \Big ( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^\dagger (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} \Big)^{1/2} \\ &\leq \sqrt{\gamma}. \end{align*} The third line uses Cauchy-Schwarz, and the fourth line uses the assumption $\sum_a (\sum_b C^x_{a,b}) (\sum_b C^x_{a,b})^\dagger \leq I$ to bound the first factor by $1$ and the assumption $A^x_a \approx_\gamma B^x_a$ to bound the second factor by $\sqrt{\gamma}$. As for \Cref{eq:closeness4}, we want to bound \begin{equation*} \Big | \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} \ket{\psi} \Big | = \Big | \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} (C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b})^\dagger ((A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^\dagger - (B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^\dagger) \ket{\psi} \Big |. \end{equation*} It then follows from \Cref{eq:closeness3} that this is at most $\sqrt{\gamma}$.
nodes.section: 4.4.3 Deriving consistency relations from the state-dependent distance
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz on the difference, bounding one factor by the operator-norm assumption; the second statement follows by taking adjoints.

nodes.name: Simple closeness of inner products for sub-measurements
nodes.statement: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$, $B = \{B^x_a\}$, and $C = \{C^x_a\}$ be sub-measurements such that $A^x_a \approx_{\delta} B^x_a$. Then \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 4.4.3 Deriving consistency relations from the state-dependent distance
assumptions: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$, $B = \{B^x_a\}$, and $C = \{C^x_a\}$ be sub-measurements such that $A^x_a \approx_{\delta} B^x_a$.
nodes.label: prop:easy-approx-from-approx-delta

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big| \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \cdot (C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq~& \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}}\\ \leq~& \sqrt{\delta} \cdot \sqrt{1}. \end{align*} This completes the proof.
nodes.section: 4.4.3 Deriving consistency relations from the state-dependent distance
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz on the difference, using that C is a sub-measurement.

nodes.name: Left multiplication preserves state-dependent closeness
nodes.statement: Let $\{A^x_a\}, \{B^x_a\},$ and $\{C^x_{a,b}\}$ be matrices. Suppose that $A^{x}_a \approx_\delta B^{x}_a$ and that for all $x$ and $a$, $\sum_b (C^{x}_{a,b})^\dagger (C^{x}_{a,b}) \leq I$. Then \[ C^{x}_{a,b} A^x_{a} \approx_{\delta} C^{x}_{a,b} B^{x}_a. \]
nodes.section: 4.4.3 Deriving consistency relations from the state-dependent distance
assumptions: Let $\{A^x_a\}, \{B^x_a\},$ and $\{C^x_{a,b}\}$ be matrices.
Suppose that $A^{x}_a \approx_\delta B^{x}_a$ and that for all $x$ and $a$, $\sum_b (C^{x}_{a,b})^\dagger (C^{x}_{a,b}) \leq I$.
nodes.label: prop:cab-approx-delta

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The error we wish to bound is \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^\dagger (C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b})^\dagger C^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a,b} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} &\leq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^\dagger (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} \\ &\leq \delta. \qedhere \end{align*}
nodes.section: 4.4.3 Deriving consistency relations from the state-dependent distance
nodes.statement_short: Bound the error directly using the operator inequality on the C matrices.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality for vectors squared
nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\psi_1}, \ldots, \ket{\psi_k}$ be vectors. Then \begin{equation*} \Vert \ket{\psi_1} + \cdots + \ket{\psi_k} \Vert^2 \leq k \cdot(\Vert \ket{\psi_1}\Vert^2 + \cdots + \Vert \ket{\psi_k}\Vert^2). \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let $\ket{\psi_1}, \ldots, \ket{\psi_k}$ be vectors.
nodes.label: prop:triangle-inequality-for-vectors-squared

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: First, if $x_1, \ldots, x_k \in \mathbb R$, then \begin{equation} (x_1 + \cdots + x_k)^2 = \sum_{i, j= 1}^k x_i x_j \leq \sum_{i, j= 1}^k \frac{x_i^2 + x_j^2}{2} = \sum_{i, j= 1}^k x_i^2 = \sum_{i=1}^k k \cdot x_i^2. \end{equation} Next, by the triangle inequality \begin{align*} \Vert \ket{\psi_1} + \cdots + \ket{\psi_k} \Vert^2 & = (\Vert \ket{\psi_1} + \cdots + \ket{\psi_k} \Vert)^2\\ & \leq (\Vert \ket{\psi_1}\Vert + \cdots + \Vert \ket{\psi_k} \Vert)^2\\ & \leq k \cdot(\Vert \ket{\psi_1}\Vert^2 + \cdots + \Vert \ket{\psi_k}\Vert^2). \end{align*} where the last step uses \Cref{eq:prop-for-real-numbers} applied to the case of $x_i = \Vert \ket{\psi_i}\Vert$.
nodes.statement_short: Prove the scalar inequality by AM-GM, then combine with the triangle inequality for norms.

nodes.name: Equation (6)
nodes.statement: (x_1 + \cdots + x_k)^2 = \sum_{i, j= 1}^k x_i x_j \leq \sum_{i, j= 1}^k \frac{x_i^2 + x_j^2}{2} = \sum_{i, j= 1}^k x_i^2 = \sum_{i=1}^k k \cdot x_i^2.
nodes.label: eq:prop-for-real-numbers

nodes.name: Triangle inequality for the state-dependent distance
nodes.statement: Suppose $A_1 = \{(A_1)^x_a\}, \ldots, A_{k+1} = \{(A_{k+1})^x_a\}$ is a set of matrices such that \begin{equation*} (A_i)^x_a \approx_{\delta_i} (A_{i+1})^x_a \end{equation*} for all $i \in [k]$. Then \begin{equation*} (A_1)^x_a \approx_{k \cdot (\delta_1 + \cdots + \delta_{k})} (A_{k+1})^x_a. \end{equation*}
assumptions: Suppose $A_1 = \{(A_1)^x_a\}, \ldots, A_{k+1} = \{(A_{k+1})^x_a\}$ is a set of matrices such that
(A_i)^x_a \approx_{\delta_i} (A_{i+1})^x_a
nodes.label: prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We want to bound \begin{align*} &~\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{x}} \sum_a \Vert ((A_1)^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - (A_{k+1})^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\\ = &~\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{x}} \sum_a \Vert (((A_1)^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - (A_2)^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) + \cdots.+ ((A_{k})^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - (A_{k+1})^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a))\ket{\psi}\Vert^2\\ \leq &~\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{x}} \sum_a k\cdot(\Vert ((A_1)^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - (A_2)^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 + \cdots.+ \Vert((A_k)^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - (A_{k+1})^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)\ket{\psi}\Vert^2)\\ \leq &~k\cdot(\delta_1 + \cdots + \delta_{k}), \end{align*} where the inequality uses \Cref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-vectors-squared} applied to the vectors $((A_i)^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - (A_{i+1})^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi}$ for $i \in [k]$.
nodes.statement_short: Telescope the difference and apply the triangle inequality for vectors squared.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality for consistency
nodes.statement: Suppose that $A$, $B$, $C$, and~$D$ are measurements such that \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\epsilon} I \otimes B^x_a, \quad C^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a, \quad C^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\gamma} I \otimes D^x_a. \end{equation*} Then \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\epsilon + 2\sqrt{\delta + \gamma}} I \otimes D^x_a. \end{equation*}
assumptions: Suppose that $A$, $B$, $C$, and~$D$ are measurements such that
nodes.label: prop:simeq-triangle-inequality

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Because $B$, $C$, and~$D$ are measurements, \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx} implies that \begin{equation*} C^x_a \otimes I \approx_{2\delta} I \otimes B^x_a, \quad C^x_a \otimes I \approx_{2\gamma} I \otimes D^x_a. \end{equation*} The triangle inequality, \Cref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}, then implies that \begin{equation*} I \otimes B^x_a \approx_{4 \delta + 4 \gamma} I \otimes D^x_a. \end{equation*} Finally, \Cref{prop:triangle-sub} implies that \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\epsilon + \sqrt{4 \delta + 4 \gamma}} I \otimes D^x_a. \end{equation*} This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Convert consistency to state-dependent closeness, chain by the triangle inequality, and transfer back.

nodes.name: Data processing for consistency
nodes.statement: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be two measurements such that \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a. \end{equation*} Then for any function~$f$, \begin{equation*} A^x_{[f(a)=b]} \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_{[f(a)=b]}. \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ and $B = \{B^x_a\}$ be two measurements such that
A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes B^x_a.
nodes.label: prop:simeq-data-processing

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
We want to bound  egin{align*} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{b 
eq b'}  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b]} \otimes B^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b']}\ket{\psi} & = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{b 
eq b'} \sum_{a: f(a) = b} \sum_{a': f(a') = b'}  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{a} \otimes B^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{a'}\ket{\psi}\ & \leq \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a 
eq a'}  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{a} \otimes B^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{a'}\ket{\psi}\ & \leq \delta. \end{align*} This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Disagreements after post-processing are a subset of the original disagreements.

nodes.name: Consistency with a measurement gives closeness
nodes.statement: Let $\{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement and let $\{B^x_a\}$ be a measurement such that on average over $x$, \[ A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_\gamma I \otimes B^x_a \,. \] Then the following hold \begin{gather} A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{\gamma} A^x_a \otimes B^x_a \approx_{\gamma} A^x \otimes B^x_a, \end{gather} where $A^x = \sum_a A^x_a$. As a result, by \Cref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}, \begin{equation*} A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{4\gamma} A^x \otimes B^x_a \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let $\{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement and let $\{B^x_a\}$ be a measurement such that on average over $x$,
A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_\gamma I \otimes B^x_a \,.
nodes.label: prop:cons-sub-meas

nodes.name: Equation (7)
nodes.statement: A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{\gamma} A^x_a \otimes B^x_a \approx_{\gamma} A^x \otimes B^x_a,
nodes.label: eq:closeness5

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We establish the first approximation in \Cref{eq:closeness5}: \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Big (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes (I - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \Big)^2 \ket{\psi} \\ &\leq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes (I - B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} \\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{\substack{a,b : \\ b \neq a}} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi} \\ &\leq \gamma \,. \end{align*} The first inequality folows from the fact that $A^x_a \otimes (I - B^x_a)$ has operator norm at most $1$, and the third line follows from the fact that $\{B^x_b\}$ is a complete measurement, and the last line follows from the assumption of consistency between the $A$ and $B$ (sub-)measurements. To establish the second approximation in \Cref{eq:closeness5}, we compute the difference: \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Big ( (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} - A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \Big)^2 \ket{\psi} \\ &\leq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} - A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{\substack{a,a' : \\ a \neq a'}} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{a'} \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \\ &\leq \gamma \,. \end{align*} The second line follows from the fact that $(A^x - A^x_a) \otimes B^x_a$ has operator norm at most $1$, and the last inequality follows from the consistency between the $A$ and $B$ (sub-)measurements.
nodes.statement_short: Bound each squared difference by the inconsistency using operator-norm bounds and completeness of B.

nodes.name: Switching sandwiched operators
nodes.statement: Suppose $\{A^x_a\}$ is a projective sub-measurement satisfying \begin{equation} A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{\delta} I \otimes A^x_a. \end{equation} Then for any $0 \leq B \leq I$, the following holds: \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a B A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{2\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} B \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} BA^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} \end{equation}
assumptions: Suppose $\{A^x_a\}$ is a projective sub-measurement satisfying
A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{\delta} I \otimes A^x_a.
Then for any $0 \leq B \leq I$, the following holds:

nodes.name: Equation (8)
nodes.statement: A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{\delta} I \otimes A^x_a.
nodes.label: eq:Aapproxd

nodes.name: Equation (9)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a B A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{2\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} B \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} BA^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi}
nodes.label: eq:switch-sandwich

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We will show the first approximation in \Cref{eq:switch-sandwich} in two steps. First, we show that \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a B A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a B \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To do so, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big| \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a B \otimes I)\cdot (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi} \Big|\\ \leq~& \Big( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a B^2 A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Big)^{1/2} \cdot \Big(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \Big)^{1/2} \\ \leq~& \sqrt{\delta}.\tag{because $B \leq I$ and \eqref{eq:Aapproxd}} \end{align*} Next, we show that \begin{equation*} \eqref{eq:shift-right-A} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a B \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_ a\bra{\psi} B \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}. \end{equation*} To do so, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \cdot(B \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi}\Big| \tag{because~$A$ is projective}\\ \leq~& \Big( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \Big)^{1/2} \cdot \Big(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} B^2 \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \Big)^{1/2} \\ \leq~& \sqrt{\delta}.\tag{because $B \leq I$ and \eqref{eq:Aapproxd}} \end{align*} Thus, the first approximation in \Cref{eq:switch-sandwich} follows. To show the second approximation, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_a \bra{\psi} (B\otimes I) \cdot ( A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a ) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ =~&\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} (B\otimes I)\cdot \sum_a ( A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a ) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq~& \Big( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} B^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Big)^{1/2} \cdot \Big( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \cdot(A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b) \ket{\psi} \Big)^{1/2}. \end{align*} The first term in the product is at most $1$ because $B \leq I$. We bound the expression inside the second square root as follows. \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \cdot(A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b) \ket{\psi} \\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a, b} \bra{\psi}(A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \otimes I + I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b - A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b - A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)\ket{\psi}\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi} + \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_a \bra{\psi} I \otimes (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi} - 2\cdot\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi}A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$A$ is projective} \\ \leq~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi} + \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_a \bra{\psi} I \otimes (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi} - 2\cdot\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi}A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \\ \leq~& \delta, \end{align*} where the last step uses \Cref{eq:Aapproxd}.
nodes.statement_short: Move the projector A_a across the tensor product one factor at a time, bounding each move by Cauchy-Schwarz and self-closeness of A.

nodes.name: Equation (10)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a B A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a B \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}.

nodes.name: Completeness transfer from a projective sub-measurement
nodes.statement: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement and let $P$ be a projective sub-measurement such that $A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{\epsilon} P_a^x \otimes I$. Then \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} P \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 2\sqrt{\epsilon}. \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement
let $P$ be a projective sub-measurement such that $A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{\epsilon} P_a^x \otimes I$.
nodes.label: prop:completeness-transfer-projective-P

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We calculate: \begin{align*} \bra{\psi} P \otimes I \ket{\psi} &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} P^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} \\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (P^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$P$ is projective}\\ &\approx_{\sqrt{\epsilon}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \cdot P^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \tag{by \Cref{prop:easy-approx-from-approx-delta}} \\ &\approx_{\sqrt{\epsilon}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a)^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi} \tag{by \Cref{prop:easy-approx-from-approx-delta}} \\ &\leq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi}\\ & = \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{align*} This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Chain of approximations replacing P by A using projectivity of P and the simple closeness proposition.

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency
nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a permutation-invariant state in $\mathcal{H} \otimes \mathcal{H}$ and let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement acting on~$\mathcal{H}$. Then $A$ is \emph{$\delta$-strongly self consistent} if \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \delta. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: A is delta-strongly self-consistent if both provers measuring A agree except with probability delta relative to A's completeness.
nodes.label: def:strong-self-consistency

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency implies self-consistency
nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a permutation-invariant state, and let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement. If \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \delta \end{equation*} then $A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes A^x_a$. This is an ``if and only if" if $A$ is a measurement.
assumptions: Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a permutation-invariant state,
let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement.
\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \delta
conclusions: This is an ``if and only if" if $A$ is a measurement.
nodes.label: prop:other-two-notions-of-self-consistency

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For a sub-measurement~$A$, \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_b \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes (A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}- A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes (I- A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a) \ket{\psi}\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}. \end{align*} This is at most~$\delta$ if $A$ is $\delta$-strongly self-consistent. On the other hand, if~$A$ is a measurement, then the inequality becomes an equality. Hence, if $A^x_a \otimes I \simeq_{\delta} I \otimes A^x_a$, then $A$ is $\delta$-strongly self-consistent.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the disagreement by completeness minus agreement; for measurements the bound is an equality.

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency implies self-closeness
nodes.statement: Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a permutation-invariant state, and let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement. If \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \delta \end{equation*} then $A^x_a \otimes I \approx_{2\delta} I \otimes A^x_a$. This is an ``if and only if" if $A$ is projective.
assumptions: Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a permutation-invariant state,
let $A = \{A^x_a\}$ be a sub-measurement.
conclusions: This is an ``if and only if" if $A$ is projective.

Our goal is to bound  egin{align} &\mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b \Vert(A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b]} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b]}) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2

onumber\ =~&2\cdot \Big( \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b  ra{\psi} (A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b]})^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b]} \otimes A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b]} \ket{\psi}\Big)
onumber\ \leq~&2\cdot \Big( \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b]} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_b  ra{\psi} A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b]} \otimes A^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[f(a)=b]} \ket{\psi}\Big).

nodes.statement: We calculate: \begin{align*} \bra{\psi} B \otimes I \ket{\psi} &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} \\ &\geq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \\ & \geq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes B^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} - \sqrt{\epsilon} \tag{by \Cref{prop:easy-approx-from-approx-delta}} \\ & \geq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} - 2\sqrt{\epsilon} \tag{by \Cref{prop:easy-approx-from-approx-delta}} \\ & \geq \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \delta - 2\sqrt{\epsilon}. \end{align*} This completes the proof.

Then for any function~$f$, \begin{equation*} P^x_{[f(a)=b]} \otimes I \approx_{8\delta + 8\sqrt{\epsilon}} A_{[f(a)=b]}^x \otimes I. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: We will consider an orthonormal basis for $\mathbb C^{k+1}$ consisting of a vector $\ket{a}$ for each $a \in \mathcal{A}$ and the vector $\ket{\bot}$. Let~$U$ be any unitary such that for each vector $\ket{\psi} \in \mathbb C^d$, \begin{align*} U \cdot (\ket{\psi} \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}}) &= \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} ((A_{a})^{1/2} \ket{\psi}) \otimes \ket{a} + ((1 - A)^{1/2}\ket{\psi}) \otimes \ket{\bot}\\ &= \Big(\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} (A_{a})^{1/2} \otimes \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \otimes \ket{\bot}\Big) \cdot \ket{\psi}. \end{align*} This implies that \begin{equation*} U \cdot (I \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}}) = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} (A_{a})^{1/2} \otimes \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \otimes \ket{\bot}. \end{equation*} Hence, for any $a \in \mathcal{A}$, \begin{equation*} (I \otimes \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}}) = (I \otimes \bra{a}) \cdot \Big(\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} (A_{a})^{1/2} \otimes \ket{a} + (1 - A)^{1/2} \otimes \ket{\bot}\Big) = (A_a)^{1/2}. \end{equation*} Then the desired projective sub-measurement is \[ \widehat{A}_a = U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \otimes \ket{a} \bra{a}) \cdot U. \] This is because \begin{align*} (I \otimes \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot \widehat{A}_{a} \cdot (I \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}}) &=(I \otimes \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot (U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \otimes \ket{a} \bra{a}) \cdot U) \cdot (I \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}})\\ &=(I \otimes \bra{\mathsf{aux}} ) \cdot U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \otimes \ket{a}) \cdot (I\otimes \bra{a}) \cdot U \cdot (I \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}})\\ &= (A_a)^{1/2} \cdot (A_a)^{1/2} = A_a. \end{align*} This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Construct a unitary U mapping psi tensor aux to sum_a sqrt(A_a) psi tensor |a> plus the incomplete part, and conjugate the basis projectors by U.

nodes.name: Example 5.4
nodes.statement:
We now carry out a simple example in which Naimark preserves ``$\simeq_\delta$'' statements without preserving ``$\approx_\delta$'' statements. Let $\ket{\psi}$ be an arbitrary state in $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}} \otimes \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{B}}$, where $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}} = \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{B}} = \mathbb C^d$. In addition, let $A = \{A_0, A_1\}$ and $B = \{B_0, B_1\}$ be the two-outcome measurements in which $A_0 = A_1 = B_0 = B_1 =  rac{1}{2} \cdot I_{d 	imes d}$. Then  egin{align*} \sum_{a 
eq b}  ra{\psi} A_a \otimes B_b\ket{\psi} &=  ra{\psi} A_0 \otimes B_1\ket{\psi} +  ra{\psi} A_1 \otimes B_0\ket{\psi}\ &=  rac{1}{4} \cdot  ra{\psi} I \otimes I \ket{\psi} +  rac{1}{4} \cdot  ra{\psi} I \otimes I \ket{\psi} =  rac{1}{2}, \end{align*} and so $A_a \otimes I \simeq_{1/2} I \otimes A_a$. In addition,  egin{equation*} \sum_a \Vert (A_a \otimes I - I \otimes B_a) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 = \sum_a \Big\Vert \Big( rac{1}{2} \cdot I \otimes I -  rac{1}{2} \cdot I \otimes I\Big) \ket{\psi}\Big\Vert^2 = 0, \end{equation*} and so $A_a \otimes I \approx_0 I \otimes B_a$. Now we carry out the steps of Naimark dilation. Because~$A$ and~$B$ are two-outcome, we will set $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}_{\mathsf{aux}}} = \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{B}_{\mathsf{aux}}} = \mathbb C^2$, spanned by the basis vectors $\ket{0}$ and $\ket{1}$. (\Cref{lem:naimark-helper} actually asks that the auxiliary space have dimension $2+1 = 3$, where the third dimension is spanned by the basis vector $\ket{ ot}$. However, this is unnecessary for this example because~$A$ and~$B$ are measurements rather than sub-measurements.) We will choose our two local auxiliary states to be  egin{equation*} \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} = \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}} = \ket{+} =  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ket{0} +  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ket{1}. \end{equation*} We first construct $\widehat{A}$ by following the proof of \Cref{lem:naimark-helper}. To begin, it asks for~$U$ to be a unitary such that for any $\ket{\phi}$ in $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{A}}$,  egin{align*} U \cdot (\ket{\phi} \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}}) &=U \cdot (\ket{\phi} \otimes \ket{+})\ &= ((A_{0})^{1/2} \ket{\phi}) \otimes \ket{0} + ((A_{1})^{1/2} \ket{\phi}) \otimes \ket{1}\ &= \Big(\Big( rac{1}{2}\cdot I\Big)^{1/2} \ket{\phi}\Big) \otimes \ket{0} + \Big(\Big( rac{1}{2}\cdot I\Big)^{1/2} \ket{\phi}\Big) \otimes \ket{1}\ &= rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \ket{\phi} \otimes \ket{0} +  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \ket{\phi} \otimes \ket{1}\ &= \ket{\phi} \otimes \ket{+}. \end{align*} As a result, we can simply take~$U$ to be the identity matrix. Thus,  egin{equation*} \widehat{A}_a = U^{\dagger} \cdot (I \otimes \ket{a}  ra{a}) \cdot U = I \otimes \ket{a} ra{a}. \end{equation*} By a similar argument, we can take $\widehat{B}_a = I \otimes \ket{a} ra{a}$ for $a \in \{0, 1\}$ as well. Now we set $\ket{\widehat{\psi}} = \ket{\psi}\otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} \otimes \ket{\mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}}$. By \Cref{thm:naimark}, we already know that $\widehat{A}_a \otimes I \approx_0 I \otimes \widehat{B}_a$ on state $\ket{\widehat{\phi}}$ because this holds for the un-hatted state and measurements. On the other hand, we will now show that $\widehat{A}_a \otimes I \approx_{\delta} I \otimes \widehat{B}_a$ only for $\delta \geq 1$, in contrast to the un-hatted case where it holds for $\delta = 0$. To see this, we calculate as follows.  egin{align} &\sum_a \Vert (\widehat{A}_a \otimes I_{\mathrm{B}, \mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}} - I_{\mathrm{A}, \mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} \otimes \widehat{B}_a) \ket{\widehat{\psi}}\Vert^2
onumber\ ={}& \sum_a \Vert ((I_{\mathrm{A}} \otimes \ket{a} ra{a}) \otimes I_{\mathrm{B}, \mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{B}}} - I_{\mathrm{A}, \mathsf{aux}_{\mathrm{A}}} \otimes (I_{\mathrm{B}} \otimes \ket{a} ra{a})) \ket{\psi} \otimes \ket{+} \otimes \ket{+}\Vert^2
onumber\ ={}& \sum_a \Big\Vert \Big( rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \ket{\psi} \otimes \ket{a}\otimes\ket{+} -  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \ket{\psi} \otimes \ket{+} \otimes \ket{a}\Big) \Big\Vert^2
onumber\ ={}& \sum_a  rac{1}{2} \cdot  raket{\psi \mid \psi} \cdot ( ra{a} \otimes  ra{+}-  ra{+} \otimes  ra{a}) \cdot (\ket{a} \otimes \ket{+}- \ket{+} \otimes \ket{a}). \end{align} For each~$a$, we have that  egin{align*} &( ra{a} \otimes  ra{+}-  ra{+} \otimes  ra{a}) \cdot (\ket{a} \otimes \ket{+}- \ket{+} \otimes \ket{a})\ ={}& 2 -  raket{a \mid +} \cdot  raket{+ \mid a} -  raket{+ \mid a} \cdot  raket{a \mid +}\ ={}& 2 -  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} -  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot  rac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\ ={}& 1. \end{align*} Plugging this into \Cref{eq:awefea}, we arrive at our bound.
nodes.statement_short: Two-outcome measurements A_a=B_a=I/2 are 0-close, but after Naimark dilation with |+> auxiliary states they are only 1-close.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Let $A = \{A_a\}$ be a sub-measurement with outcomes $a \in \mathcal{A}$ whose strong self-consistency is \begin{equation*} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes A_a \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_a \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\zeta. \end{equation*} Note that \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} A \otimes A \ket{\psi} = \sum_{a, b} \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes A_b \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes A_a \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\zeta. \end{equation*} Rearranging, \begin{align*} \bra{\psi} A \otimes (I - A)\ket{\psi} &= \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \bra{\psi} A \otimes A \ket{\psi}\\ &\leq (\bra{\psi} A \otimes A \ket{\psi} + \zeta) - \bra{\psi} A \otimes A \ket{\psi} = \zeta. \end{align*} As a result, \begin{align*} \bra{\psi} (I-A) \otimes (I-A) \ket{\psi} &= \bra{\psi} (I-A) \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \bra{\psi} (I-A) \otimes A \ket{\psi}\\ &\geq \bra{\psi} (I-A) \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \zeta. \end{align*} Let $\widehat{A}$ be the POVM measurement with outcomes in $\widehat{\mathcal{A}} = \mathcal{A} \cup \{\bot\}$ defined as \begin{equation*} \widehat{A}_a = \left\{\begin{array}{cl} A_a & \text{if $a \in \mathcal{A}$},\\ (I-A) & \text{if $a = \bot$.} \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} Then the strong self-consistency of $\widehat{A}$ is \begin{align*} \sum_{a \in \widehat{\mathcal{A}}} \bra{\psi} \widehat{A}_a \otimes \widehat{A}_a \ket{\psi} & = \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes A_a \ket{\psi} + \bra{\psi} \widehat{A}_{\bot} \otimes \widehat{A}_{\bot} \ket{\psi}\\ & \geq \Big(\sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \bra{\psi} A_a \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \zeta\Big) + \bra{\psi} (I-A) \otimes (I-A) \ket{\psi}\\ & \geq \Big( \bra{\psi} A \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \zeta\Big) + \Big(\bra{\psi} (I-A) \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \zeta\Big)\\ & = 1 - 2\zeta. \end{align*} Because $\widehat{A}$ is a measurement, \Cref{prop:other-two-notions-of-self-consistency} states that this is equivalent to \begin{equation*} \widehat{A}_a \otimes I \simeq_{2\zeta} I \otimes \widehat{A}_a. \end{equation*} As a result, \Cref{lem:orthonormalization-main-lemma} implies the existence of a projective sub-measurement $\widehat{P} = \{\widehat{P}_a\}_{a \in \widehat{\mathcal{A}}}$ such that \begin{equation*} \widehat{A}_a \otimes I \approx_{84\cdot(2\zeta)^{1/4}} \widehat{P}_a \otimes I. \end{equation*} If we define the projective sub-measurement $P = \{P_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ by $P_a = \widehat{P}_a$ for all $a \in \mathcal{A}$, then \begin{equation*} \sum_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \Vert (A_a - P_a) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 \leq \sum_{a \in \widehat{\mathcal{A}}} \Vert (\widehat{A}_a - \widehat{P}_a) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 \leq 84 \cdot (2\zeta)^{1/4}. \end{equation*} Thus, $A_a \otimes I \approx_{84 \cdot (2\zeta)^{1/4}} P_a \otimes I$. We conclude the proof by noting that $84 \cdot (2\zeta)^{1/4} \leq 100 \cdot \zeta^{1/4}$ because $84 \cdot (2)^{1/4} \approx 99.89\leq100$.
