nodes.label: lem:add-in-u

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement_short: Expand H as an average of H^v, move both A^v factors across using self-consistency, then swap v for u using the global variance bound, each by Cauchy-Schwarz.

nodes.name: Equation (65)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes H^{\boldsymbol{v}}_h \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:expand-that-H

nodes.name: Equation (66)
nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:expand-that-H} \approx_{\sqrt{2\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o) \otimes (T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:move-one

nodes.name: Equation (67)
nodes.statement: \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes (T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}))\ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_h\cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}}.
nodes.label: eq:move-one-cauchy-schwarz

nodes.name: Equation (68)
nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:move-one} \approx_{\sqrt{2\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:move-another

nodes.name: Equation (69)
nodes.statement: &\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o) \otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}\Big|\nonumber\\ &\leq\sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}\nonumber\\ &\quad\cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}}.
nodes.label: eq:move-another-cauchy-schwarz

nodes.name: Equation (70)
nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:move-another} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:change-one

nodes.name: Equation (71)
nodes.statement: \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}.
nodes.label: eq:change-one-cauchy-schwarz

nodes.name: Equation (72)
nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:change-one} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:change-another

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound the completeness of H by <Z> by moving A across twice, then use Z >= A_g and consistency of G with A.

nodes.name: Equation (73)
nodes.statement: \sum_h \bra{\psi} H_h \otimes I \ket{\psi} & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_h \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \cdot T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:bracketize-the-expression

nodes.name: Equation (74)
nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:bracketize-the-expression} \approx_{2\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:yet-another-move-a

nodes.name: Equation (75)
nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:yet-another-move-a} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:mysterious-case-of-the-disappearing-a

nodes.name: Equation (76)
nodes.statement: \sum_h \bra{\psi} H_h \otimes I \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 3\sqrt{\delta}.
nodes.label: eq:gonna-use-this-later-H-versus-Z

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
The inconsistency of~$H$ with~$A$ is  egin{equation} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a 
eq b}  ra{\psi} A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes H_{[h( oldsymbol{u}) = b]} \ket{\psi} = \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a, h: h( oldsymbol{u}) 
eq a}  ra{\psi} A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes H_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} We now apply \Cref{lem:add-in-u} to the right-hand side of \Cref{eq:consistency-with-A-baby-step}. To do so, we set $\mathcal{O} = \mathbb F_q^m$, $M = A$, and $S_u = \{(a, h) : h(u) 
eq a\}$. Then \Cref{lem:add-in-u} implies that  egin{equation*} \eqref{eq:consistency-with-A-baby-step} \approx_{4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a, h: h( oldsymbol{u}) 
eq a}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_a \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})})\otimes T_h \ket{\psi}, \end{equation*} which is equal to~$0$ because~$A$ is projective. This implies that  egin{equation} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a 
eq b}  ra{\psi} A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes H_{[h( oldsymbol{u}) = b]} \ket{\psi} \leq 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}. \end{equation} The proof follows from noting that  egin{align*} 4\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} &= 4 \cdot \sqrt{24 m \cdot\Big(\epsilon + \delta +  rac{md}{q}\Big)}\ &\leq 20 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\ &\leq \zeta. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the technical lemma with M = A; the sandwiched term vanishes by projectivity of A.

nodes.name: Equation (77)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes H_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = b]} \ket{\psi} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a, h: h(\boldsymbol{u}) \neq a} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes H_h \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:consistency-with-A-baby-step

nodes.name: Equation (78)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes H_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = b]} \ket{\psi} \leq 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}.
nodes.label: eq:explicit-bound-for-A-consistency

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
We begin by recording the following facts which follow from the definition of $H^u_h$ and the projectivity of~$A$:  egin{align} H^u_h &= A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)} = A^u_{h(u)} \cdot H^u_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)},\ A^u_{h(u)} \cdot H^u_{h'} \cdot A^u_{h(u)} &= H^u_{h'} \cdot A^u_{h(u)} = (A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^u_{h(u)}) \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h(u) = h'(u)]. \end{align} The strong self-consistency of~$H$ is  egin{equation} \sum_{h\in\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} H_h \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} = \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} H_h^{ oldsymbol{u}} \otimes H_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} We now apply \Cref{lem:add-in-u} to the right-hand side of \Cref{eq:self-consistency-baby-step}. To do so, we set  egin{equation*} 	ext{$\mathcal{O} =\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, $M = H$, and $S_u = \{(h, h) : h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}\}$.} \end{equation*} Then \Cref{lem:add-in-u} implies that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:self-consistency-baby-step} \approx_{4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} \cdot H_h^{ oldsymbol{u}} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Having placed two $A$'s on the left-hand side, we want to show that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:release-the-kraken} \approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} +  rac{md}{q}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} \cdot H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} We note that \eqref{eq:threw-in-h-prime} is at least as big as \eqref{eq:release-the-kraken}. Thus, we want to upper-bound  egin{align} \eqref{eq:threw-in-h-prime}-\eqref{eq:release-the-kraken} & = \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} \cdot H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}
onumber\ & = \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})], \end{align} where the second equality is by~\Cref{eq:h-blt}. To do this, we first show that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:added-indicator} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})]. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference.  egin{multline} \Big|\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} ( (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})]\Big|\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} ( (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \cdot T_{h'} \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}}\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})]}. \end{multline} The term inside the first square root is  egin{align*} &\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h}  ra{\psi} ( (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \cdot  igg(\sum_{h' 
eq h} T_{h'} igg) \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}\ \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})^2 \otimes T_h\ket{\psi},	ag{because $T$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*} But $T \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, and so by \Cref{lem:global-variance-of-points} this expression is at most~$\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$. The term inside the second square root is equal to  egin{equation*} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})], \end{equation*} which is at most~$1$ because $T$ and $H^{ oldsymbol{u}}$ are sub-measurements. Next, we show that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:swapped-u-for-v} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})]. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference.  egin{multline*} \Big|\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})]\Big|\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})]}\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} ( (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \cdot T_{h'} \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}))\otimes T_h\ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*} The term inside the first square root is at most  egin{align} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})\otimes T_h\ket{\psi} & = \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \cdot  igg(\sum_{h' 
eq h} T_{h'} igg) \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}\ & \leq \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})^2\otimes T_h\ket{\psi}	ag{$T$ is a sub-measurement}\ & \leq \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h}  ra{\psi} I \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}	ag{because $A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \leq I$}\ & \leq 1, \end{align} where the last step again uses the fact that~$T$ is a sub-measurement. As for the term inside the second square root, it is equal to the term inside the first square root in \Cref{eq:swapped-u-for-cauchy-schwarz}, which we showed was at most $\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$. Finally, \Cref{eq:swapped-u-for-v-this-time-it's-personal} is equal to  egin{align*} &\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi} \cdot \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})]\ \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  rac{md}{q} 	ag{by Schwartz-Zippel}\ \leq~&  rac{md}{q}. 	ag{by \Cref{eq:gonna-use-this-later}} \end{align*} By~\Cref{eq:h-blt}, \Cref{eq:threw-in-h-prime} is equal to  egin{equation} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} (H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} Now, we show that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:delete-an-A} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} (H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference.  egin{align*} &\Big|\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} (H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\Big|\ &\leq \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}}\ &\quad\cdot \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} ((A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \cdot H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}}. \end{align*} The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$T$ and~$H^{ oldsymbol{u}}$ are sub-measurements. The term inside the second square root is  egin{align*} &\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h}  ra{\psi} ((A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \cdot  igg( \sum_{h'} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} igg) \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\ \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})})^2 \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}. 	ag{because $H^{ oldsymbol{u}}$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*} But $T \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$, and so by \Cref{lem:global-variance-of-points} this expression is at most~$\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$. Next, we show that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:swap-u-for-v-attack-of-the-clones} \approx_{\sqrt{2\delta}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes (T_h \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference.  egin{align*} &\Big|\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} (H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'}\otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}\Big|\ =~&\Big|\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q}  ra{\psi}  igg( \sum_{h'}H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes \sum_{h:h( oldsymbol{v}) = a} T_h  igg) \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_a) \ket{\psi}\Big|\ \leq~& \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q}  ra{\psi}  igg( \sum_{h'}H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes \sum_{h:h( oldsymbol{v}) = a} T_h igg)^2\ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q}  ra{\psi}(A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}}. \end{align*} The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$T$ and~$H^{ oldsymbol{u}}$ are sub-measurements, and the expression inside the second square root is at most~$2\delta$ by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx} and the self-consistency of~$A$. Now, \Cref{eq:move-over-v} is equal to  egin{align*} &\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \sum_{h, h'}  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes (T_h\cdot \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{v}} A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \sum_{h, h'}  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes (T_h\cdot Z)\ket{\psi} 	ag{by \Cref{eq:swap-Z-for-A}}\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \sum_{ h'}  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes Z\ket{\psi} 	ag{because~$T$ is a measurement}\ \geq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \sum_{ h'}  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{v}} A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h'( oldsymbol{v})} \ket{\psi} 	ag{by \Cref{eq:Z-greater-than-A}}\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},  oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{ h'}  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h'( oldsymbol{v})} \ket{\psi}\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a}  ra{\psi} H_{[h( oldsymbol{v})=a]} \otimes A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{a} \ket{\psi}\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a}  ra{\psi} H_{[h( oldsymbol{v})=a]} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a
eq b}  ra{\psi} H_{[h( oldsymbol{v})=a]} \otimes A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{b} \ket{\psi}	ag{because~$A$ is a measurement}\ \geq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a}  ra{\psi} H_{[h( oldsymbol{v})=a]} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} 	ag{by \Cref{eq:explicit-bound-for-A-consistency}}\ =~& \sum_{h}  ra{\psi} H_h \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}. \end{align*} In total, we have shown that  egin{equation*} \sum_{h\in\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} H_h \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_{h}  ra{\psi} H_h \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 7 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} - \sqrt{2\delta} -  rac{md}{q} - 4\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}. \end{equation*} Because  egin{align*} 11 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} + \sqrt{2\delta} +  rac{md}{q} & = 11 \sqrt{24m\cdot\Big(\epsilon + \delta +  rac{md}{q}\Big)} + \sqrt{2\delta} +  rac{md}{q}\ &\leq 55 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big) + 2\sqrt{\delta} + m \cdot (d/q)^{1/2}\ &\leq 57 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\ &\leq \zeta, \end{align*} this concludes the proof of \Cref{item:self-improvement-self}.

nodes.statement: The boundedness of~$H$ is \begin{align*} &\bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes H_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]} \ket{\psi} \\ =~& \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \otimes H_h \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} I \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} +\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_{a, h:h(\boldsymbol{u})\neq a} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$A$ is a measurement}\\ \leq~& \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} I \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} + 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}\tag{by \Cref{eq:explicit-bound-for-A-consistency}}\\ \leq~& 3 \sqrt{\delta} + 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}.\tag{by \Cref{eq:gonna-use-this-later-H-versus-Z}} \end{align*} We can bound the error by \begin{align*} 3 \sqrt{\delta} + 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} & = 3 \sqrt{\delta} + 4 \sqrt{24m\cdot\Big(\epsilon + \delta + \frac{md}{q}\Big)}\\ & \leq 3 \sqrt{\delta} + 20 m\cdot\Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\\ &\leq 23 m\cdot\Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\\ & \leq \zeta. \end{align*} This completes the proof. \qed

nodes.name: Self-improvement (restated for measurements)
nodes.statement: Let $G \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ be a measurement with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^{m}$, \begin{equation*} A^{u}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G_{[g(u)=a]}. \end{equation*} \end{enumerate} Let \begin{equation*} \zeta = 3000m\cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big). \end{equation*} Then there exists a projective sub-measurement $H \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item(Completeness): If $H = \sum_h H_h$, then \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} H \otimes I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\nu)-\zeta. \end{equation*} \item(Consistency with~$A$): On average over $\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m$, \begin{equation*} A^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\zeta} I \otimes H_{[h(u) = a]}. \end{equation*} \item(Strong self-consistency): \begin{equation*} H_h \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes H_h. \end{equation*} \item(Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix~$Z$ such that \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} Z \otimes (I - H) \ket{\psi} \leq \zeta \end{equation*} and for each $h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, \begin{equation*} Z \geq \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}\right). \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}

On average over independent and uniformly random $\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v} \sim \mathbb F_q^m$, \begin{equation*} (A^{u}_a \cdot A^{v}_b) \otimes I \approx_{32\gamma m} (A^{v}_b\cdot A^{u}_a) \otimes I. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The strategy passes the diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma$. Therefore, it passes the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test with probability $1- \gamma\cdot m$. This means that \begin{equation*} A^{u}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\gamma \cdot m} I \otimes L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}, \end{equation*} on average over a uniformly random $\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^{m}$ and a uniformly random line $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ in $\mathbb F_q^m$ containing $\boldsymbol{u}$. By~\Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx}, this implies that \begin{equation} A^{u}_a \otimes I \approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} I \otimes L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}. \end{equation} Let $\boldsymbol{u}$ and $\boldsymbol{v}$ be independent and uniformly random points in $\mathbb F_q^m$. Let $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ be a uniformly random line in $\mathbb F_q^m$ containing both points. (If $\boldsymbol{u}$ and $\boldsymbol{v}$ are distinct, then $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is just the unique line that passes through both of them. Otherwise, $\boldsymbol{u} = \boldsymbol{v}$, and $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is a uniformly random line passing through $\boldsymbol{u}$.) Then the marginal distribution on $\boldsymbol{u}$ and $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is as in \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}, as is the marginal distribution on $\boldsymbol{v}$ and $\boldsymbol{\ell}$. As a result, \begin{align*} (A^{u}_a \cdot A^{v}_b) \otimes I &\approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} A^{u}_a \otimes L^{\ell}_{[f(v)=b]} \tag{by \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}}\\ &\approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} I \otimes (L^{\ell}_{[f(v)=b]} \cdot L^{\ell}_{[f'(u)=a]}) \tag{by \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}}\\ &= I \otimes (L^{\ell}_{[f'(u)=a]} \cdot L^{\ell}_{[f(v)=b]}) \tag{because~$L$ is projective}\\ &\approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} A^{v}_b \otimes L^{\ell}_{[f'(u)=a]} \tag{by \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}}\\ &\approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} (A^{v}_b \cdot A^{u}_a) \otimes I. \tag{by \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \end{align*} The theorem now follows from \Cref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}.
nodes.statement_short: Use the m-restricted diagonal lines test: both points lie on a random line, so each A can be replaced by the projective line measurement, which commutes with itself.

nodes.name: Commutativity of G after evaluation
nodes.statement: Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be an $(\epsilon, \delta, \gamma)$-good symmetric strategy for the $(m+1,q,d)$ low individual degree test. Let $\{G^x\} \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$ be a collection of projective sub-measurements indexed by $x \in \mathbb F_q$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $(\boldsymbol{u}, {\boldsymbol{x}}) \sim \mathbb F_q^{m+1}$, \begin{equation*} A^{u, x}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\zeta} I \otimes G^x_{[g(u)=a]}. \end{equation*} \item (Strong self-consistency): On average over~${\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q$, \begin{equation*} G^x_g \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes G^x_g. \end{equation*} \item (Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix $Z^x$ for each $x \in \mathbb F_q$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}})\otimes Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \ket{\psi} \leq \zeta \end{equation*} and for each $x \in \mathbb F_q$ and $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, \begin{equation*} Z^x \geq \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u}, x}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\right). \end{equation*} \end{enumerate} Let \begin{equation*} \nu = 48 m \cdot (\gamma^{1/2} + \zeta^{1/2}). \end{equation*} Then on average over independent and uniformly random $(\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}), (\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}) \sim \mathbb F_q^{m+1}$, \begin{equation*} G^x_{[g(u) = a]} G^y_{[h(v) = b]} \otimes I \approx_{\nu} G^y_{[h(v) = b]} G^x_{[g(u) = a]} \otimes I. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Evaluated sub-measurements G^x_{[g(u)=a]} and G^y_{[h(v)=b]} approximately commute, with error 48m(gamma^{1/2}+zeta^{1/2}).

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Our goal is to bound the magnitude of \begin{align} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ \approx_{6\sqrt{\gamma(m+1)}} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}. \end{align} where the second line follows from \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} and \Cref{thm:commutativity-points}. We now proceed nearly identically to \Cref{clm:g-comm-stability}. \begin{align} \eqref{eq:just-got-commuted} &=\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b}\sum_{g:g(\boldsymbol{u})=a} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \nonumber\\ &=\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})} \ket{\psi}. \end{align} Then we can bound the magnitude as follows. \begin{multline*} |\eqref{eq:g-comm-stab7}| = \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi} \Big(\sqrt{G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g}\otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b\Big) \cdot \Big(\sqrt{G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g} G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\Big)\ket{\psi} \Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g\otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b\ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*} The term inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$A$ are sub-measurements. The term inside the second square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\ket{\psi}\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\right)\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\ket{\psi}\tag{by~\Cref{item:data-processed-boundedness}}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\zeta.\tag{by~\Cref{item:data-processed-boundedness}} \end{align*} This concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Commute the points measurements, then bound as in the first claim via boundedness.

nodes.name: Commutativity of G
nodes.statement: Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be an $(\epsilon, \delta, \gamma)$-good symmetric strategy for the $(m,q,d)$ low individual degree test. Let $\{G^x\}_{x \in \mathbb F_q}$ denote a set of projective sub-measurements in $\polysub{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $(\boldsymbol{u}, {\boldsymbol{x}}) \sim \mathbb F_q^{m+1}$, \begin{equation*} A^{u, x}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\zeta} I \otimes G^x_{[g(u)=a]}. \end{equation*} \item (Strong self-consistency): On average over~${\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q$, \begin{equation*} G^x_g \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes G^x_g. \end{equation*} \item (Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix $Z^x$ for each $x \in \mathbb F_q$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}})\otimes Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \ket{\psi} \leq \zeta \end{equation*} and for each $x \in \mathbb F_q$ and $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, \begin{equation*} Z^x \geq \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u}, x}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\right). \end{equation*} \end{enumerate} Let \begin{equation*} \nu = 30m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/4}+ \zeta^{1/4} + (d/q)^{1/4} \right). \end{equation*} Then on average over independent and uniformly random $(\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}), (\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}) \sim \mathbb F_q^{m+1}$, \begin{equation*} G^{x}_{g} G^{y}_h \otimes I \approx_{\nu} G^y_h G^x_g \otimes I \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The polynomial sub-measurements G^x_g and G^y_h approximately commute, with error 30m(gamma^{1/4}+zeta^{1/4}+(d/q)^{1/4}).

conclusions: G^{x}_{g} G^{y}_h \otimes I \approx_{\nu} G^y_h G^x_g \otimes I

nodes.name: Normalization condition for sandwiched sub-measurements
nodes.statement: Let $P = \{P_a\}$ be a sub-measurement and $Q = \{Q_b\}$ be a projective sub-measurement. Define $C_{a, b} = Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_b$. Then $ \sum_a (\sum_b C_{a, b})^\dagger (\sum_b C_{a, b}) = \sum_a (\sum_b C_{a, b}) (\sum_b C_{a, b})^\dagger \leq I. $
assumptions: Let $P = \{P_a\}$ be a sub-measurement and $Q = \{Q_b\}$ be a projective sub-measurement.
Define $C_{a, b} = Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_b$.
conclusions: \sum_a (\sum_b C_{a, b})^\dagger (\sum_b C_{a, b}) = \sum_a (\sum_b C_{a, b}) (\sum_b C_{a, b})^\dagger \leq I.
nodes.label: lem:normalization-condition

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The first equality follows from the fact that $C_{a, b}$ is Hermitian. As for the second equality, \begin{align*} \sum_a \Big(\sum_b C_{a, b}\Big) \Big(\sum_b C_{a, b}\Big)^\dagger &= \sum_a \sum_{b, b'} C_{a, b} \cdot C_{a, b'}\tag{$C_{a, b'}$ is Hermitian}\\ &= \sum_a \sum_{b, b'} (Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_b) \cdot (Q_{b'} \cdot P_a \cdot Q_{b'})\\ &= \sum_a \sum_{b} Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_{b}\tag{because $Q$ is projective}\\ &\leq \sum_a \sum_{b} Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_{b}\tag{because $Q_b \leq I$}\\ &\leq I, \end{align*} because~$P$ and~$Q$ are sub-measurements.
nodes.statement_short: Hermiticity of C, then projectivity of Q collapses the double sum.

nodes.label: prop:ld-dnoteq

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For any $z = (z_1, \ldots, z_k) \in \mathbb F_q^k$, \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} = z] & = \frac{1}{q^k},\\ \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\boldsymbol{y} = z] & = \left\{\begin{array}{cl} \frac{1}{\binom{q}{k} k!} & \text{if $z \in \distinct{k}$,}\\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{array}\right. \end{align*} Because $\frac{1}{\binom{q}{k} k!} \geq \frac{1}{q^k}$, $\mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} = z] \geq \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\boldsymbol{y} = z]$ if and only if $z \notin \distinct{k}$. Hence, \begin{align*} d_{\mathrm{TV}}({\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}) &= \max_{S \subseteq \mathbb F_q^k}\{\mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \in S] - \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\boldsymbol{y} \in S]\}\\ &= \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \in \overline{\distinct{k}}] - \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\boldsymbol{y} \in \overline{\distinct{k}}] = \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \in \overline{\distinct{k}}]. \end{align*} We can upper-bound this probability as follows. \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \in \overline{\distinct{k}}] &= \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\exists i : {\boldsymbol{x}}_i \in \{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{i-1}\}]\\ &\leq \sum_{i=2}^k \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}}_i \in \{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{i-1}\}] \leq \sum_{i=2}^k \left(\frac{i-1}{q}\right) = \frac{k(k-1)}{2q}. \end{align*} This concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: The TV distance is the probability that independent tuples collide, bounded by a union bound.

nodes.name: Equation (125)
nodes.statement: \bra{\psi} G^{d+1}\otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx \bra{\psi} G\otimes I \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:subtract-a-G

nodes.name: Equation (126)
nodes.statement: \bra{\psi} G^{d+1}\otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx 1 - (d+1) \cdot \kappa,
nodes.label: eq:dumbo-bound-for-idiots

nodes.name: Equation (127)
nodes.statement: \bra{\psi} G^{d+2} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{\Delta} \bra{\psi} G^{d+1} \otimes I \ket{\psi},
nodes.label: eq:step-one-of-grand-plan

nodes.name: Equation (128)
nodes.statement: \Delta \geq \bra{\psi} G^{d+1} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \bra{\psi} G^{d+2} \otimes I \ket{\psi} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim \mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^{d+1}] - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim \mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^{d+2}] = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim\mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^{d+1}(1-\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}})].
nodes.label: eq:equivalent-way-of-writing-grand-plan

nodes.name: Scalar inequality for powers
nodes.statement: For any real number $0 \leq \lambda \leq 1$, \begin{equation*} \lambda (1-\lambda^d) \leq 2 \cdot \Big(\lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda)\Big)^{1/(d+1)}. \end{equation*}
assumptions: For any real number $0 \leq \lambda \leq 1$,
nodes.label: lem:looks-easy-but-took-me-a-while

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The lemma is trivial for $\lambda = 1$, and so we will assume that $\lambda \neq 1$. We note that \begin{align*} \lambda^{d+1} (1-\lambda^d)^{d+1} \leq \lambda^{d+1} (1-\lambda^d) &= \lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda) \cdot \left(\frac{1-\lambda^d}{1-\lambda}\right)\\ &= \lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda) \cdot (1 + \lambda + \cdots + \lambda^{d-1}) \leq d \cdot \lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda). \end{align*} The lemma now follows by taking the $(d+1)$-st root of both sides and noting that $d^{1/(d+1)} \leq 2$ for all integers $d \geq 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Factor 1-lambda^d as (1-lambda) times a geometric sum, then take (d+1)-st roots.

nodes.name: Incomplete part of G and its completion
nodes.statement: For each $x \in \mathbb F_q$, we write $G^x = \sum_g G^x_g$ and $G^x_{\bot} = I - G^x$ for the ``complete" and ``incomplete" parts of $G^x$, respectively. It will be convenient to sometimes regard $G^x$ as a complete measurement by throwing in the additional measurement outcome ``$\bot$". To distinguish this from $G^x$ as a sub-measurement, we will use the notation ``$\widehat{G}^x$". In other words, we let $\widehat{G} = \{\widehat{G}^x_g\}$ be the projective measurement defined as \begin{equation*} \widehat{G}^x_g = \left\{\begin{array}{rl} G^x_g & \text{if } g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d},\\ G^x_{\bot} & \text{if } g = \bot. \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} This measurement has outcomes ranging over the set $\mathcal{P}^+(m,q,d) := \polyfunc{m}{q}{d} \cup \{\bot\}$.
nodes.statement_short: G^x_bot = I - G^x, and G-hat adds bot as an extra outcome to make a projective measurement.

nodes.name: Types
nodes.statement: A type $\tau$ is an element of $\{0, 1\}^k$ for some integer~$k$. We write $|\tau| = \tau_1 + \cdots + \tau_k$ for the Hamming weight of~$\tau$. We will also associate $\tau$ with the set $\{i \mid \tau_i = 1\}$ and write $i \in \tau$ if $\tau_i = 1$.

nodes.name: The pasted measurement (second construction)
nodes.statement: Let $k \geq d+1$ be an integer. \begin{enumerate} \item (Pasting): Let $x_1, \ldots, x_k \in \mathbb F_q$. We will define an initial ``sandwiched" measurement as follows: \begin{equation*} \widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_{k}}_{g_1, \ldots, g_{k}} = \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdot \widehat{G}^{x_2}_{g_2} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_{k}}_{g_{k}} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_2}_{g_2} \cdot \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1}. \end{equation*} \item (Interpolation): Next, let $(x_1, \ldots, x_{k}) \in \distinct{k}$. For any string $w \in \{0, 1\}^k$ and polynomial $h \in \polyfunc{m+1}{q}{d}$, we define $h_w$ to be the tuple $(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathcal{P}^+(m, q, d)^k$ where $g_i = \bot$ if $w_i = 0$ and $g_i = h|_{x_i}$ otherwise. We define the interpolated measurement \begin{equation*} H^{x_1, \ldots, x_{k}}_{h} = \sum_{w : |w| \geq d+1} \widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_{k}}_{h_w}. \end{equation*} \item (Averaging): Finally, we randomize over the choice of $(x_1, \ldots, x_{k})$. In other words, we define \begin{equation*} H_{h} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{({\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{k}) \sim \distinct{k}} H^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{k}}_h. \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Measure G-hat at k points sequentially, keep outcomes with at least d+1 non-bot results, interpolate them into a global polynomial, and average over distinct points.

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency of G's complete part
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} G^{x} \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes G^{x}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: lem:g-complete-self-consistency

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Because~$G$ is a projective measurement, \Cref{prop:two-notions-of-self-consistency} implies that the strong self-consistency of~$G$ from \Cref{item:ld-pasting-self-consistency} is equivalent to \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \ket{\psi} \geq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes I\ket{\psi} - \frac{1}{2}\cdot \zeta. \end{equation} Our goal is to bound \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \Vert (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2\\ =~&2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \ket{\psi}\\ =~&2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g_1} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g, h} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{h} \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \ket{\psi}. \end{align*} But this is at most~$\zeta$ by \Cref{eq:ld-g-self-consistency}.
nodes.statement_short: Convert strong self-consistency to the agreement form and expand the squared distance.

nodes.name: Equation (129)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \ket{\psi} \geq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes I\ket{\psi} - \frac{1}{2}\cdot \zeta.
nodes.label: eq:ld-g-self-consistency

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency of G's incomplete part
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} G^{x}_{\bot} \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes G^{x}_{\bot}. \end{equation*}
nodes.label: cor:g-bot-self-consistency

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: For any~$x$, \begin{equation*} G^x_{\bot} \otimes I - I \otimes G^x_{\bot} = (I - G^x) \otimes I - I \otimes (I - G^x) = I \otimes G^x - G^x \otimes I. \end{equation*} Thus, \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \| (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot} \otimes I -I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot}) \ket{\psi} \|^2 = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \| (I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} - G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I) \ket{\psi} \|^2, \end{equation*} which is at most $\zeta$ by \Cref{lem:g-complete-self-consistency}.
nodes.statement_short: The difference for G_bot equals minus that for G^x.

nodes.name: Commutativity with G^x_g implies commutativity with G^x
nodes.statement: Let $M = \{M^x_o\}$ be a projective sub-measurement with outcomes in some set~$\mathcal{O}$. Suppose that \begin{equation} M^x_o \otimes I \approx_{\omega} I \otimes M^x_o, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} G^x_g M^y_o \otimes I \approx_{\chi} M^y_o G^x_g \otimes I \end{equation} over independent and uniformly random ${\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y} \sim \mathbb F_q$. Then \begin{equation*} G^x M^y_o \otimes I \approx_{6\sqrt{\zeta} + 6\sqrt{\omega} + 4\sqrt{\chi}} M^y_o G^x \otimes I. \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let $M = \{M^x_o\}$ be a projective sub-measurement with outcomes in some set~$\mathcal{O}$.
M^x_o \otimes I \approx_{\omega} I \otimes M^x_o,
G^x_g M^y_o \otimes I \approx_{\chi} M^y_o G^x_g \otimes I
conclusions: G^x M^y_o \otimes I \approx_{6\sqrt{\zeta} + 6\sqrt{\omega} + 4\sqrt{\chi}} M^y_o G^x \otimes I.
nodes.label: lem:commutativity-switcheroo

nodes.statement: M^x_o \otimes I \approx_{\omega} I \otimes M^x_o,

nodes.name: Equation (131)
nodes.statement: G^x_g M^y_o \otimes I \approx_{\chi} M^y_o G^x_g \otimes I

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement_short: Expand the commutator norm into four terms and show each is close to <G tensor M>, splitting G^x into its outcomes and commuting them past M one at a time.

nodes.name: Equation (132)
nodes.statement: &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_o \Vert (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\nonumber\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}})^2 M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} + \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o)^2 G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ & \qquad - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_g \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:g-commute-with-gg-error

nodes.name: Equation (133)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$G$ is projective}\\ & \approx_{\sqrt{\chi}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes I \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:split-G-and-commute

nodes.name: Equation (135)
nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:split-G-and-commute} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g\ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:move-G-for-great-justice

nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:move-G-for-great-justice} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I\ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:move-G-for-even-greater-justice

nodes.statement: \eqref{eq:move-G-for-even-greater-justice} & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I\ket{\psi} \tag{because~$G$ is projective}\\ & \approx_{\sqrt{\chi}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o,g} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I\ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:commute-the-G-yet-again

nodes.name: Equation (139)
nodes.statement: \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{2 \sqrt{\zeta} + 2 \sqrt{\omega} + 2 \sqrt{\chi}} \bra{\psi} G \otimes M \ket{\psi}.
nodes.label: eq:term-three-for-use-right-now

nodes.name: Commutativity of G's complete part
nodes.statement_short: G^x_g commutes with G^y, and G^x with G^y, up to nu_2 = 36m(gamma^{1/16}+zeta^{1/16}+(d/q)^{1/16}).
conclusions: G^x_g G^y \otimes I &\approx_{\nu_2} G^y G^x_g \otimes I\\ G^x G^y \otimes I &\approx_{\nu_2} G^y G^x \otimes I,
nodes.label: cor:commuting-with-G-complete

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement_short: Apply the switcheroo lemma twice, first with M = G^x and then with M = G^y, and bound the resulting errors.

nodes.name: Equation (140)
nodes.statement: G^x_g G^y_h \otimes I \approx_{\nu_{\mathrm{commute}}} G^y_h G^x_g \otimes I.
nodes.label: eq:com-main-copy

nodes.name: Equation (141)
nodes.statement: G^x_g G^y \otimes I \approx_{\theta_1} G^y G^x_g \otimes I
nodes.label: eq:applied-the-lemma-to-com-main-copy

nodes.name: Commutativity of G's incomplete part
conclusions: G^x_g G^y_{\bot} \otimes I &\approx_{\nu_2} G^y_{\bot} G^x_g \otimes I\\ G^x_{\bot} G^y_{\bot} \otimes I &\approx_{\nu_2} G^y_{\bot} G^x_{\bot} \otimes I,
nodes.label: cor:commuting-with-G-incomplete

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: First, we note that \begin{equation*} G^x_g G^y_{\bot} - G^y_{\bot} G^x_g = G^x_g \cdot (I - G^y) - (I- G^y)\cdot G^x_g = G^y G^x_g - G^x_g G^y. \end{equation*} Hence, by \Cref{cor:commuting-with-G-complete}, \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}}\sum_g \Vert (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}}\sum_g \Vert (G^{\boldsymbol{y}} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g - G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 \leq \nu_2. \end{equation*} Next, we note that \begin{align*} G^x_{\bot} G^y_{\bot} - G^y_{\bot} G^x_{\bot} &= (I - G^x) \cdot (I - G^y) - (I - G^y) \cdot (I - G^x)\\ & = (I - G^x - G^y + G^x G^y) - (I - G^y - G^x + G^y G^x)\\ &= G^x G^y - G^y G^x. \end{align*} As a result, by \Cref{cor:commuting-with-G-complete}, \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \Vert (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot}) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \Vert (G^{\boldsymbol{y}} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} - G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 \leq \nu_2.\qedhere \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Commutators with G_bot = I - G equal minus commutators with G.

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency and commutation of G-hat
nodes.statement: $\widehat{G}$ obeys the following strong self-consistency and commutation properties. \begin{align} \widehat{G}^{x}_{g} \otimes I &\approx_{2\zeta} I \otimes \widehat{G}^{x}_{g}, \\ \widehat{G}^{x}_{g}\widehat{G}^{y}_{h} \otimes I &\approx_{\nu_3} \widehat{G}^{y}_{h} \widehat{G}^{x}_{g} \otimes I, \end{align} where \[ \nu_{3} = 138 m \cdot \left(\zeta^{1/16} + \gamma^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right). \]
nodes.label: cor:G-hat-facts

nodes.name: Equation (142)
nodes.statement: \widehat{G}^{x}_{g} \otimes I &\approx_{2\zeta} I \otimes \widehat{G}^{x}_{g},
nodes.label: eq:gselfconall

nodes.statement: \widehat{G}^{x}_{g}\widehat{G}^{y}_{h} \otimes I &\approx_{\nu_3} \widehat{G}^{y}_{h} \widehat{G}^{x}_{g} \otimes I,
nodes.label: eq:gcomall

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
We begin with \Cref{eq:gselfconall}. To prove this, we wish to bound  egin{align*} &\mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \Vert(\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2\ =~&\mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 + \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot} \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot}) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2\ \leq~& \zeta + \zeta = 2\zeta, \end{align*} by \Cref{item:ld-pasting-self-consistency} and \Cref{cor:g-bot-self-consistency}. Next, we show \Cref{eq:gcomall}. To prove this, we wish to bound  egin{align*} &\mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h} \Vert(\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g \widehat{G}^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h - \widehat{G}^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\ =~&\mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h - G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 + \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{ ot} - G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{ ot} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\ & \quad + \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g\in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{ ot} - G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{ ot} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 + \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{h\in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h - G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\ \leq~& 
u_{\mathrm{commute}} + 3
u_2, \end{align*} by \Cref{eq:quote-com-main} and \Cref{cor:commuting-with-G-incomplete}. We can therefore bound this by  egin{align*} 
u_{\mathrm{commute}} + 3

nodes.statement_short: Split the sums over outcomes into polynomial and bot parts and apply the previous results to each.

nodes.name: Commuting past multiple G-hats
nodes.statement: For all $k \geq 2$, \[ \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \widehat{G}^{x_2}_{g_2} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_k}_{g_k} \otimes I \approx_{\nu_4} \widehat{G}^{x_2}_{g_2} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_k}_{g_k} \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \otimes I, \] where \begin{equation*} \nu_4 = 426 k^2 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} +\zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right). \end{equation*}
assumptions: For all $k \geq 2$,
nodes.label: lem:commute-g-half-sandwich

nodes.name: Proof

nodes.name: Consistency of H-hat with B
assumptions: For any $1 \leq i \leq k$,
nodes.label: lem:ld-sandwich-line-one-point

nodes.name: Outcome sets of a given type
nodes.statement: Let $\tau \in \{0, 1\}^k$ be a type. We define the following two subsets of $\mathcal{P}^+(m,q,d)^k$. \begin{itemize} \item We define $\mathsf{Outcomes}_{\tau}$ to be the set of tuples $(g_1, \ldots, g_k)$ such that $g_i \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ for each $i \in \tau$ and $g_i = \bot$ for each $i \notin \tau$. This is the set of possible outcomes of the $\widehat{H}$ measurement of type~$\tau$. \item Let $x_1, \ldots, x_k \in \mathbb F_q$. We define $\mathsf{Global}_{\tau}(x)$ to be the subset of $\mathsf{Outcomes}_{\tau}$ containing only those tuples which are consistent with a global polynomial. In other words, $(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Global}_{\tau}(x)$ if there exists an $h \in \polyfunc{m+1}{q}{d}$ such that $g_i = h|_{x_i}$ for each $i \in \tau$. Next, we define \begin{equation*} \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{\tau}(x)} = \mathsf{Outcomes}_{\tau} \setminus \mathsf{Global}_{\tau}(x). \end{equation*} This contains those tuples of type~$\tau$ with no consistent global polynomial. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Completeness of H over all outcomes
nodes.statement: Let ${\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_k \sim \mathbb F_q$ be sampled uniformly at random. Then \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} H \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{\nu_7} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{\tau:|\tau| \geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{\tau}} \bra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi}, \end{equation*} where \begin{equation*} \nu_7 = 46 k^2m \cdot \left(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} +\gamma^{1/32} + \zeta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\right). \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let ${\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_k \sim \mathbb F_q$ be sampled uniformly at random.
nodes.label: lem:over-all-outcomes

nodes.name: Proof

Let $( oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k) \sim \mathsf{Distinct}_k$. By definition,  egin{align}  ra{\psi} H \otimes I \ket{\psi} &= \sum_h  ra{\psi} H_h \otimes I \ket{\psi}
onumber\ &= \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_h  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_h \otimes I \ket{\psi}
onumber\ &= \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_h \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{h_{	au}} \otimes I \ket{\psi}
onumber\ &= \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_h \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) = h_	au}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi}
onumber\ &= \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{align} The sum in \Cref{eq:sum-restricted-to-global-polynomial} is over $g_1, \ldots, g_k$ which are consistent with a global polynomial. We will now show that the value of this sum remains largely unchanged if we drop this condition. In particular, we claim that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:sum-restricted-to-global-polynomial} \approx_{ rac{k^2}{q} + k \cdot
u_5 +  rac{md}{q}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{	au}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we note that $\eqref{eq:remove-the-restriction} \geq \eqref{eq:sum-restricted-to-global-polynomial}$. Hence, it suffices to upper bound their difference.  egin{align} \eqref{eq:remove-the-restriction} - \eqref{eq:sum-restricted-to-global-polynomial} &= \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi}
onumber\ &= \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi}, \end{align} because~$B$ is a measurement. Next, we claim that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:B-appears-out-of-thin-air} \approx_{ rac{k^2}{q} + k \cdot
u_5} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[ orall i\in 	au, f( oldsymbol{y}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})]. \end{equation} To show this, we note that $\eqref{eq:B-appears-out-of-thin-air} \geq \eqref{eq:add-in-indicator-for-f-and-g}$. Thus, it suffices to upper bound their difference $\eqref{eq:B-appears-out-of-thin-air} - \eqref{eq:add-in-indicator-for-f-and-g}$. This is given by  egin{equation} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au: |	au|\geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\exists i \in 	au, f( oldsymbol{y}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]. \end{equation} Recall that ${ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k \sim \mathbb F_q$ are sampled independently and uniformly at random. Then \Cref{prop:ld-dnoteq} implies that \Cref{eq:about-to-swap-x-for-y} is $(k^2/q)$-close to  egin{align*} &\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{	au: |	au|\geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}({ oldsymbol{x}})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\exists i \in 	au, f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]\ \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{	au}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\exists i \in 	au, f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]\ \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{	au} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{	au}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\exists i \in 	au, f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]\ \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{	au} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{	au}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot \Big(\sum_{i\in 	au}  oldsymbol{1}[f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]\Big)\ =~& \sum_i \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{g_1, \ldots, g_k : g_i 
eq  ot} \sum_{f: f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i)

u_5. \end{align*} Returning to \Cref{eq:add-in-indicator-for-f-and-g}, we introduce the notation $\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g,  oldsymbol{y},  oldsymbol{u})$ to indicate whether there is a consistent degree-$d$ polynomial interpolating the $g_i$'s along the line in direction~$u$. In other words,  egin{equation*} \mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g,  oldsymbol{y},  oldsymbol{u}) = \left\{ egin{array}{rl} 1 & 	ext{if $\exists f$ such that $f( oldsymbol{y}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})$ for all $i \in 	au$,}\ 0 & 	ext{otherwise.} \end{array}ight. \end{equation*} Clearly, for any $f$,  egin{equation*}  oldsymbol{1}[ orall i\in 	au, f( oldsymbol{y}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})] \leq  oldsymbol{1}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g,  oldsymbol{y},  oldsymbol{u})] \end{equation*} because the left-hand side indicates whether~$f$ is the consistent degree-$d$ polynomial interpolating along direction~$u$. As a result,  egin{align} \eqref{eq:add-in-indicator-for-f-and-g} \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au|\geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, oldsymbol{y}, oldsymbol{u})]
onumber\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au|\geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes \Big(\sum_f B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f\Big) \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, oldsymbol{y}, oldsymbol{u})]
onumber\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au|\geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, oldsymbol{y}, oldsymbol{u})]
onumber\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au|\geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \cdot \mathop{ f Pr/}_{ oldsymbol{u}}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, oldsymbol{y}, oldsymbol{u})]. \end{align} Let us now fix $(y_1, \ldots, y_k) \in \mathsf{Distinct}_k$, a type $	au$ such that $|	au| \geq d+1$, and $(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}(y)}$. Suppose without loss of generality that $	au_1 = \cdots = 	au_{d+1} = 1$, so that $g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1} \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$. Then there is a unique polynomial $h^* \in \polyfunc{m+1}{q}{d}$ which interpolates $g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1}$. In other words, for all $1 \leq i \leq d+1$,  egin{equation*} h^*(u, y_i) = g_i(u). \end{equation*} In addition, for any $u$, $(h^*)|_u$ is the unique degree-$d$ polynomial which interpolates $g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1}$ along the line in direction~$u$. Thus, if there is a consistent degree-$d$ polynomial interpolating all the $g_i$'s along the line in direction~$u$, then it is $(h^*)|_u$. In math,  egin{equation*} \mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, y,u) = 1 \qquad 	ext{if and only if} \qquad  orall i \in 	au, g_i(u) = h^*(u, y_i). \end{equation*} On the other hand, because $(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}(y)}$, there exists an $i^* \in 	au$ such that $g_{i^*} 
eq (h^*)|_{y_{i^*}}$. Hence,  egin{equation*} \mathop{ f Pr/}_{ oldsymbol{u}}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, y, oldsymbol{u})] \leq \mathop{ f Pr/}_{ oldsymbol{u}}[g_{i^*}( oldsymbol{u}) = h^*( oldsymbol{u}, y_{i^*})] = \mathop{ f Pr/}_{ oldsymbol{u}}[g_{i^*}( oldsymbol{u}) = (h^*)|_{y_{i^*}}( oldsymbol{u})] \leq  rac{md}{q}, \end{equation*} by Schwartz-Zippel. As a result,  egin{align*} \eqref{eq:consistent-indicator} & \leq \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au|\geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \cdot  rac{md}{q}\ &\leq \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{g_1, \ldots, g_k}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \cdot  rac{md}{q}\ & =  rac{md}{q}. \end{align*} This establishes \Cref{eq:remove-the-restriction}. Finally, \Cref{prop:ld-dnoteq} implies that \Cref{eq:remove-the-restriction} is $(k^2/q)$-close to  egin{equation*} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{	au}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation*} In total, this gives an error of  egin{align*} 2  rac{k^2}{q} +  rac{md}{q}+ k \cdot 
u_5 & = 2  rac{k^2}{q} +  rac{md}{q} + k \cdot 43 km \cdot \left(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + \gamma^{1/32} + \zeta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}ight)\ & \leq 3  rac{k^2 md}{q} + 43 k^2m \cdot \left(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} +\gamma^{1/32} +\zeta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}ight)\ & \leq 3 k^2 m (d/q)^{1/32} + 43 k^2m \cdot \left(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} +\gamma^{1/32} + \zeta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}ight)\ & \leq 46 k^2m \cdot \left(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + \gamma^{1/32} + \zeta^{1/32} +(d/q)^{1/32}ight). \end{align*} This completes the proof of the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Drop the global-consistency restriction: inconsistent tuples either disagree with B (H-hat consistency lemma) or are caught by Schwartz-Zippel; switch between distinct and independent points twice.

nodes.name: From H-hat to powers of G
nodes.statement: Let ${\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_k \sim \mathbb F_q$ be sampled uniformly at random. Then \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{\tau:|\tau| \geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_{k}) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{\tau}} \bra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \dots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{\nu_8} \sum_{i = d+1}^k \binom{k}{i} \bra{\psi} G^i (I-G)^{k-i} \otimes I \ket{\psi}, \end{equation*} where \begin{equation*} \nu_8 = 46 k m \cdot \left( \gamma^{1/32} + \zeta^{1/32} +(d/q)^{1/32}\right). \end{equation*}
assumptions: Let ${\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_k \sim \mathbb F_q$ be sampled uniformly at random.
nodes.label: lem:from-H-to-G

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement_short: Peel off one G-hat factor at a time, moving it to the other tensor factor (self-consistency) and commuting it past the rest (multi-commutation), tracking types with the operators S. The key step is the recurrence for S.

nodes.name: m-variate polynomial over a finite field
nodes.statement: An $m$-variate polynomial over the finite field~$\mathbb F_q$ is a function $g:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ of the form \begin{equation*} g(x_1, \ldots, x_m) = \sum_{i_1, \ldots, i_m} c_{i_1, \ldots, i_m} \cdot x_1^{i_1} \cdots x_{m}^{i_m}, \end{equation*} where each coefficient~$c_{i_1, \ldots, i_m}$ is an element of~$\mathbb F_q$.

nodes.name: Total degree and individual degree
nodes.statement: We say that~$g$ has \emph{total degree $d$} (or \emph{degree $d$}, for short) if $i_1 + \cdots + i_m \leq d$ for each nonzero coefficient $c_{i_1, \ldots, i_m}$, and \emph{individual degree $d$} if $i_1, \ldots, i_m \leq d$ for each nonzero coefficient $c_{i_1, \ldots, i_m}$.
nodes.statement_short: A polynomial has total degree d if every monomial has degree sum at most d, individual degree d if each exponent is at most d.

nodes.name: Low (individual) degree testing
nodes.statement: \emph{Low (individual) degree testing} refers to the task of verifying that an unknown function $g:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ is representable as a polynomial of (individual) degree~$d$ by querying~$g$ on a small number of points $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$.

nodes.name: Surface-versus-point low-degree test
nodes.statement: In this setting, the surface-versus-point low degree test, parameterized by an integer $k \geq 1$, is performed by the verifier as follows. \begin{enumerate} \item Select~$\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m$ uniformly at random. Give it to Prover~$\mathrm{A}$. They respond with a value~$\boldsymbol{a} \in \mathbb F_q$. \item Select a uniformly random $k$-dimensional affine surface~$\boldsymbol{s}$ in~$\mathbb F_q^m$ containing~$\boldsymbol{u}$. Give it to Prover~$\mathrm{B}$. They respond with a degree-$d$ $k$-variate polynomial $\boldsymbol{f}:\boldsymbol{s}\rightarrow \mathbb F_q$. \item Accept if $\boldsymbol{f}(\boldsymbol{u}) = \boldsymbol{a}$.
nodes.statement_short: Referee sends a random point to Prover A and a random k-dimensional surface through it to Prover B, accepting if B's polynomial agrees with A's value.

nodes.name: Local characterization of low-degree polynomials
nodes.statement: This test is motivated by the following ``local characterization" of low-degree polynomials: a polynomial $g:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ is degree-$d$ if and only if $g|_s$ is degree-$d$ for all $k$-dimensional surfaces~$s$.
conclusions: a polynomial $g:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ is degree-$d$ if and only if $g|_s$ is degree-$d$ for all $k$-dimensional surfaces~$s$
equivalent_conditions: a polynomial $g:\mathbb F_q^m \rightarrow \mathbb F_q$ is degree-$d$

nodes.name: Local characterization of low individual degree polynomials
nodes.statement: A similar ``local characterization" of low individual degree polynomials states that a polynomial~$g$ has individual degree $d$ if and only if $g|_{\ell}$ is a univariate degree-$d$ polynomial for all axis-parallel lines~$\ell$.
conclusions: a polynomial~$g$ has individual degree $d$ if and only if $g|_{\ell}$ is a univariate degree-$d$ polynomial for all axis-parallel lines~$\ell$
equivalent_conditions: $g|_{\ell}$ is a univariate degree-$d$ polynomial for all axis-parallel lines~$\ell$

nodes.name: Axis-parallel line
nodes.statement: An axis-parallel line is a line of the form $\ell = \{u + a \cdot e_i \mid i \in \mathbb F_q\}$, for $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$ and $i \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$.

nodes.name: Low individual degree test (two-prover outline)
nodes.statement: Motivated by this, the low individual degree test follows the same outline as the surface-versus-point low degree test except with the second step substituted with the following. \begin{enumerate} \setcounter{enumi}{1} \item Select a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ in~$\mathbb F_q^m$ containing~$\boldsymbol{u}$. Give it to Prover~$\mathrm{B}$. They respond with a degree-$d$ univariate polynomial $\boldsymbol{f}:\boldsymbol{\ell}\rightarrow \mathbb F_q$.
nodes.statement_short: Same as the surface-versus-point test but Prover B receives a random axis-parallel line through the point.

nodes.name: Multilinearity test
nodes.statement: When $d = 1$, the low individual degree test is called the \emph{multilinearity test} because a polynomial with individual degree $d = 1$ is a multilinear polynomial.

nodes.name: Tightness of the m and epsilon dependence
nodes.statement: \Cref{ex:bad-individual-degree-example} shows that the dependence on~$m$ and~$\epsilon$ in \Cref{thm:main-informal} is tight up to polynomial factors.
conclusions: the dependence on~$m$ and~$\epsilon$ in \Cref{thm:main-informal} is tight up to polynomial factors

nodes.name: Scaled-down consequences of quantum low-degree tests
nodes.statement: It remains open whether the complexity-theoretic consequences of~\cite{Vid16,NV18b,NV18a} to the ``scaled down'' setting still hold.
nodes.section: 1.1 Quantum soundness of the low degree tests

nodes.name: Quantum soundness of the classical low-degree test
nodes.statement: Is the classical low-degree test quantum sound? Can the Consolidation step be fixed?

nodes.name: Removing the diagonal lines test
nodes.statement: Even if the classical low-degree test is shown quantum sound, there are still interesting questions to be answered about the low individual degree test. For example, can the diagonal lines test be removed? (See \Cref{sec:the-test} for a description of this subtest.) Doing so would likely simplify the proof of $\mathsf{MIP}^* = \mathsf{RE}$~\cite{JNV+20}, as one could replace the complicated ``conditional linear functions'' used in the proof with a simpler subclass known as ``coordinate deletion functions''. However, as discussed at the end of \Cref{sec:technical-overview}, we know of an example that requires the diagonal lines test for the low individual degree test with parameters $m = 2$, $d = 2$, and $q = 4$. Can we find similar examples for larger~$q$?
also_stated_at: Whether this counterexample can be extended to larger~$q$ remains an open question.

nodes.name: Quantum soundness of affine-invariant and tensor-product tests
nodes.statement: Classically, the low degree test generalized in various directions, including tests for affine invariant properties~\cite{KS08,Sud11} and tests for tensor product codes (see, for example, \cite{CMS17}). Does quantum soundness hold for these tests as well?

nodes.name: Conceptual reason for quantum soundness of classical testers
nodes.statement: This work continues the trend of showing that well-studied classical property testers are also quantum sound. Prior to this, the work of~\cite{IV12} (see also \cite[Chapter 2]{Vid11}) showed that the linearity tester of Blum, Luby, and Rubinfield~\cite{BLR93} is also quantum sound. The proofs of these results have so far been case-by-case adaptations of the classical proofs to the quantum setting; in the case of this paper, the proof is highly nontrivial and involves many ad hoc calculations which fortunately go in our favor. Is there a more conceptual reason why quantum soundness holds for these testers? Perhaps a reduction from the quantum case to the classical case?

nodes.name: Commutation from axis-parallel lines for bivariate multilinearity test
nodes.statement: Despite this example, we know that commutation between all pairs of points \emph{can} be deduced from the axis-parallel lines test alone, rending the diagonal lines test unnecessary, at least in the case of the bivariate ($m = 2$) multilinearity test (the low individual degree test when $d = 1$).

nodes.name: Noncommuting perfect strategy for m=2, d=2, q=4
