u + e^{- k/(80000m^2)}\Big) + 
uight) + 2
u + e^{- k/(80000m^2)}
onumber\ &\leq \left(1 +  rac{1}{100m}ight) \cdot (m^2+3) \cdot\Big(
u + e^{- k/(80000m^2)}\Big). \end{align} Now, because $m \geq 2$,  egin{equation*}  rac{1}{100m} \cdot (m^2+3) \leq  rac{1}{100m}\cdot (m^2+4m-5) =  rac{1}{100m}\cdot (m-1) (m+5) \leq m-1 \leq 2(m-1). \end{equation*} Hence,  egin{equation*} \left(1 +  rac{1}{100m}ight) \cdot (m^2+3) = m^2 + 3 +  rac{1}{100m} \cdot (m^2+3) \leq m^2 + 3 + 2(m-1) = m^2 + 2m + 1 = (m+1)^2. \end{equation*} As a result,  egin{equation*} \eqref{eq:gonna-bound-m-function} \leq (m+1)^2\cdot\Big(
u + e^{- k/(80000m^2)}\Big) \leq (m+1)^2\cdot\Big(
u + e^{- k/(80000(m+1)^2)}\Big). \end{equation*} This is the bound guaranteed by the theorem and so it completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Inductive step from m to m+1

nodes.name: Fix the strategy and its x-restrictions
nodes.statement: Now we perform the induction step. Assuming that \Cref{thm:main-induction} holds for~$m \geq 1$, we will show that it holds for~$m+1$ as well. Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be an $(\epsilon, \delta, \gamma)$-good symmetric strategy for the $(m+1,q,d)$ low individual degree test. Let $k \geq (m+1)d$ be an integer. For each $x \in \mathbb F_q$, let $(\psi, A^x, B^x, L^x)$ be the corresponding $x$-restricted strategy. In addition, write $\epsilon_x$ for the probability that it fails the axis-parallel lines test, $\delta_x$ for the probability it fails the self-consistency test, and $\gamma_x$ for the probability it fails the diagonal lines test.
nodes.statement_short: Fix the strategy and its x-restrictions

nodes.name: Apply the inductive hypothesis to each restriction
nodes.statement: For each $x \in \mathbb F_q$, we apply the inductive hypothesis to the $x$-restricted strategy with the same integer~$k$. This is possible because $k \geq (m+1)d \geq md$. Let \begin{equation*} \nu_x = 1000k^2 m^2 \cdot\Big(\epsilon_x^{1/1024} + \delta_x^{1/1024} + \gamma_x^{1/1024} + (d/q)^{1/1024}\Big), \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} \sigma_x = m^2 \cdot\Big(\nu_x + e^{- k/(80000m^2)}\Big) \end{equation*} Then the inductive hypothesis states that there exists a measurement $G^x \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ such that \begin{equation*} (A^x)^u_a\otimes I \simeq_{\sigma_x} I \otimes G^x_{[g(u)=a]}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the inductive hypothesis to each restriction

nodes.name: Self-improve each G^x
nodes.statement: Next, we apply self-improvement to each~$G^x$. Let \begin{equation*} \zeta_x = 3000m \cdot \Big(\epsilon_x^{1/32} + \delta_x^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big). \end{equation*} Then \Cref{thm:self-improvement-in-induction-section} produces a projective sub-measurement $\widehat{G}^x \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$ such that for each $x \in \mathbb F_q$, the following statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item(Completeness): If $\widehat{G}^x = \sum_g \widehat{G}^x_g$, then \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} \widehat{G}^x \otimes I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\sigma_x) - \zeta_x. \end{equation*} \item(Consistency with~$A^x$): On average over $\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m$, \begin{equation*} (A^x)^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\zeta_x} I \otimes \widehat{G}^x_{[g(u) = a]}. \end{equation*} \item(Strong self-consistency): \begin{equation*} \widehat{G}^x_g \otimes I \approx_{\zeta_x} I \otimes \widehat{G}^x_g. \end{equation*} \item(Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix~$Z^x$ such that \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} Z^x \otimes (I - \widehat{G}^x) \ket{\psi} \leq \zeta_x \end{equation*} and for each $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, \begin{equation*} Z^x \geq \Big( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} (A^x)^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\Big). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Completeness of the improved G^x
nodes.statement: Next, we apply self-improvement to each~$G^x$. Let \begin{equation*} \zeta_x = 3000m \cdot \Big(\epsilon_x^{1/32} + \delta_x^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big). \end{equation*} Then \Cref{thm:self-improvement-in-induction-section} produces a projective sub-measurement $\widehat{G}^x \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$ such that for each $x \in \mathbb F_q$, the following statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item(Completeness): If $\widehat{G}^x = \sum_g \widehat{G}^x_g$, then \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} \widehat{G}^x \otimes I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\sigma_x) - \zeta_x. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Consistency with A^x
nodes.statement: (Consistency with~$A^x$): On average over $\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m$, \begin{equation*} (A^x)^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\zeta_x} I \otimes \widehat{G}^x_{[g(u) = a]}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency
nodes.statement: (Strong self-consistency): \begin{equation*} \widehat{G}^x_g \otimes I \approx_{\zeta_x} I \otimes \widehat{G}^x_g. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Boundedness
nodes.statement: (Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix~$Z^x$ such that \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} Z^x \otimes (I - \widehat{G}^x) \ket{\psi} \leq \zeta_x \end{equation*} and for each $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, \begin{equation*} Z^x \geq \Big( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} (A^x)^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\Big). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Average the error parameters by concavity
nodes.statement_short: Average the error parameters by concavity

nodes.name: Averaged hypotheses for pasting
nodes.statement: Having defined these, the following statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item(Completeness): If $\widehat{G} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_g \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g$, then \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} \widehat{G} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\sigma) - \zeta. \end{equation*} \item(Consistency with~$A$): On average over $(\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}) \sim \mathbb F_q^{m+1}$, \begin{equation*} A^{u,x}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\zeta} I \otimes \widehat{G}^x_{[g(u) = a]}. \end{equation*} \item(Strong self-consistency): On average over ${\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q$, \begin{equation*} \widehat{G}^x_g \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes \widehat{G}^x_g. \end{equation*} \item(Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix~$Z^x$ for each $x \in \mathbb F_q$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes (I - \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \ket{\psi} \leq \zeta \end{equation*} and for each $x \in\mathbb F_q$ and $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, \begin{equation*} Z^x \geq \Big( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u},x}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\Big). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Averaged completeness
nodes.statement: Having defined these, the following statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item(Completeness): If $\widehat{G} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_g \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g$, then \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} \widehat{G} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \geq (1-\sigma) - \zeta. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Averaged consistency with A
nodes.statement: (Consistency with~$A$): On average over $(\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}) \sim \mathbb F_q^{m+1}$, \begin{equation*} A^{u,x}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\zeta} I \otimes \widehat{G}^x_{[g(u) = a]}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Averaged strong self-consistency
nodes.statement: (Strong self-consistency): On average over ${\boldsymbol{x}} \sim \mathbb F_q$, \begin{equation*} \widehat{G}^x_g \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes \widehat{G}^x_g. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Averaged boundedness
nodes.statement: (Boundedness): There exists a positive-semidefinite matrix~$Z^x$ for each $x \in \mathbb F_q$ such that \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes (I - \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \ket{\psi} \leq \zeta \end{equation*} and for each $x \in\mathbb F_q$ and $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, \begin{equation*} Z^x \geq \Big( \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u},x}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\Big). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Bound the pasting error parameter by nu
nodes.statement: We are now ready to apply \Cref{thm:ld-pasting-in-induction-section}. To do so, we note that because $(3000)^{1/32} \leq 2$ and $32 \cdot 32 = 1024$, \begin{align*} \zeta^{1/32} &= \Big(3000 (m+1) \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big)\Big)^{1/32}\\ &\leq 2 (m+1) \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/1024} + \delta^{1/1024} + (d/q)^{1/1024}\Big). \end{align*} Hence, \begin{align*} &100 k^2m \cdot \left(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + \gamma^{1/32} + \zeta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\right)\\ \leq~&100 k^2m \cdot \left(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + \gamma^{1/32} + 2 (m+1) \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/1024} + \delta^{1/1024} + (d/q)^{1/1024}\Big)+ (d/q)^{1/32}\right)\\ \leq~& 200 k^2 m(m+1) \cdot\left(\epsilon^{1/1024} + \delta^{1/1024} + \gamma^{1/1024} + \epsilon^{1/1024} + \delta^{1/1024} + (d/q)^{1/1024}+ (d/q)^{1/1024}\right)\\ \leq~& 1000 k^2 (m+1)^2 \cdot\left(\epsilon^{1/1024} + \delta^{1/1024} + \gamma^{1/1024} + (d/q)^{1/1024}\right)\\ =~& \nu. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the pasting error parameter by nu

nodes.name: Apply pasting
nodes.statement: Then \Cref{thm:ld-pasting-in-induction-section} implies the existence of a pasted measurement $H \in \polysub{m+1}{q}{d}$ which satisfies the following property. On average over $\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^{m+1}$, \begin{equation*} A^{u}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\sigma^*} I \otimes H_{[h(u)=a]}, \end{equation*} where \begin{equation*} \sigma^* = (\sigma + \zeta) \cdot \left(1 + \frac{1}{100m}\right) + 2\nu + e^{- k/(80000m^2)}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Bound sigma*
sigma* <= (m+1)^2(nu + e^{-k/...})
nodes.statement: Now, because $m \geq 2$, \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{100m} \cdot (m^2+3) \leq \frac{1}{100m}\cdot (m^2+4m-5) = \frac{1}{100m}\cdot (m-1) (m+5) \leq m-1 \leq 2(m-1). \end{equation*} Hence, \begin{equation*} \left(1 + \frac{1}{100m}\right) \cdot (m^2+3) = m^2 + 3 + \frac{1}{100m} \cdot (m^2+3) \leq m^2 + 3 + 2(m-1) = m^2 + 2m + 1 = (m+1)^2. \end{equation*} As a result, \begin{equation*} \eqref{eq:gonna-bound-m-function} \leq (m+1)^2\cdot\Big(\nu + e^{- k/(80000m^2)}\Big) \leq (m+1)^2\cdot\Big(\nu + e^{- k/(80000(m+1)^2)}\Big). \end{equation*} This is the bound guaranteed by the theorem and so it completes the proof.

nodes.name: Rewrite I/M via uniform endpoints
nodes.statement: If we draw $(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C$, then both $\boldsymbol{u}$ and~$\boldsymbol{v}$ are distributed as uniformly random elements of~$\mathbb F_q^m$. As a result, \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{M} \cdot I = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \in \mathbb F_q^m} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}}\bra{\boldsymbol{u}} = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}}\bra{\boldsymbol{u}} + \ket{\boldsymbol{v}}\bra{\boldsymbol{v}}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Symmetrize K
nodes.statement: In addition, $(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v})$ is distributed identically to $(\boldsymbol{v}, \boldsymbol{u})$. As a result, \begin{equation*} K = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}}\bra{\boldsymbol{v}} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}}\bra{\boldsymbol{v}} + \ket{\boldsymbol{v}}\bra{\boldsymbol{u}}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Combine to get the formula
nodes.statement: Combining these two, \begin{equation*} L = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \left[\ket{\boldsymbol{u}}\bra{\boldsymbol{u}} + \ket{\boldsymbol{v}}\bra{\boldsymbol{v}} - \ket{\boldsymbol{u}}\bra{\boldsymbol{v}} - \ket{\boldsymbol{v}}\bra{\boldsymbol{u}}\right] = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} (\ket{\boldsymbol{u}} - \ket{\boldsymbol{v}}) \cdot (\bra{\boldsymbol{u}} - \bra{\boldsymbol{v}}).\qedhere \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Orthonormality
nodes.statement: First, we prove \Cref{item:orthonormal}. Given $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb F_q^m$, \begin{equation*} \braket{\varphi_\alpha \mid \varphi_\beta} = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[u \cdot (\beta-\alpha)]} = \left\{\begin{array}{rl} 1 & \text{if } \alpha = \beta,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array} \right.\tag{by~\Cref{prop:fourier-fact-vector}} \end{equation*} As a result, the $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ vectors form an orthonormal basis of~$\mathbb C^V$.

nodes.name: Inner products via the character sum
nodes.statement: Given $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb F_q^m$, \begin{equation*} \braket{\varphi_\alpha \mid \varphi_\beta} = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[u \cdot (\beta-\alpha)]} = \left\{\begin{array}{rl} 1 & \text{if } \alpha = \beta,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array} \right.\tag{by~\Cref{prop:fourier-fact-vector}} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Inner products via the character sum

nodes.name: Conclude orthonormal basis
nodes.statement: As a result, the $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ vectors form an orthonormal basis of~$\mathbb C^V$.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues
nodes.statement: Next, we prove \Cref{item:eigenvector}. Given $\alpha \in \mathbb F_q^m$, \begin{equation} K \cdot \ket{\varphi_\alpha} = \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}}\bra{\boldsymbol{v}}\right) \cdot \bigg(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[u \cdot \alpha]}\cdot \ket{u}\bigg)\\ = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[\boldsymbol{v} \cdot \alpha]} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}}. \end{equation} By definition of a random edge, we can replace~$\boldsymbol{v}$ with $\boldsymbol{u} + {\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot e_{\boldsymbol{i}}$, where $\boldsymbol{i}$ is a uniformly random index in $\{1, \ldots, m\}$ and ${\boldsymbol{x}}$ is a uniformly random element of $\mathbb F_q$. As a result, \begin{equation*} \eqref{eq:eigenvector-calculation} = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{i}, {\boldsymbol{x}}} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[(\boldsymbol{u} + {\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot e_{\boldsymbol{i}}) \cdot \alpha]} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}} = \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i}, {\boldsymbol{x}}}\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[({\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot e_{\boldsymbol{i}}) \cdot \alpha]}\right) \cdot \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[\boldsymbol{u} \cdot \alpha]} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}} = \frac{1}{M}\left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i}, {\boldsymbol{x}}}\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot \alpha_{\boldsymbol{i}}]}\right) \cdot \ket{\varphi_\alpha}. \end{equation*} Hence, $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ is an eigenvector of~$K$ with eigenvalue \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{M} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i}} \left[\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot \alpha_{\boldsymbol{i}}]}\right] = \frac{1}{M} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i}} \left[\boldsymbol{1}[\alpha_{\boldsymbol{i}} = 0]\right] = \frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m - |\alpha|}{m}. \tag{by~\Cref{prop:fourier-fact-scalar}} \end{equation*} This concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Apply K to phi_alpha
nodes.statement: Given $\alpha \in \mathbb F_q^m$, \begin{equation} K \cdot \ket{\varphi_\alpha} = \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}}\bra{\boldsymbol{v}}\right) \cdot \bigg(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[u \cdot \alpha]}\cdot \ket{u}\bigg)\\ = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[\boldsymbol{v} \cdot \alpha]} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Substitute v = u + x e_i
nodes.statement: By definition of a random edge, we can replace~$\boldsymbol{v}$ with $\boldsymbol{u} + {\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot e_{\boldsymbol{i}}$, where $\boldsymbol{i}$ is a uniformly random index in $\{1, \ldots, m\}$ and ${\boldsymbol{x}}$ is a uniformly random element of $\mathbb F_q$. As a result, \begin{equation*} \eqref{eq:eigenvector-calculation} = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{i}, {\boldsymbol{x}}} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[(\boldsymbol{u} + {\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot e_{\boldsymbol{i}}) \cdot \alpha]} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}} = \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i}, {\boldsymbol{x}}}\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[({\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot e_{\boldsymbol{i}}) \cdot \alpha]}\right) \cdot \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \omega^{\mathrm{tr}[\boldsymbol{u} \cdot \alpha]} \ket{\boldsymbol{u}} = \frac{1}{M}\left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i}, {\boldsymbol{x}}}\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot \alpha_{\boldsymbol{i}}]}\right) \cdot \ket{\varphi_\alpha}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Compute the eigenvalue via the scalar character sum
nodes.statement: Hence, $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ is an eigenvector of~$K$ with eigenvalue \begin{equation*} \frac{1}{M} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i}} \left[\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\omega^{\mathrm{tr}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \cdot \alpha_{\boldsymbol{i}}]}\right] = \frac{1}{M} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i}} \left[\boldsymbol{1}[\alpha_{\boldsymbol{i}} = 0]\right] = \frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m - |\alpha|}{m}. \tag{by~\Cref{prop:fourier-fact-scalar}} \end{equation*} This concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the eigenvalue via the scalar character sum

nodes.name: Relate eigenvalues of K and L
nodes.statement: Let $\mu_1 \geq \mu_2 \geq \cdots \geq \mu_M$ be the eigenvalues of~$K$. Then $\mu_i = \frac{1}{M} - \lambda_i$.
nodes.statement_short: Relate eigenvalues of K and L

nodes.name: Reduce to the top two eigenvalues of K
nodes.statement: Thus, it suffices to show that $\mu_1 = \frac{1}{M}$ and $\mu_2 = \frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m-1}{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the top two eigenvalues of K

nodes.name: Read them off from the eigenvectors
nodes.statement: By \Cref{prop:eigenvectors}, $\ket{\varphi_\alpha}$ has eigenvalue $\frac{1}{M}$ when $|\alpha| = 0$ and eigenvalue $\frac{1}{M} \cdot \frac{m-1}{m}$ when $|\alpha| =1$.
nodes.statement_short: Read them off from the eigenvectors

nodes.name: Compute (<u|-<v|) A_combine
nodes.statement: For any $u, v \in \mathbb F_q^m$, \begin{align} ((\bra{u} - \bra{v}) \otimes \bra{\psi})\cdot A_{\mathrm{combine}} &= ((\bra{u} - \bra{v}) \otimes \bra{\psi})\cdot \sum_{w \in \mathbb F_q^m} \ket{w} \otimes A^w \otimes I\nonumber\\ &= \bra{\psi}\cdot ((A^u- A^v) \otimes I). \end{align}

nodes.name: Expand with the Laplacian rewrite
nodes.statement: As a result, \begin{align*} &A_{\mathrm{combine}}^\dagger \cdot L \otimes \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot A_{\mathrm{combine}}\\ =~& \frac{1}{2} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} A_{\mathrm{combine}}^\dagger ((\ket{\boldsymbol{u}} - \ket{\boldsymbol{v}}) \cdot (\bra{\boldsymbol{u}} - \bra{\boldsymbol{v}})\otimes \ket{\psi} \bra{\psi})\cdot A_{\mathrm{combine}}\tag{by \Cref{prop:laplacian-rewrite}}\\ =~& \frac{1}{2} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} ((A^{\boldsymbol{u}} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}) \otimes I) \cdot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot ((A^{\boldsymbol{u}} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}) \otimes I). \tag{by \eqref{eq:reader-probably-has-no-idea-whats-going-on-yet}} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Take the trace
nodes.statement: Thus, if we take the trace, \begin{equation*} \mathrm{Tr}(A_{\mathrm{combine}}^\dagger \cdot (L \otimes \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) \cdot A_{\mathrm{combine}}) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}})^2 \otimes I \cdot \ket{\psi} = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A, \psi). \end{equation*} This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Compute A_0
nodes.statement: We begin by computing~$A_0$: \begin{equation*} A_0 = \bra{\varphi_0} \otimes I \cdot A_{\mathrm{combine}} = \bigg(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} \bra{u}\bigg) \otimes I \cdot \bigg(\sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} \ket{u} \otimes A^u \otimes I\bigg) = \frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} A^u \otimes I. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Constant component is A_avg
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} \ket{\varphi_0} \otimes A_0 = \bigg(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} \ket{u}\bigg)\otimes \bigg(\frac{1}{M^{1/2}} \cdot \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} A^u \otimes I\bigg) &= \frac{1}{M} \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} \ket{u} \otimes \sum_{v \in \mathbb F_q^m} A^v \otimes I\\ &= \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} \ket{u} \otimes A_{\mathrm{avg}} \otimes I, \end{align*} where we have written $A_{\mathrm{avg}} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}$.

nodes.name: Orthogonal component is A^u - A_avg
nodes.statement: As a result, \begin{equation*} \ket{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp} = A_{\mathrm{combine}} - \ket{\varphi_0} \otimes A_0 = \sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^n} \ket{u} \otimes (A^u - A_{\mathrm{avg}}) \otimes I. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Expand the quadratic form
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{align*} &\bra{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp} \cdot (I \otimes \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) \cdot \ket{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp}\\ =&\sum_{u, v \in \mathbb F_q^m} \braket{u \mid v} \otimes ((A^u - A_{\mathrm{avg}}) \otimes I) \cdot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot ((A^v - A_{\mathrm{avg}}) \otimes I)\\ =&\sum_{u \in \mathbb F_q^m} ((A^u - A_{\mathrm{avg}}) \otimes I) \cdot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot ((A^u - A_{\mathrm{avg}}) \otimes I). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Take the trace
nodes.statement: As a result, if we take the trace, \begin{equation} \frac{1}{M} \cdot \mathrm{Tr}(\bra{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp} \cdot (I \otimes \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) \cdot \ket{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp}) = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}} - A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Variance around the mean equals pairwise variance
nodes.statement: We can rewrite the squared expression as \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}(A^{\boldsymbol{u}} - A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2 &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}((A^{\boldsymbol{u}})^2 + (A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2 - A^{\boldsymbol{u}} \cdot A_{\mathrm{avg}} - A_{\mathrm{avg}} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}})\\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}((A^{\boldsymbol{u}})^2 - (A_{\mathrm{avg}})^2)\\ &= \frac{1}{2}\cdot\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}((A^{\boldsymbol{u}})^2 + (A^{\boldsymbol{v}})^2 - A^{\boldsymbol{u}} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}})\\ &= \frac{1}{2}\cdot\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}(A^{\boldsymbol{u}} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}})^2. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Variance around the mean equals pairwise variance

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus, \begin{equation*} \eqref{eq:just-took-trace} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}})^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi} = \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A, \psi). \end{equation*} This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Constant vector is a 0-eigenvector of L
nodes.statement: We begin by computing \begin{align} A_{\mathrm{combine}}^\dagger \cdot L \otimes \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot A_{\mathrm{combine}} &=(\bra{\varphi_0} \otimes A_0 + \bra{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp}) \cdot L \otimes \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot (\ket{\varphi_0} \otimes A_0 + \ket{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp})\nonumber\\ &=\bra{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp} \cdot L \otimes \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot \ket{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp} \nonumber\\ & = \bra{\varphi_{\perp}} L \ket{\varphi_{\perp}} \cdot A_{\perp} \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} A_{\perp} , \end{align} where the second step follows from the fact that $\ket{\varphi_{0}}$ is a $0$-eigenvector for $L$.
nodes.statement_short: Constant vector is a 0-eigenvector of L

nodes.name: Apply the spectral gap
nodes.statement: Note that because $\ket{\varphi_{\perp}}$ is orthogonal to $\ket{\varphi_0}$, \begin{equation*} \bra{\varphi_{\perp}} L \ket{\varphi_{\perp}} \geq \frac{1}{mM} \cdot \braket{\varphi_{\perp} \mid \varphi_{\perp}} \end{equation*} by \Cref{cor:laplacian-spectral-gap}.

nodes.name: Combine the two rewrites
nodes.statement: As a result, \begin{align*} \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A,\psi) & = \mathrm{Tr}(A_{\mathrm{combine}}^\dagger \cdot L \otimes \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot A_{\mathrm{combine}}) \tag{by \Cref{lem:local-rewrite}}\\ & = \bra{\varphi_{\perp}} L \ket{\varphi_{\perp}} \cdot \mathrm{Tr}(A_{\perp} \cdot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot A_{\perp}) \tag{by \Cref{eq:used-0-eigenvector}}\\ & \geq \frac{1}{mM} \cdot \braket{\varphi_{\perp} \mid \varphi_{\perp}} \cdot \mathrm{Tr}(A_{\perp} \cdot \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi} \cdot A_{\perp})\\ & = \frac{1}{mM} \cdot \mathrm{Tr}(\bra{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp} \cdot (I \otimes \ket{\psi}\bra{\psi}) \cdot \ket{\varphi_{\perp}} \otimes A_{\perp})\\ &= \frac{1}{m} \cdot \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A,\psi) . \tag{by \Cref{lem:global-rewrite}} \end{align*} This concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Sample a point, line and second point
nodes.statement: Let $\boldsymbol{u}$ and $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ be distributed as in the axis-parallel lines test, and sample $\boldsymbol{v} \sim \boldsymbol{\ell}$. Then $\boldsymbol{v}$ and $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ are also distributed as in the axis-parallel lines test.
nodes.section: 8 Global variance of the points measurements
nodes.statement_short: Sample a point, line and second point

nodes.name: Chain of six approximations via the lines measurement
nodes.statement: As a result, \begin{align*} A^u_{g(u)} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} &\approx_{2\delta} I \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} A^u_{g(u)}\tag{by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx}}\\ &\approx_{2\epsilon} B^\ell_{[f(u) = g(u)]} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2}\tag{by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx}}\\ &\approx_{\frac{md}{q}} B^\ell_{g|_{\ell}} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2}\tag{by \Cref{lem:generalize-b}}\\ &\approx_{\frac{md}{q}} B^\ell_{[f(v) = g(v)]} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2}\tag{by \Cref{lem:generalize-b}}\\ &\approx_{2\epsilon} I \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} A^v_{g(v)} \tag{by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx}}\\ &\approx_{2\delta} A^v_{g(v)} \otimes (G_g)^{1/2}.\tag{by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx}} \end{align*} Steps 1, 2, 5, and 6 are also using \Cref{rem:good-strat-characterization,prop:cab-approx-delta}.
nodes.section: 8 Global variance of the points measurements
nodes.statement_short: Chain of six approximations via the lines measurement

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: The lemma now follows from \Cref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}.
nodes.section: 8 Global variance of the points measurements

nodes.name: Rewrite the distance
nodes.statement: We want to bound \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{g(\boldsymbol{v})} ) \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{g(\boldsymbol{v})} )^2 \otimes G_g \ket{\psi}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 8 Global variance of the points measurements

nodes.name: Define A(g) and psi_g
nodes.statement: For each $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, define \begin{equation*} \forall u \in \mathbb F_q^m, ~ A(g)^u := A^u_{g(u)}, \qquad \text{and} \qquad \ket{\psi_g} := I \otimes (G_g)^{1/2} \ket{\psi}. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 8 Global variance of the points measurements

nodes.name: Apply local-to-global and the local variance bound
nodes.statement: Then \begin{align*} \eqref{eq:TODO:bound-this!} & = \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v} \sim \mathbb F_q^n} \bra{\psi_g} (A(g)^{\boldsymbol{u}} - A(g)^{\boldsymbol{v}})^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi_g}\\ & = \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}2\cdot \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{global}}(A(g), \psi_g)\\ & \leq \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}2m\cdot \mathbf{Var}_{\mathrm{local}}(A(g), \psi_g)\tag{by \Cref{lem:local-to-global}}\\ & = m \cdot \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}\mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \bra{\psi_g} (A(g)^{\boldsymbol{u}} - A(g)^{\boldsymbol{v}})^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi_g}\\ & = m \cdot \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}\mathop{\bf E\/}_{(\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}) \sim C} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{g(\boldsymbol{v})})^2 \otimes G_g \ket{\psi}\\ & \leq m \cdot 24\left(\epsilon + \delta + \frac{md}{q}\right).\tag{by \Cref{eq:equivalent-local-variance}} \end{align*} This concludes the proof.
nodes.section: 8 Global variance of the points measurements
nodes.statement_short: Apply local-to-global and the local variance bound

nodes.name: Plan: rewrite the primal canonically
nodes.statement: To show that~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} and~\eqref{eq:dual-objective} are dual to each other, we begin by rewriting the primal~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} in canonical form.

nodes.name: Define the canonical primal
nodes.statement: Let $r$ be the dimension of the space on which~$A$ acts. Let $M = |\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}|$ be the number of polynomials with individual degree $d$. We will assume some ordering of these polynomials $g_1, \ldots, g_M \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ which is allowed to be arbitrary. Consider the following semidefinite program: \begin{align} \sup &\quad \mathrm{tr}(C^\dagger X) \\ \text{s.t.} &\quad \mathrm{tr}(D_{ij}^\dagger X) = b_{ij} \qquad\forall i,j\in\{1,\ldots,r\},\nonumber\\ &\quad X \geq 0,\nonumber \end{align} where the variables~$C$, $D_{ij}$, and $b_{ij}$ are defined as follows: \begin{equation*} C = \sum_{i = 1}^M \ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes A_{g_i} \end{equation*} \begin{equation*} \forall i,j \in [r], \quad D_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^{M+1} \ket{k}\bra{k} \otimes \ket{i}\bra{j}, \qquad b_{ij} = \left\{\begin{array}{rl} 1 & \text{if } i = j,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array}\right. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Canonical primal equals the original primal
nodes.statement: We claim that \eqref{eq:primal-canonical} is equivalent to \eqref{eq:primal-objective}. To see this, let \begin{equation*} X = \sum_{i, j =1}^{M+1} \ket{i}\bra{j} \otimes X_{ij} \end{equation*} be a feasible solution to \eqref{eq:primal-canonical}. Then because $X \geq 0$, $X_{i i} \geq 0$ for each $i \in [M+1]$. In addition \begin{align*} \mathrm{tr}(D_{i_1 i_2}^\dagger X) &= \sum_k \sum_{j_1 j_2} \mathrm{tr}((\ket{k}\bra{k} \otimes \ket{i_1}\bra{i_2})\cdot(\ket{j_1} \bra{j_2} \otimes X_{j_1 j_2}))\\ &= \sum_k \bra{i_2} X_{k k} \ket{i_1}\\ &= \left\{\begin{array}{rl} 1 & \text{if } i_1 = i_2,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array}\right. \end{align*} This is equivalent to the statement $\sum_{i=1}^{M+1} X_{i i} = I$, which implies that $\sum_{i=1}^M X_{i i} \leq I$. Finally, the objective value \eqref{eq:primal-canonical} is \begin{align*} \mathrm{tr}(C^\dagger X) & = \sum_{i = 1}^M \sum_{j,k = 1}^{M+1} \mathrm{tr}((\ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes A_{g_i}^\dagger) \cdot (\ket{j}\bra{k} \otimes X_{j, k}))\\ &= \sum_{i = 1}^M \mathrm{tr}(A_{g_i}^\dagger \cdot X_{i, i})\\ &= \sum_{i = 1}^M \mathrm{tr}(A_{g_i} \cdot X_{i, i}). \tag{because~$A$ is Hermitian} \end{align*} As a result, setting $T_{g_i} = X_{i i}$ for each $i \in [M]$ gives a feasible solution to the original semidefinite program~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} with a matching objective value. A similar transformation allows us to convert solutions of~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} to~\eqref{eq:primal-canonical}.
nodes.statement_short: Canonical primal equals the original primal

nodes.name: Take a feasible block matrix X
nodes.statement: To see this, let \begin{equation*} X = \sum_{i, j =1}^{M+1} \ket{i}\bra{j} \otimes X_{ij} \end{equation*} be a feasible solution to \eqref{eq:primal-canonical}.
nodes.statement_short: Take a feasible block matrix X

nodes.name: Constraints force sum of diagonal blocks = I
nodes.statement: Then because $X \geq 0$, $X_{i i} \geq 0$ for each $i \in [M+1]$. In addition \begin{align*} \mathrm{tr}(D_{i_1 i_2}^\dagger X) &= \sum_k \sum_{j_1 j_2} \mathrm{tr}((\ket{k}\bra{k} \otimes \ket{i_1}\bra{i_2})\cdot(\ket{j_1} \bra{j_2} \otimes X_{j_1 j_2}))\\ &= \sum_k \bra{i_2} X_{k k} \ket{i_1}\\ &= \left\{\begin{array}{rl} 1 & \text{if } i_1 = i_2,\\ 0 & \text{otherwise}. \end{array}\right. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Constraints force sum of diagonal blocks = I

nodes.name: Diagonal blocks give a sub-measurement
nodes.statement: This is equivalent to the statement $\sum_{i=1}^{M+1} X_{i i} = I$, which implies that $\sum_{i=1}^M X_{i i} \leq I$.

nodes.name: Objective values match
nodes.statement: Finally, the objective value \eqref{eq:primal-canonical} is \begin{align*} \mathrm{tr}(C^\dagger X) & = \sum_{i = 1}^M \sum_{j,k = 1}^{M+1} \mathrm{tr}((\ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes A_{g_i}^\dagger) \cdot (\ket{j}\bra{k} \otimes X_{j, k}))\\ &= \sum_{i = 1}^M \mathrm{tr}(A_{g_i}^\dagger \cdot X_{i, i})\\ &= \sum_{i = 1}^M \mathrm{tr}(A_{g_i} \cdot X_{i, i}). \tag{because~$A$ is Hermitian} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Translate solutions both ways
nodes.statement: As a result, setting $T_{g_i} = X_{i i}$ for each $i \in [M]$ gives a feasible solution to the original semidefinite program~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} with a matching objective value. A similar transformation allows us to convert solutions of~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} to~\eqref{eq:primal-canonical}.

nodes.name: Write the canonical dual
nodes.statement: The dual of \eqref{eq:primal-canonical} is \begin{align} \inf &\quad \sum_i\, z_{ij} b_{ij} \\ \text{s.t.} &\quad \sum_{i,j} \,z_{ij} D_{ij} \geq C. \end{align}

nodes.name: Canonical dual equals the original dual
nodes.statement: We claim that \eqref{eq:dual-canonical} is equivalent to \eqref{eq:dual-objective}. To see this, we first calculate \begin{align*} \sum_{i,j=1}^r \,z_{ij} D_{ij} = \sum_{i,j=1}^r z_{ij} \cdot \sum_{k=1}^{M+1} \ket{k}\bra{k} \otimes \ket{i}\bra{j} &= \sum_{k=1}^{M+1} \ket{k}\bra{k} \otimes \left(\sum_{i, j=1}^r z_{ij}\ket{i}\bra{j}\right)\\ &=: \sum_{k=1}^{M+1}\ket{k}\bra{k} \otimes Z. \end{align*} Then the constraint \eqref{eq:dual-canonical-constraint} states that \begin{equation*} \sum_{i=1}^{M+1}\ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes Z \geq C = \sum_{i = 1}^M \ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes A_{g_i}, \end{equation*} which is equivalent to the statement that $Z \geq A_{g_i}$ for all $i \in [M]$ and $Z \geq 0$. In other words, $Z$ is a feasible solution to the original dual SDP \eqref{eq:dual-objective}, with value \begin{equation*} \mathrm{tr}(Z) = \sum_{i=1}^r Z_{i i} = \sum_{i,j=1}^r b_{i j} Z_{i j} = \sum_{i,j=1}^r b_{i j} z_{i j}, \end{equation*} the same value as in \eqref{eq:dual-canonical}. Hence, the two dual programs are the same as well, which implies that \eqref{eq:primal-objective} and \eqref{eq:dual-objective} form a primal/dual pair.
nodes.statement_short: Canonical dual equals the original dual

nodes.name: Compute sum z_ij D_ij
nodes.statement: To see this, we first calculate \begin{align*} \sum_{i,j=1}^r \,z_{ij} D_{ij} = \sum_{i,j=1}^r z_{ij} \cdot \sum_{k=1}^{M+1} \ket{k}\bra{k} \otimes \ket{i}\bra{j} &= \sum_{k=1}^{M+1} \ket{k}\bra{k} \otimes \left(\sum_{i, j=1}^r z_{ij}\ket{i}\bra{j}\right)\\ &=: \sum_{k=1}^{M+1}\ket{k}\bra{k} \otimes Z. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Constraint becomes Z >= A_g
nodes.statement: Then the constraint \eqref{eq:dual-canonical-constraint} states that \begin{equation*} \sum_{i=1}^{M+1}\ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes Z \geq C = \sum_{i = 1}^M \ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes A_{g_i}, \end{equation*} which is equivalent to the statement that $Z \geq A_{g_i}$ for all $i \in [M]$ and $Z \geq 0$.

nodes.name: Objective values match
nodes.statement: In other words, $Z$ is a feasible solution to the original dual SDP \eqref{eq:dual-objective}, with value \begin{equation*} \mathrm{tr}(Z) = \sum_{i=1}^r Z_{i i} = \sum_{i,j=1}^r b_{i j} Z_{i j} = \sum_{i,j=1}^r b_{i j} z_{i j}, \end{equation*} the same value as in \eqref{eq:dual-canonical}.

nodes.name: The programs form a primal/dual pair
nodes.statement: Hence, the two dual programs are the same as well, which implies that \eqref{eq:primal-objective} and \eqref{eq:dual-objective} form a primal/dual pair.
nodes.statement_short: The programs form a primal/dual pair

nodes.name: Strict feasibility gives strong duality via Slater
nodes.statement: To show that a primal/dual pair satisfies \emph{strong duality}, i.e.\ that their optimum values are the same, we use Slater's condition~\cite[Section~5.2.3]{cvxbook} and show that they satisfy \emph{strict feasibility}, which means both have a feasible solution which is positive \emph{definite} that satisfies all constraints with a strict inequality. It can be checked that the following two solutions to \eqref{eq:primal-objective} and \eqref{eq:dual-objective} satisfy this property: \begin{equation*} \forall g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}, \quad T_g = \frac{1}{2M} \cdot I, \qquad\qquad\qquad Z = 2I. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Strict feasibility gives strong duality via Slater

nodes.name: Complementary slackness
nodes.statement: Because they satisfy strong duality, their optimal solutions satisfy the \emph{complementary slackness} condition (see~\cite{AHO97}). If $X$ and $(z_{ij})$ are an optimal pair of solutions to~\eqref{eq:primal-canonical} and~\eqref{eq:dual-canonical} respectively, this implies that \begin{equation} X\Big( \sum_{i,j} \,z_{ij} D_{ij} - C \Big) \,=\, 0 \;. \end{equation} Clearly for any optimal pair $(X,z_{ij})$ we can assume without loss of generality that $X$ is block-diagonal.

nodes.name: Translate slackness to T and Z
nodes.statement: Then if we translate \eqref{eq:complementary-slackness} back to the variables $\{T_g\}$ and $Z$, we get \begin{align*} 0 = X\Big( \sum_{i,j} \,z_{ij} D_{ij} - C \Big) &= \sum_{i=1}^{M+1} \ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes X_{ii} \cdot \bigg(\sum_{i=1}^{M+1} \ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes Z - \sum_{i=1}^M \ket{i}\bra{i}\otimes A_{g_i}\bigg)\\ &= \sum_{i=1}^{M} \ket{i}\bra{i} \otimes (X_{ii} \cdot (Z - A_{g_i})) + \ket{M+1}\bra{M+1} \otimes (X_{M+1,M+1} \cdot Z). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Translate slackness to T and Z

nodes.name: Conclude T_g(Z - A_g) = 0 and sum T_g = I
nodes.statement: This implies that $X_{ii} \cdot (Z - A_{g_i}) = 0$ for $i \in [M]$ and $X_{M+1, M+1} = 0$. Translating back to the variables $\{T_g\}$ and $Z$, this gives $T_g(Z-A_g)=0$ for all $g\in\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$ and $\sum_g T_g = I$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude T_g(Z - A_g) = 0 and sum T_g = I

nodes.name: Take optimal SDP solutions T and Z
nodes.statement: We let $T = \{T_g\}$ and $Z$ be the optimal solutions to the SDPs~\eqref{eq:primal-objective} and \eqref{eq:dual-objective} respectively given by \Cref{lem:sdp}. Then~$T$ is a measurement, and \begin{align} \forall g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}: \qquad Z &\geq (\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}), \\ T_g \cdot Z &= T_g \cdot (\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Take optimal SDP solutions T and Z

nodes.name: Define H^u and show it is a sub-measurement
nodes.statement: For each $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$, define $H^u = \{H^u_h\}_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}$ as \begin{equation*} H^u_h := A^u_{h(u)}\cdot T_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)}. \end{equation*} Let $u \in \mathbb F_q^m$. Then \begin{align*} \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} H^u_h & = \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)}\\ & = \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q}A^u_{a} \cdot \bigg(\sum_{h:h(u) = a} T_h\bigg) \cdot A^u_{a}\\ & \leq \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} (A^u_{a})^2\tag{because~$T$ is a measurement}\\ & = \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} A^u_{a}\tag{$A$ is projective}\\ & = I. \end{align*} Hence, $H^u$ is a sub-measurement, and therefore $H^u \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define H^u and show it is a sub-measurement

nodes.name: Average to H, a sub-measurement
nodes.statement: Next, define $H = \{H_h\}_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}$ as \begin{equation*} H_h := \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m}H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_h. \end{equation*} Then \begin{equation*} \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} H_h = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_h \leq I. \tag{$H^u$ is a sub-measurement} \end{equation*} Hence, $H$ is a sub-measurement, and therefore $H \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$.

nodes.name: Set zeta_variance
nodes.statement: Set \begin{equation*} \zeta_{\mathrm{variance}} = 24m\cdot\Big(\epsilon + \delta + \frac{md}{q}\Big) \end{equation*} to be the error in \Cref{eq:local-variance-of-points-equation}.

nodes.name: Announce the technical lemma
nodes.statement: Prior to showing that~$H$ satisfies \Cref{item:self-improvement-A-consistency,item:self-improvement-completeness,item:self-improvement-self,item:self-improvement-boundedness}, we will prove the following technical lemma.

nodes.name: Expand H as an average of H^v
nodes.statement: We begin by expanding \begin{align} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes H^{\boldsymbol{v}}_h \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Expand H as an average of H^v

nodes.name: Move one A^v to the left
nodes.statement: We claim that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:expand-that-H} \approx_{\sqrt{2\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o) \otimes (T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes (T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}))\ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_h\cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline} The term inside the first square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a) \cdot \bigg( \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}},h(\boldsymbol{v}) = a}M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes T_h\bigg) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a) \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}, \tag{because $M^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ and $T_h$ are sub-measurements} \end{align*} which is at most~$2\delta$ by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx} and because~$A$ is $\delta$-self-consistent. The term inside the second square root is \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes H^{\boldsymbol{v}}_h \ket{\psi}, \end{equation*} which is at most~$1$ because $M^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ and $H^{\boldsymbol{v}}$ are sub-measurements.
nodes.statement_short: Move one A^v to the left

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes (T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}))\ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_h\cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline}

nodes.name: First factor at most 2delta
nodes.statement: The term inside the first square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a) \cdot \bigg( \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}},h(\boldsymbol{v}) = a}M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes T_h\bigg) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a) \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}, \tag{because $M^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ and $T_h$ are sub-measurements} \end{align*} which is at most~$2\delta$ by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx} and because~$A$ is $\delta$-self-consistent.

nodes.name: Second factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The term inside the second square root is \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes H^{\boldsymbol{v}}_h \ket{\psi}, \end{equation*} which is at most~$1$ because $M^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ and $H^{\boldsymbol{v}}$ are sub-measurements.

nodes.name: Move the other A^v to the left
nodes.statement: Next, we claim that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:move-one} \approx_{\sqrt{2\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align} &\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o) \otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}\Big|\nonumber\\ &\leq\sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}\nonumber\\ &\quad\cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}}. \end{align} The term inside the first square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot \bigg(\sum_{o:(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \bigg)\cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})^2 \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\tag{because~$M$ is a sub-measurement}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} I \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\tag{because~$A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \leq I$}\\ =~&1.\tag{because~$T$ is a measurement} \end{align*} As for the term inside the second square root, it is equal to the term inside the first square root in \Cref{eq:move-one-cauchy-schwarz}, which we showed was at most $2\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Move the other A^v to the left

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align} &\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o) \otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}\Big|\nonumber\\ &\leq\sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}\nonumber\\ &\quad\cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}}. \end{align}

nodes.name: First factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The term inside the first square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot \bigg(\sum_{o:(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \bigg)\cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})^2 \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\tag{because~$M$ is a sub-measurement}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} I \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\tag{because~$A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \leq I$}\\ =~&1.\tag{because~$T$ is a measurement} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Second factor at most 2delta
nodes.statement: As for the term inside the second square root, it is equal to the term inside the first square root in \Cref{eq:move-one-cauchy-schwarz}, which we showed was at most $2\delta$.

nodes.name: Swap one A^v for A^u
nodes.statement: Having moved both $A$'s to the left-hand side, we want to show that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:move-another} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline} The term inside the first square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot \bigg( \sum_{o:(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}}M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o\bigg) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})^2 \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \tag{because~$M^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*} But $T \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$, and so by \Cref{lem:global-variance-of-points} this expression is at most $\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$. As for the term inside the second square root, it is equal to the term inside the first square root in \Cref{eq:move-another-cauchy-schwarz}, which we showed was at most~$1$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline}

nodes.name: Bound by squared difference
nodes.statement: The term inside the first square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot \bigg( \sum_{o:(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}}M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o\bigg) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})^2 \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \tag{because~$M^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Global variance bound
nodes.statement: But $T \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$, and so by \Cref{lem:global-variance-of-points} this expression is at most $\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$.

nodes.name: Second factor at most 1
nodes.statement: As for the term inside the second square root, it is equal to the term inside the first square root in \Cref{eq:move-another-cauchy-schwarz}, which we showed was at most~$1$.

nodes.name: Swap the other A^v for A^u
nodes.statement: Finally, we want to show that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:change-one} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline*} \Big| \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*} The term inside the first square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot \bigg(\sum_{o:(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \bigg)\cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})^2 \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\tag{because~$M$ is a sub-measurement}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} I \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\tag{because~$A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \leq I$}\\ =~&1.\tag{because~$T$ is a measurement} \end{align*} As for the term inside the second square root, it is equal to the term inside the first square root in \Cref{eq:change-one-cauchy-schwarz}, which we showed was at most $\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Swap the other A^v for A^u

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline*} \Big| \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \cdot M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} - A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: First factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The term inside the first square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot \bigg(\sum_{o:(o, h) \in S_{\boldsymbol{u}}} M^{\boldsymbol{u}}_o \bigg)\cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})^2 \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\tag{because~$M$ is a sub-measurement}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} I \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\tag{because~$A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \leq I$}\\ =~&1.\tag{because~$T$ is a measurement} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Second factor bounded by zeta_variance
nodes.statement: As for the term inside the second square root, it is equal to the term inside the first square root in \Cref{eq:change-one-cauchy-schwarz}, which we showed was at most $\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$.

nodes.name: Total error 4sqrt(zeta_variance)
nodes.statement: This concludes the proof with an error of $2\sqrt{2\delta} + 2\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}$. The lemma now follows by observing that $2\delta \leq \zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$.

nodes.name: Write completeness via T
nodes.statement: The completeness of~$H$ is \begin{align} \sum_h \bra{\psi} H_h \otimes I \ket{\psi} & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_h \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \cdot T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Move one A to the other side
nodes.statement: We claim that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:bracketize-the-expression} \approx_{2\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference \begin{multline*} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \cdot (( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes I) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a})^2 \ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \cdot T^2_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*} The expression inside the first square root is at most $2\delta \leq 4 \delta$ by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx} and the self-consistency of~$A$, and the expression inside the second square root is at most~$1$ because $T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \leq I$.
nodes.statement_short: Move one A to the other side

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference \begin{multline*} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \cdot (( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes I) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a})^2 \ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \cdot T^2_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: Bound the factors
nodes.statement: The expression inside the first square root is at most $2\delta \leq 4 \delta$ by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx} and the self-consistency of~$A$, and the expression inside the second square root is at most~$1$ because $T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \leq I$.

nodes.name: Remove the other A
nodes.statement: Next, we claim that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:yet-another-move-a} \approx_{\sqrt{\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline*} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes (I-A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]})^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a})^2 \otimes (I-A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a})^2 \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*} The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$T$ is a sub-measurement. By the projectivity of~$A$, the expression inside the second square root is equal to \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes (I-A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \ket{\psi} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_{a\neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{b} \ket{\psi}, \end{equation*} which is at most~$\delta$ by the self-consistency of~$A$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline*} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes (I-A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( T_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]})^2 \otimes I \ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a})^2 \otimes (I-A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a})^2 \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: First factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$T$ is a sub-measurement.

nodes.name: Second factor at most delta
nodes.statement: By the projectivity of~$A$, the expression inside the second square root is equal to \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} ( A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \otimes (I-A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a}) \ket{\psi} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_{a\neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{b} \ket{\psi}, \end{equation*} which is at most~$\delta$ by the self-consistency of~$A$.

nodes.name: Replace E_u A by Z via complementary slackness
nodes.statement: We can rewrite \Cref{eq:mysterious-case-of-the-disappearing-a} as \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} ( T_{h} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \sum_h \bra{\psi} ( T_{h} \cdot\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \sum_h \bra{\psi} ( T_{h} \cdot Z) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\tag{by \Cref{eq:swap-Z-for-A}}\\ =~& \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi}.\tag{because~$T$ is a measurement} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Replace E_u A by Z via complementary slackness

nodes.name: Record completeness >= <Z> - 3sqrt(delta)
nodes.statement: We pause and record what we have shown so far: \begin{equation} \sum_h \bra{\psi} H_h \otimes I \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 3\sqrt{\delta}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lower bound <Z> by 1 - nu
nodes.statement: At this point, we can lower-bound \begin{align*} \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} \geq~& \sum_g \bra{\psi} Z \otimes G_g \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$G$ is a sub-measurement}\\ \geq~& \sum_g \bra{\psi} (\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes G_g \ket{\psi} \tag{by \Cref{eq:Z-greater-than-A}}\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes G_{[g(\boldsymbol{u})=a]} \ket{\psi}\\ \geq~& 1-\nu.\tag{by \Cref{item:self-improvement-G-consistency} and \Cref{prop:simeq-for-measurements}} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus, the completeness is at least $1 - \nu - 3\sqrt{\delta}$. The proof follows from noting that $3\sqrt{\delta} \leq \zeta$.

nodes.name: Write the inconsistency
nodes.statement: The inconsistency of~$H$ with~$A$ is \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes H_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = b]} \ket{\psi} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a, h: h(\boldsymbol{u}) \neq a} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes H_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Apply the technical lemma with M = A
nodes.statement: We now apply \Cref{lem:add-in-u} to the right-hand side of \Cref{eq:consistency-with-A-baby-step}. To do so, we set $\mathcal{O} = \mathbb F_q^m$, $M = A$, and $S_u = \{(a, h) : h(u) \neq a\}$. Then \Cref{lem:add-in-u} implies that \begin{equation*} \eqref{eq:consistency-with-A-baby-step} \approx_{4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a, h: h(\boldsymbol{u}) \neq a} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_a \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})})\otimes T_h \ket{\psi}, \end{equation*} which is equal to~$0$ because~$A$ is projective.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the technical lemma with M = A

nodes.name: Inconsistency at most 4sqrt(zeta_variance)
nodes.statement: This implies that \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{a \neq b} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes H_{[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = b]} \ket{\psi} \leq 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Bound by zeta
nodes.statement: The proof follows from noting that \begin{align*} 4\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} &= 4 \cdot \sqrt{24 m \cdot\Big(\epsilon + \delta + \frac{md}{q}\Big)}\\ &\leq 20 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\\ &\leq \zeta. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Sandwich identities for H^u
nodes.statement: We begin by recording the following facts which follow from the definition of $H^u_h$ and the projectivity of~$A$: \begin{align} H^u_h &= A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)} = A^u_{h(u)} \cdot H^u_h \cdot A^u_{h(u)},\\ A^u_{h(u)} \cdot H^u_{h'} \cdot A^u_{h(u)} &= H^u_{h'} \cdot A^u_{h(u)} = (A^u_{h(u)} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^u_{h(u)}) \cdot \boldsymbol{1}[h(u) = h'(u)]. \end{align}

nodes.name: Write the self-agreement
nodes.statement: The strong self-consistency of~$H$ is \begin{equation} \sum_{h\in\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} H_h \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} H_h^{\boldsymbol{u}} \otimes H_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Apply the technical lemma with M = H
nodes.statement: We now apply \Cref{lem:add-in-u} to the right-hand side of \Cref{eq:self-consistency-baby-step}. To do so, we set \begin{equation*} \text{$\mathcal{O} =\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, $M = H$, and $S_u = \{(h, h) : h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}\}$.} \end{equation*} Then \Cref{lem:add-in-u} implies that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:self-consistency-baby-step} \approx_{4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \cdot H_h^{\boldsymbol{u}} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the technical lemma with M = H

nodes.name: Add the terms with h distinct from h'
nodes.statement:
Having placed two $A$'s on the left-hand side, we want to show that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:release-the-kraken} \approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} +  rac{md}{q}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} \cdot H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} We note that \eqref{eq:threw-in-h-prime} is at least as big as \eqref{eq:release-the-kraken}. Thus, we want to upper-bound  egin{align} \eqref{eq:threw-in-h-prime}-\eqref{eq:release-the-kraken} & = \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} \cdot H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}

The term inside the second square root is equal to  egin{equation*} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h 
eq h'}  ra{\psi} H^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{u}) = h'( oldsymbol{u})], \end{equation*} which is at most~$1$ because $T$ and $H^{ oldsymbol{u}}$ are sub-measurements. Next, we show that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:swapped-u-for-v} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h

eq h'}  ra{\psi} (A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot  rac{md}{q} 	ag{by Schwartz-Zippel}\ \leq~&  rac{md}{q}. 	ag{by \Cref{eq:gonna-use-this-later}} \end{align*}
