eq h'}  ra{\psi} ( (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}) \cdot T_{h'} \cdot (A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{h( oldsymbol{u})} - A^{ oldsymbol{v}}_{h( oldsymbol{v})}))\otimes T_h\ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: First factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The term inside the first square root is at most \begin{align} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h \neq h'} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})\otimes T_h\ket{\psi} & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot \bigg(\sum_{h' \neq h} T_{h'}\bigg) \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}\\ & \leq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})^2\otimes T_h\ket{\psi}\tag{$T$ is a sub-measurement}\\ & \leq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} I \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}\tag{because $A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \leq I$}\\ & \leq 1, \end{align} where the last step again uses the fact that~$T$ is a sub-measurement.

nodes.name: Second factor at most zeta_variance
nodes.statement: As for the term inside the second square root, it is equal to the term inside the first square root in \Cref{eq:swapped-u-for-cauchy-schwarz}, which we showed was at most $\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$.

nodes.name: Off-diagonal terms at most md/q by Schwartz-Zippel
nodes.statement: Finally, \Cref{eq:swapped-u-for-v-this-time-it's-personal} is equal to \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h \neq h'} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}}\boldsymbol{1}[h(\boldsymbol{u}) = h'(\boldsymbol{u})]\\ \leq~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h \neq h'} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \cdot T_{h'} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi} \cdot \frac{md}{q} \tag{by Schwartz-Zippel}\\ \leq~& \frac{md}{q}. \tag{by \Cref{eq:gonna-use-this-later}} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Off-diagonal terms at most md/q by Schwartz-Zippel

nodes.name: Delete an A
nodes.statement: By~\Cref{eq:h-blt}, \Cref{eq:threw-in-h-prime} is equal to \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^m} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} (H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Swap A^u for A^v
nodes.statement: Now, we show that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:delete-an-A} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} (H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} (H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ &\leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}}\\ &\quad\cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}}. \end{align*} The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$T$ and~$H^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ are sub-measurements. The term inside the second square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot \bigg( \sum_{h'} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'}\bigg) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})^2 \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}. \tag{because $H^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*} But $T \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$, and so by \Cref{lem:global-variance-of-points} this expression is at most~$\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} (H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ &\leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}}\\ &\quad\cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: First factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$T$ and~$H^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ are sub-measurements.

nodes.name: Bound by squared difference
nodes.statement: The term inside the second square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} ((A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \cdot \bigg( \sum_{h'} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'}\bigg) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})) \otimes T_h \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} (A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} - A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})})^2 \otimes T_h\ket{\psi}. \tag{because $H^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Global variance bound
nodes.statement: But $T \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$, and so by \Cref{lem:global-variance-of-points} this expression is at most~$\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}$.

nodes.name: Move A^v to the other side
nodes.statement: Next, we show that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:swap-u-for-v-attack-of-the-clones} \approx_{\sqrt{2\delta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes (T_h \cdot A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} (H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'}\otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ =~&\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi} \bigg( \sum_{h'}H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes \sum_{h:h(\boldsymbol{v}) = a} T_h \bigg) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq~& \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi} \bigg( \sum_{h'}H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes \sum_{h:h(\boldsymbol{v}) = a} T_h\bigg)^2\ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi}(A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}}. \end{align*} The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$T$ and~$H^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ are sub-measurements, and the expression inside the second square root is at most~$2\delta$ by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx} and the self-consistency of~$A$.
nodes.statement_short: Move A^v to the other side

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{h, h' \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} (H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'}\otimes T_h) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})} \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ =~&\Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi} \bigg( \sum_{h'}H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes \sum_{h:h(\boldsymbol{v}) = a} T_h \bigg) \cdot (A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq~& \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi} \bigg( \sum_{h'}H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes \sum_{h:h(\boldsymbol{v}) = a} T_h\bigg)^2\ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a \in \mathbb F_q} \bra{\psi}(A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a \otimes I - I \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_a)^2 \ket{\psi}}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Bound both factors
nodes.statement: The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$T$ and~$H^{\boldsymbol{u}}$ are sub-measurements, and the expression inside the second square root is at most~$2\delta$ by \Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx} and the self-consistency of~$A$.

nodes.name: Lower bound via Z and consistency with A
nodes.statement: Now, \Cref{eq:move-over-v} is equal to \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_{h, h'} \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes (T_h\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h(\boldsymbol{v})}) \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_{h, h'} \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes (T_h\cdot Z)\ket{\psi} \tag{by \Cref{eq:swap-Z-for-A}}\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_{ h'} \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes Z\ket{\psi} \tag{because~$T$ is a measurement}\\ \geq~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_{ h'} \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h'(\boldsymbol{v})} \ket{\psi} \tag{by \Cref{eq:Z-greater-than-A}}\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, \boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{ h'} \bra{\psi} H^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h'} \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{h'(\boldsymbol{v})} \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} H_{[h(\boldsymbol{v})=a]} \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{a} \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} H_{[h(\boldsymbol{v})=a]} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a\neq b} \bra{\psi} H_{[h(\boldsymbol{v})=a]} \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}}_{b} \ket{\psi}\tag{because~$A$ is a measurement}\\ \geq~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} \sum_{a} \bra{\psi} H_{[h(\boldsymbol{v})=a]} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} \tag{by \Cref{eq:explicit-bound-for-A-consistency}}\\ =~& \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} H_h \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound via Z and consistency with A

nodes.name: Collect errors, bounded by zeta
nodes.statement: In total, we have shown that \begin{equation*} \sum_{h\in\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \bra{\psi} H_h \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} \geq \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} H_h \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 7 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} - \sqrt{2\delta} - \frac{md}{q} - 4\sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}. \end{equation*} Because \begin{align*} 11 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} + \sqrt{2\delta} + \frac{md}{q} & = 11 \sqrt{24m\cdot\Big(\epsilon + \delta + \frac{md}{q}\Big)} + \sqrt{2\delta} + \frac{md}{q}\\ &\leq 55 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big) + 2\sqrt{\delta} + m \cdot (d/q)^{1/2}\\ &\leq 57 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\\ &\leq \zeta, \end{align*} this concludes the proof of \Cref{item:self-improvement-self}.

nodes.name: Bound via consistency and completeness
nodes.statement: The boundedness of~$H$ is \begin{align*} &\bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_a \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes H_{[h(\boldsymbol{u})=a]} \ket{\psi} \\ =~& \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{h(\boldsymbol{u})} \otimes H_h \ket{\psi}\\ =~& \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} I \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} +\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_{a, h:h(\boldsymbol{u})\neq a} \bra{\psi} A^{\boldsymbol{u}}_{a} \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$A$ is a measurement}\\ \leq~& \bra{\psi} Z \otimes I \ket{\psi} -\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \sum_h \bra{\psi} I \otimes H_h \ket{\psi} + 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}\tag{by \Cref{eq:explicit-bound-for-A-consistency}}\\ \leq~& 3 \sqrt{\delta} + 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}}.\tag{by \Cref{eq:gonna-use-this-later-H-versus-Z}} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Error at most zeta
nodes.statement: We can bound the error by \begin{align*} 3 \sqrt{\delta} + 4 \sqrt{\zeta_{\mathrm{variance}}} & = 3 \sqrt{\delta} + 4 \sqrt{24m\cdot\Big(\epsilon + \delta + \frac{md}{q}\Big)}\\ & \leq 3 \sqrt{\delta} + 20 m\cdot\Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\\ &\leq 23 m\cdot\Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\\ & \leq \zeta. \end{align*} This completes the proof. \qed

nodes.name: WLOG parameters at most 1
nodes.statement: We note that the bound we are proving is trivial when at least one of $\epsilon$, $\delta$, or $d/q$ is $\geq 1$. In this case, $\zeta \geq 3000$. Hence, we may assume that $\gamma, \zeta, d/q \leq 1$. This will aid us when carrying out the error calculations near the end of the proof, as it allows us to bound terms like $\epsilon^{1/2}$ by terms like $\epsilon^{1/4}$.

nodes.name: Apply the non-projective lemma
nodes.statement: To begin, apply \Cref{lem:self-improvement-helper} to~$G$. Let $\widehat{H} \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$ be the sub-measurement it outputs and let $\widehat{\zeta}$ be the error \begin{equation*} \widehat{\zeta} = 100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency of H-hat
nodes.statement: By \Cref{item:self-improvement-self} of \Cref{lem:self-improvement-helper}, \begin{equation*} \sum_{h} \bra{\psi} \widehat{H}_h \otimes \widehat{H}_h \ket{\psi} \geq \bra{\psi} \widehat{H} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \widehat{\zeta}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Orthogonalize to projective H
nodes.statement: Thus, \Cref{thm:orthonormalization} implies the existence of a projective sub-measurement $H \in \polysub{m}{q}{d}$ such that \begin{equation} \widehat{H}_h \otimes I \approx_{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}} H_{h} \otimes I, \end{equation} where \begin{equation*} \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}} = 100 \widehat{\zeta}^{1/4}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Data processing closeness
nodes.statement: In addition, \Cref{prop:self-consistency-implies-data-processing} implies that \begin{equation} \widehat{H}_{[h(u)=a]} \otimes I \approx_{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}}} H_{[h(u)=a]} \otimes I, \end{equation} where \begin{equation*} \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}} = 8 \widehat{\zeta} + 8 \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Verify the four properties
Completeness
nodes.statement: (Completeness): \Cref{prop:completeness-transfer-self-consistent-A} implies that \begin{align*} \bra{\psi} H \otimes I \ket{\psi} & \geq \bra{\psi} \widehat{H} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \widehat{\zeta} - 2\sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}}\\ & \geq (1-\nu) - 2\widehat{\zeta} - 2\sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}}. \tag{by \Cref{item:self-improvement-projective-completeness} of \Cref{lem:self-improvement-helper}} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Consistency with A
nodes.statement: (Consistency with~$A$): \Cref{prop:triangle-sub} applied to \Cref{item:self-improvement-projective-A-consistency} of \Cref{lem:self-improvement-helper} implies that \begin{equation*} A^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\widehat{\zeta} + \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}}}} I \otimes H_{[h(u) = a]}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Strong self-consistency
nodes.statement: (Strong self-consistency): \Cref{prop:two-notions-of-self-consistency} implies that \begin{equation*} \widehat{H}_h \otimes I \approx_{2\widehat{\zeta}} I \otimes \widehat{H}_h. \end{equation*} Thus, \begin{equation*} H_h \otimes I \approx_{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}} \widehat{H}_{h} \otimes I \approx_{2\widehat{\zeta}} I \otimes \widehat{H}_{h} \approx_{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}} I \otimes H_h. \end{equation*} Hence, by \Cref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}, \begin{equation*} H_h \otimes I \approx_{6 \widehat{\zeta} + 6\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}} I \otimes H_h. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Boundedness
List the four errors
nodes.statement: This shows the four properties hold with errors \begin{equation*} 2\widehat{\zeta} + 2\sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}},\quad \widehat{\zeta} + \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}}},\quad 6 \widehat{\zeta} + 6\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}},\quad \text{and} \quad \widehat{\zeta} + \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}}}, \end{equation*} respectively.

nodes.name: Bound all errors by zeta
nodes.statement: We now show that these four are bounded by~$\zeta$. First, using the fact that $100^{1/4} \leq 4$, we note that \begin{align*} \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}} = 100 \widehat{\zeta}^{1/4} &= 100 \Big(100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\Big)^{1/4}\\ &\leq 400 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big). \end{align*} Hence, \begin{align*} 6 \widehat{\zeta} + 6\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}} & \leq 6 \Big(100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\Big) + 6 \Big(400 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big)\Big)\\ &\leq 600m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big) +2400 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big)\\ &= 3000m\cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big), \end{align*} which is less than~$\zeta$. In addition, using the fact that~$\sqrt{400} = 20$, we also note that \begin{align*} \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}} &= 8 \widehat{\zeta} + 8 \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}}\\ &\leq 8 \Big(100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\Big) + 8 \sqrt{400 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big)}\\ &\leq 800m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/16} + \delta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\Big) + 160m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/16} + \delta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\Big)\\ &= 960m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/16} + \delta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\Big), \end{align*} which is clearly less than $\zeta$. Thus, $2\widehat{\zeta} + 2\sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}} \leq \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}} \leq \zeta$. Finally, using $\sqrt{960} \leq 31$, \begin{align*} \widehat{\zeta} + \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}}} &\leq 100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big) + \sqrt{960m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/16} + \delta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\Big)}\\ &\leq 100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big) + 31 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big)\\ &= 131m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big), \end{align*} which is also less than~$\zeta$. This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Bound zeta_ortho
nodes.statement: First, using the fact that $100^{1/4} \leq 4$, we note that \begin{align*} \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}} = 100 \widehat{\zeta}^{1/4} &= 100 \Big(100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\Big)^{1/4}\\ &\leq 400 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big). \end{align*}

nodes.name: Bound the self-consistency error
nodes.statement: Hence, \begin{align*} 6 \widehat{\zeta} + 6\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}} & \leq 6 \Big(100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\Big) + 6 \Big(400 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big)\Big)\\ &\leq 600m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big) +2400 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big)\\ &= 3000m\cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big), \end{align*} which is less than~$\zeta$.

nodes.name: Bound zeta_dataprocess
nodes.statement: In addition, using the fact that~$\sqrt{400} = 20$, we also note that \begin{align*} \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}} &= 8 \widehat{\zeta} + 8 \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}}\\ &\leq 8 \Big(100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big)\Big) + 8 \sqrt{400 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/8} + \delta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\Big)}\\ &\leq 800m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/16} + \delta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\Big) + 160m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/16} + \delta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\Big)\\ &= 960m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/16} + \delta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\Big), \end{align*} which is clearly less than $\zeta$.

nodes.name: Bound the completeness error
nodes.statement: Thus, $2\widehat{\zeta} + 2\sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{ortho}}} \leq \widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}} \leq \zeta$.

nodes.name: Bound the remaining errors
nodes.statement: Finally, using $\sqrt{960} \leq 31$, \begin{align*} \widehat{\zeta} + \sqrt{\widehat{\zeta}_{\mathrm{dataprocess}}} &\leq 100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/2} + \delta^{1/2} + (d/q)^{1/2}\Big) + \sqrt{960m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/16} + \delta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\Big)}\\ &\leq 100m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big) + 31 m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big)\\ &= 131m \cdot \Big(\epsilon^{1/32} + \delta^{1/32} + (d/q)^{1/32}\Big), \end{align*} which is also less than~$\zeta$. This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Consistency with diagonal lines
nodes.statement: The strategy passes the diagonal lines test with probability $1-\gamma$. Therefore, it passes the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test with probability $1- \gamma\cdot m$. This means that \begin{equation*} A^{u}_a \otimes I \simeq_{\gamma \cdot m} I \otimes L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}, \end{equation*} on average over a uniformly random $\boldsymbol{u} \sim \mathbb F_q^{m}$ and a uniformly random line $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ in $\mathbb F_q^m$ containing $\boldsymbol{u}$.

nodes.name: Convert to closeness
nodes.statement: By~\Cref{prop:simeq-to-approx}, this implies that \begin{equation} A^{u}_a \otimes I \approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} I \otimes L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Choose a random line through both points
nodes.statement: Let $\boldsymbol{u}$ and $\boldsymbol{v}$ be independent and uniformly random points in $\mathbb F_q^m$. Let $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ be a uniformly random line in $\mathbb F_q^m$ containing both points. (If $\boldsymbol{u}$ and $\boldsymbol{v}$ are distinct, then $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is just the unique line that passes through both of them. Otherwise, $\boldsymbol{u} = \boldsymbol{v}$, and $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is a uniformly random line passing through $\boldsymbol{u}$.) Then the marginal distribution on $\boldsymbol{u}$ and $\boldsymbol{\ell}$ is as in \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}, as is the marginal distribution on $\boldsymbol{v}$ and $\boldsymbol{\ell}$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose a random line through both points

nodes.name: Chain through the projective line measurement
nodes.statement: As a result, \begin{align*} (A^{u}_a \cdot A^{v}_b) \otimes I &\approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} A^{u}_a \otimes L^{\ell}_{[f(v)=b]} \tag{by \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}}\\ &\approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} I \otimes (L^{\ell}_{[f(v)=b]} \cdot L^{\ell}_{[f'(u)=a]}) \tag{by \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}}\\ &= I \otimes (L^{\ell}_{[f'(u)=a]} \cdot L^{\ell}_{[f(v)=b]}) \tag{because~$L$ is projective}\\ &\approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} A^{v}_b \otimes L^{\ell}_{[f'(u)=a]} \tag{by \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}}\\ &\approx_{2\cdot \gamma \cdot m} (A^{v}_b \cdot A^{u}_a) \otimes I. \tag{by \Cref{eq:point-diagonal-line-approx}} \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain through the projective line measurement

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: The theorem now follows from \Cref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}.

nodes.name: Abbreviate G^{u,x}_a
nodes.statement: For notational convenience we use the abbreviation $G^{u,x}_a = G^{x}_{[g(u) = a]}$ for all $(u,x) \in \mathbb F_q^{m+1}$.

nodes.name: Expand the commutator norm
nodes.statement: We expand the square: \begin{align} & \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} ( G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b - G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a )^\dagger \cdot( G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b - G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a ) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \nonumber\\ =~& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} ( G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a - G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b ) \cdot( G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b - G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a ) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \nonumber\\ =~& 2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \Big ( \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Big ), \end{align} where the last step uses the projectivity of~$G$.

nodes.name: Goal: second term close to first
nodes.statement: We will show that the second term of \Cref{eq:gcom8} is close to the first term.
nodes.statement_short: Goal: second term close to first

nodes.name: G^{u,x}_a is close to G^x tensor A^{u,x}_a
nodes.statement: To begin, we note that for each $(u, x) \in \mathbb F_q^{m+1}$, \begin{equation} G^{u, x} = \sum_a G^{u, x}_a = \sum_a G^{x}_{[g(u) = a]} = G^x. \end{equation} As a result, \Cref{item:data-processed-consistency} and \Cref{prop:cons-sub-meas} imply that \begin{align} G^{u,x}_a \otimes I &\approx_{4\zeta} G^{u, x} \otimes A^{u, x}_a \nonumber\\ &= G^{x} \otimes A^{u, x}_a, \end{align} where the second step is by \Cref{eq:sum-of-gux}.
nodes.statement_short: G^{u,x}_a is close to G^x tensor A^{u,x}_a

nodes.name: Insert A^{v,y}_b on the other side
nodes.statement: We can therefore approximate the second term of \Cref{eq:gcom8} as \begin{align} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \otimes I \ket{\psi} \nonumber\\ \approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta}}& \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{y}} \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \ket{\psi}. \end{align} using \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} and \Cref{eq:add-an-a}.
nodes.statement_short: Insert A^{v,y}_b on the other side

nodes.name: Drop G^y via the first claim
nodes.statement: Next, we claim that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:apply-add-an-a-once} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}}\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} This is proved in \Cref{clm:g-comm-stability} below.
nodes.statement_short: Drop G^y via the first claim

nodes.name: Insert A^{u,x}_a and commute the A's
nodes.statement: Continuing, we have \begin{align} \eqref{eq:gcom9} &\approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \nonumber\\ &\approx_{6\sqrt{\gamma (m+1)}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \ket{\psi}. \end{align} The first approximation again uses \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} and \Cref{eq:add-an-a}. The second approximation follows from \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} and \Cref{thm:commutativity-points}.
nodes.statement_short: Insert A^{u,x}_a and commute the A's

nodes.name: Drop G^x via the second claim
nodes.statement: Next, we claim that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:dunno-what-i-should-call-this} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}+6\sqrt{\gamma(m+1)}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u}, {\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} This is proved in \Cref{clm:g-comm-stability2} below.
nodes.statement_short: Drop G^x via the second claim

nodes.name: Remove the A's again
Self-consistency after evaluation
nodes.statement: Now, \Cref{item:data-processed-self-consistency} and the fact that~$G$ is projective allows us to apply \Cref{prop:two-notions-of-self-consistency}, which states that~$G$ is $\zeta/2$-strongly self-consistent. Hence, \Cref{prop:two-notions-of-self-consistency-after-evaluation} says that we can ``post-process'' its measurement outcomes: \begin{equation*} G^x_{[g(u)=a]} \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes G^x_{[g(u)=a]}. \end{equation*} In other words, using our abbreviation, \begin{equation} G^{u,x}_a \otimes I \approx_{\zeta} I \otimes G^{u,x}_a. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Second term close to first term
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{eq:new-fact-that-i-derived} twice with the help of \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip}, we conclude that \begin{align*} \eqref{eq:gonna-cite-this-in-just-a-bit} &\approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{v}, \boldsymbol{y}}_b \ket{\psi}\\ &\approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{v}, \boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{align*} Hence we have shown that the second term of \Cref{eq:gcom8} is close to the first term.
nodes.statement_short: Second term close to first term

nodes.name: Total error 48m(sqrt(gamma)+sqrt(zeta))
nodes.statement: Putting everything together, this shows that \Cref{eq:gcom8} is bounded by \begin{align*} &2\cdot\Big(2\sqrt{\zeta} + \sqrt{\zeta} + 2\sqrt{\zeta} +6\sqrt{\gamma(m+1)} + \sqrt{\zeta} + 6\sqrt{\gamma(m+1)} + 2\sqrt{\zeta} + 2\sqrt{\zeta} + \sqrt{\zeta} + \sqrt{\zeta}\Big)\\ =~& 24 \cdot(\sqrt{\gamma(m+1)}+\sqrt{\zeta})\\ \leq~& 24\sqrt{m+1} \cdot(\sqrt{\gamma}+\sqrt{\zeta})\\ \leq~& 48 m \cdot (\sqrt{\gamma} + \sqrt{\zeta}), \end{align*} and this completes the proof of the lemma, modulo the proofs of \Cref{clm:g-comm-stability} and \Cref{clm:g-comm-stability2}.

nodes.name: Proofs of the two claims
Conclude the lemma
nodes.statement: Having proved \Cref{clm:g-comm-stability} and \Cref{clm:g-comm-stability2}, we conclude the proof of \Cref{lem:comm-data-processed-g}.

nodes.name: Recall the abbreviation
nodes.statement: Recall that $G_b^{v,y} = G^y_{[g(v)=b]}= \sum_{g : g(v) = b} G_g^y$.

nodes.name: Define the sub-measurement R^y
nodes.statement: For all $y \in \mathbb F_q$ and $g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, define the matrix \[ R^y_g = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^y_g G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a. \] Then because~$G$ is a sub-measurement, \begin{equation*} \sum_{g} R^y_g = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a\cdot \Big(\sum_g G^y_g\Big) \cdot G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \leq\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_a G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \leq I. \end{equation*} As a result, $R^y$ is a sub-measurement in $\polysub{m}{q}{d}$.

nodes.name: Rewrite the error via R^y
Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: We can now bound the magnitude as follows. \begin{multline*} |\eqref{eq:bound-this-right-now!}| = \Big| \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi}\Big(\sqrt{R^{\boldsymbol{y}}_g} \otimes I\Big) \cdot \Big(\sqrt{R^{\boldsymbol{y}}_g} (I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}, \boldsymbol{y}}_{g(\boldsymbol{v})}\Big)\ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi}R^{\boldsymbol{y}}_g \otimes I\ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g}\bra{\psi}(I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) R^{\boldsymbol{y}}_g (I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}, \boldsymbol{y}}_{g(\boldsymbol{v})}\ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: First factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The term inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$R^y$ is a sub-measurement.

nodes.name: Second factor at most zeta by boundedness
nodes.statement: The term inside the second square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g}\bra{\psi}(I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) R^{\boldsymbol{y}}_g (I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v}, \boldsymbol{y}}_{g(\boldsymbol{v})}\ket{\psi}\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g}\bra{\psi}(I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) R^{\boldsymbol{y}}_g (I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} A^{\boldsymbol{v}, \boldsymbol{y}}_{g(\boldsymbol{v})}\right)\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g}\bra{\psi}(I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) R^{\boldsymbol{y}}_g (I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes Z^{\boldsymbol{y}}\ket{\psi}\tag{by~\Cref{item:data-processed-boundedness}}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes Z^{\boldsymbol{y}}\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\zeta.\tag{by~\Cref{item:data-processed-boundedness}} \end{align*} This concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Second factor at most zeta by boundedness

nodes.name: Commute the points measurements
nodes.statement: Our goal is to bound the magnitude of \begin{align} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ \approx_{6\sqrt{\gamma(m+1)}} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi}. \end{align} where the second line follows from \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} and \Cref{thm:commutativity-points}.

nodes.name: Rewrite the expression
nodes.statement: We now proceed nearly identically to \Cref{clm:g-comm-stability}. \begin{align} \eqref{eq:just-got-commuted} &=\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b}\sum_{g:g(\boldsymbol{u})=a} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_a \ket{\psi} \nonumber\\ &=\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})} \ket{\psi}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: Then we can bound the magnitude as follows. \begin{multline*} |\eqref{eq:g-comm-stab7}| = \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi} \Big(\sqrt{G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g}\otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b\Big) \cdot \Big(\sqrt{G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g} G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\Big)\ket{\psi} \Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g\otimes A^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b\ket{\psi}} \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: First factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The term inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$A$ are sub-measurements.

nodes.name: Second factor at most zeta
nodes.statement: The term inside the second square root is \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\ket{\psi}\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes \left(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} A^{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g(\boldsymbol{u})}\right)\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\ket{\psi}\tag{by~\Cref{item:data-processed-boundedness}}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{b} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) G^{\boldsymbol{v},\boldsymbol{y}}_b (I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \bra{\psi}(I-G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes Z^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\zeta.\tag{by~\Cref{item:data-processed-boundedness}} \end{align*} This concludes the proof.

nodes.name: WLOG parameters at most 1
nodes.statement: We note that the bound we are proving is trivial when at least one of $\gamma$, $\zeta$, or $d/q$ is $\geq 1$. In this case, $\nu \geq 30$. On the other hand, \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h} \Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes I - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h} \Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes I) \ket{\psi} + (- G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h} 2\cdot \Big(\Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes I) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 + \Vert(G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I) \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\Big) \tag{by \Cref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-vectors-squared}}\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h} 4\cdot \Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes I) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 \tag{by symmetry of the terms}\\ =~&4 \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}}\sum_{g, y} \bra{\psi} (G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes I) \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&4, \tag{because~$G$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*} which is therefore less than~$\nu$. Hence, we may assume that $\gamma, \zeta, d/q \leq 1$. This will aid us when carrying out the error calculations near the end of the proof, as it allows us to bound terms like $\zeta^{1/2}$ by terms like $\zeta^{1/4}$.

nodes.name: Expand the commutator norm
nodes.statement: Our goal is to bound \begin{align} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g)^\dagger \cdot(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h} \bra{\psi} ( G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g}- G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h )\cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ =~&2\cdot\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,h} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{x}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,h} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Goal: both terms near <G tensor G>
nodes.statement: We will show that both terms in \Cref{eq:gcomterms} are close to $\bra{\psi} G \otimes G \ket{\psi}$, where we recall that $G = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{x}} G^{\boldsymbol{x}}$. With the errors we derive, this will imply \Cref{thm:com-main}.
nodes.statement_short: Goal: both terms near <G tensor G>

nodes.name: First term via switching sandwiches
nodes.statement: For the first term in \Cref{eq:gcomterms}, we have \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,h} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{x}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I \ket{\psi}&= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi}( G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g\cdot G\cdot G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \\ &\approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_g \bra{\psi} G \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \ket{\psi} \\ &= \bra{\psi} G \otimes G \ket{\psi}, \end{align*} where the approximation is by \Cref{prop:switch-sandwich} and \Cref{item:commuting-self-consistency}.

nodes.name: Normalization lemma
nodes.statement: For the second term in \Cref{eq:gcomterms}, we begin with the following lemma. \begin{lemma} Let $P = \{P_a\}$ be a sub-measurement and $Q = \{Q_b\}$ be a projective sub-measurement. Define $C_{a, b} = Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_b$. Then $ \sum_a (\sum_b C_{a, b})^\dagger (\sum_b C_{a, b}) = \sum_a (\sum_b C_{a, b}) (\sum_b C_{a, b})^\dagger \leq I. $ \end{lemma} \begin{proof} The first equality follows from the fact that $C_{a, b}$ is Hermitian. As for the second equality, \begin{align*} \sum_a \Big(\sum_b C_{a, b}\Big) \Big(\sum_b C_{a, b}\Big)^\dagger &= \sum_a \sum_{b, b'} C_{a, b} \cdot C_{a, b'}\tag{$C_{a, b'}$ is Hermitian}\\ &= \sum_a \sum_{b, b'} (Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_b) \cdot (Q_{b'} \cdot P_a \cdot Q_{b'})\\ &= \sum_a \sum_{b} Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_{b}\tag{because $Q$ is projective}\\ &\leq \sum_a \sum_{b} Q_b \cdot P_a \cdot Q_{b}\tag{because $Q_b \leq I$}\\ &\leq I, \end{align*} because~$P$ and~$Q$ are sub-measurements. \end{proof}

nodes.name: Move G^x_g to the other side
nodes.statement: First, we show that \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,h} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,h} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \ket{\psi} \end{equation} This follows from \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} where we let ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' in the Proposition be $G^x_g \otimes I$ and $I \otimes G^x_g$, respectively, and let ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' denote $G^y_h G^x_g G^y_h$. The closeness between ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' follows from \Cref{item:commuting-self-consistency}, and the normalization condition on ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' follows from the projectivity of the~$\{G^y_h\}$ measurements and \Cref{lem:normalization-condition}.
nodes.statement_short: Move G^x_g to the other side

nodes.name: Apply closeness of inner products
nodes.statement: This follows from \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} where we let ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' in the Proposition be $G^x_g \otimes I$ and $I \otimes G^x_g$, respectively, and let ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' denote $G^y_h G^x_g G^y_h$.

nodes.statement: The closeness between ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' follows from \Cref{item:commuting-self-consistency}, and the normalization condition on ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' follows from the projectivity of the~$\{G^y_h\}$ measurements and \Cref{lem:normalization-condition}.

nodes.name: Evaluate g at a random point
nodes.statement:
Next, we show that  egin{align} \eqref{eq:gcom4} = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}, oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g,h}  ra{\psi} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g \ket{\psi} \approx_{ rac{dm}{q}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},{ oldsymbol{x}}, oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h}  ra{\psi} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} \ket{\psi}. \end{align} To do so, we first compute the difference as  egin{equation} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, { oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g 
eq g', h}  oldsymbol{1}[g( oldsymbol{u}) = g'( oldsymbol{u})] \cdot  ra{\psi} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{g'} \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} This is nonnegative and real, so it suffices to upper bound it, which we do as follows.  egin{align*} \eqref{eq:gcom4-diff} & = \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{ g 
eq g',h}  ra{\psi} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{g'} \ket{\psi} \cdot \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}}  oldsymbol{1}[g( oldsymbol{u}) = g'( oldsymbol{u})]\ & \leq \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g 
eq g', h}  ra{\psi} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{g'} \ket{\psi} \cdot  rac{dm}{q} 	ag{by Schwartz-Zippel}\ & \leq  rac{dm}{q}. 	ag{because~$G$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Write the difference
nodes.statement: To do so, we first compute the difference as \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, {\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g \neq g', h} \boldsymbol{1}[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = g'(\boldsymbol{u})] \cdot \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g'} \ket{\psi}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Bound by md/q via Schwartz-Zippel
nodes.statement: This is nonnegative and real, so it suffices to upper bound it, which we do as follows. \begin{align*} \eqref{eq:gcom4-diff} & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{ g \neq g',h} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g'} \ket{\psi} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \boldsymbol{1}[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = g'(\boldsymbol{u})]\\ & \leq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g \neq g', h} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g'} \ket{\psi} \cdot \frac{dm}{q} \tag{by Schwartz-Zippel}\\ & \leq \frac{dm}{q}. \tag{because~$G$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Move G^y_h to the other side
nodes.statement: Next, we show that \begin{align} \eqref{eq:evaluate-gcom-at-points} &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h} \bra{\psi} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \ket{\psi}\tag{\Cref{eq:evaluate-gcom-at-points} rewriten}\\ &\approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}}\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ &\approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \ket{\psi}. \end{align} These two approximations are derived as follows. \begin{enumerate} \item In the first approximation we used \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} where we let ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' in the Proposition be $G^x_{[g(u)=a]} \otimes I$ and $I \otimes G^x_{[g(u) = a]}$, respectively, and let ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' denote $G^y_h G^x_{[g(u)=a]} G^y_h$. The closeness between ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' follows from \Cref{item:commuting-self-consistency}, and the normalization condition on ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' follows from the projectivity of the~$\{G^y_h\}$ measurements and \Cref{lem:normalization-condition}. \item In the second approximation we used \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} where we let ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' in the Proposition be $G^y_h \otimes I$ and $I \otimes G^y_h$, respectively, and let ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' denote $G^x_{[g(u)=a]} G^y_h G^x_{[g(u)=a]}$. The closeness between ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' follows from \Cref{item:commuting-self-consistency}, and the normalization condition on ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' follows from the projectivity of the~$\{G^x_{[g(u)=a]}\}$ measurements and \Cref{lem:normalization-condition}.

The closeness between ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' follows from \Cref{item:commuting-self-consistency}, and the normalization condition on ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' follows from the projectivity of the~$\{G^y_h\}$ measurements and \Cref{lem:normalization-condition}.

nodes.name: Second approximation
nodes.statement: In the second approximation we used \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} where we let ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' in the Proposition be $G^y_h \otimes I$ and $I \otimes G^y_h$, respectively, and let ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' denote $G^x_{[g(u)=a]} G^y_h G^x_{[g(u)=a]}$. The closeness between ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' follows from \Cref{item:commuting-self-consistency}, and the normalization condition on ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' follows from the projectivity of the~$\{G^x_{[g(u)=a]}\}$ measurements and \Cref{lem:normalization-condition}.

nodes.name: Evaluate h at a random point
nodes.statement:
Analogously to the derivation of \Cref{eq:evaluate-gcom-at-points}, we now show that  egin{align} \eqref{eq:don't-understand-the-numbering-system} & = \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u},{ oldsymbol{x}}, oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h}  ra{\psi} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h \ket{\psi} 	ag{\Cref{eq:don't-understand-the-numbering-system} restated}\ & \approx_{ rac{dm}{q}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v},{ oldsymbol{x}}, oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b}  ra{\psi} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{[h( oldsymbol{v})=b]} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{[h( oldsymbol{v})=b]} \ket{\psi}. \end{align} To do so, we first compute the difference as  egin{equation} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, oldsymbol{v}, { oldsymbol{x}}, oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h
eq h'}  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{v}) = h'( oldsymbol{v})] \cdot  ra{\psi} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{h'} \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} This is nonnegative and real, so it suffices to upper bound it, which we do as follows.  egin{align*} \eqref{eq:eq:don't-understand-the-numbering-system-diff} & = \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, { oldsymbol{x}}, oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h
eq h'}  ra{\psi} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{h'} \ket{\psi} \cdot \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{v}}  oldsymbol{1}[h( oldsymbol{v}) = h'( oldsymbol{v})]\ & \leq \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}, { oldsymbol{x}}, oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h
eq h'}  ra{\psi} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{[g( oldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{h'} \ket{\psi} \cdot  rac{dm}{q} 	ag{by Schwartz-Zippel}\ & \leq  rac{dm}{q}. 	ag{because~$G$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Write the difference
nodes.statement: To do so, we first compute the difference as \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v}, {\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h\neq h'} \boldsymbol{1}[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = h'(\boldsymbol{v})] \cdot \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{h'} \ket{\psi}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Bound by md/q via Schwartz-Zippel
nodes.statement: This is nonnegative and real, so it suffices to upper bound it, which we do as follows. \begin{align*} \eqref{eq:eq:don't-understand-the-numbering-system-diff} & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, {\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h\neq h'} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{h'} \ket{\psi} \cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{v}} \boldsymbol{1}[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = h'(\boldsymbol{v})]\\ & \leq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}, {\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,h\neq h'} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{h'} \ket{\psi} \cdot \frac{dm}{q} \tag{by Schwartz-Zippel}\\ & \leq \frac{dm}{q}. \tag{because~$G$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Name the evaluation error
nodes.statement: Now, we set \begin{equation*} \nu_{\mathrm{evaluation}} = 48 m \cdot (\gamma^{1/2} + \zeta^{1/2}) \end{equation*} to be the approximation error from \Cref{lem:comm-data-processed-g}.

nodes.name: Use commutativity after evaluation
nodes.statement: We conclude by showing that \begin{align*} \eqref{eq:evaluate-gcom-at-points-part-dos} &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = b]} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = b]} \ket{\psi} \tag{\Cref{eq:evaluate-gcom-at-points-part-dos} restated}\\ &\approx_{\sqrt{\nu_{\mathrm{evaluation}}}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = b]} \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = b]} \ket{\psi} \\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = b]} \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = b]} \ket{\psi} \\ &\approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = b]} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = b]} \ket{\psi} \\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},{\boldsymbol{x}},\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{a,b} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{[g(\boldsymbol{u}) = a]} \otimes G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{[h(\boldsymbol{v}) = b]} \ket{\psi} \\ &= \bra{\psi} G \otimes G \ket{\psi}. \end{align*} The third and fifth lines follow from the projectivity of the $G$ measurements.

nodes.name: Justify the two approximations
nodes.statement: The two approximations are derived as follows. \begin{enumerate} \item In the first approximation we used \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} where we let ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' in the Proposition be $G^x_{[g(u)=a]} G^y_{[h(v)=b]} \otimes I$ and $G^y_{[h(v)=b]} G^x_{[g(u) = a]} \otimes I$, respectively, and let ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' denote $G^x_{[g(u)=a]} \otimes G^y_{[h(v)=b]}$. The closeness between ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' follows from \Cref{lem:comm-data-processed-g}, and the normalization condition on ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' follows from it being a sub-measurement. \item In the second approximation we used \Cref{prop:closeness-of-ip} where we let ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' in the Proposition be $G^y_{[h(v)=b]} \otimes I$ and $I \otimes G^y_{[h(v)=b]}$, respectively, and let ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' denote $G^x_{[g(u)=a]} \otimes G^y_{[h(v)=b]}$. The closeness between ``$A^x_a$'' and ``$B^x_a$'' follows from \Cref{item:commuting-self-consistency}, and the normalization condition on ``$C^x_{a,b}$'' follows from it being a sub-measurement.

nodes.name: Second term near <G tensor G>
nodes.statement: This shows that the second term in \Cref{eq:gcomterms} is approximately $\bra{\psi} G \otimes G \ket{\psi}$, as desired.

nodes.name: Total error bounded by nu
nodes.statement: In total, we have incurred an error of \begin{align*} &2\cdot\left(2\sqrt{\zeta} +\sqrt{\zeta} + \frac{dm}{q} + \sqrt{\zeta} + \sqrt{\zeta} + \frac{dm}{q} + \sqrt{\nu_{\mathrm{evaluation}}} + \sqrt{\zeta} \right)\\ =~&12 \zeta^{1/2} + 2 m \cdot (d/q) + 2 \cdot \sqrt{48 m \cdot (\gamma^{1/2} + \zeta^{1/2})}\\ \leq~&12 \zeta^{1/2} + 2 m \cdot (d/q) + 14m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/4} + \zeta^{1/4}\right)\\ \leq~& 12 \zeta^{1/4} + 2m \cdot (d/q)^{1/4} + 14m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/4} + \zeta^{1/4}\right) \\ \leq~& 30m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/4}+ \zeta^{1/4} + (d/q)^{1/4} \right). \end{align*} This concludes the proof of \Cref{thm:com-main}.

nodes.name: Complete H to a measurement
nodes.statement: Let~$H$ be the sub-measurement in $\polysub{m+1}{q}{d}$ guaranteed by \Cref{lem:ld-pasting-sub-measurement}. Let $h^*$ be an arbitrary polynomial in $\polyfunc{m+1}{q}{d}$. We define the measurement~$H_{\mathrm{meas}} \in \polymeas{m+1}{q}{d}$ as follows. \begin{equation*} (H_{\mathrm{meas}})_h = \left\{\begin{array}{cl} H_{h^*} + (I- H) & \text{if $h = h^*$,}\\ H_h & \text{otherwise.} \end{array} \right. \end{equation*} This is clearly a measurement, as the sum of its POVM elements is $H + (I -H) = H$.

eq a}  ra{\psi} A^{ oldsymbol{u}}_a \otimes (H_{\mathrm{meas}})_{h} \ket{\psi}\ ={}& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \sum_{a} \sum_{h:h( oldsymbol{u})
