nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus, $A^u_a \otimes I \simeq_{\sigma} I \otimes (H_{\mathrm{meas}})_{[h(u)=a]}$. This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Write both distributions
nodes.statement: For any $z = (z_1, \ldots, z_k) \in \mathbb F_q^k$, \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} = z] & = \frac{1}{q^k},\\ \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\boldsymbol{y} = z] & = \left\{\begin{array}{cl} \frac{1}{\binom{q}{k} k!} & \text{if $z \in \distinct{k}$,}\\ 0 & \text{otherwise.} \end{array}\right. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Identify the maximizing set
nodes.statement: Because $\frac{1}{\binom{q}{k} k!} \geq \frac{1}{q^k}$, $\mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} = z] \geq \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\boldsymbol{y} = z]$ if and only if $z \notin \distinct{k}$.

nodes.name: TV equals collision probability
nodes.statement: Hence, \begin{align*} d_{\mathrm{TV}}({\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}) &= \max_{S \subseteq \mathbb F_q^k}\{\mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \in S] - \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\boldsymbol{y} \in S]\}\\ &= \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \in \overline{\distinct{k}}] - \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\boldsymbol{y} \in \overline{\distinct{k}}] = \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \in \overline{\distinct{k}}]. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Union bound
nodes.statement: We can upper-bound this probability as follows. \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}} \in \overline{\distinct{k}}] &= \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[\exists i : {\boldsymbol{x}}_i \in \{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{i-1}\}]\\ &\leq \sum_{i=2}^k \mathop{\bf Pr\/}[{\boldsymbol{x}}_i \in \{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{i-1}\}] \leq \sum_{i=2}^k \left(\frac{i-1}{q}\right) = \frac{k(k-1)}{2q}. \end{align*} This concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Overview: measure G d+1 times and interpolate
nodes.statement: The first construction of $H = \{H_h\}$ is conceptually simple: we perform the $G$ sub-measurement $d+1$ times to produce $d+1$ polynomials $g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1} \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$. We then perform polynomial interpolation to produce a single global polynomial $h \in \polyfunc{m+1}{q}{d}$. In more detail, this construction involves three steps.
nodes.statement_short: Overview: measure G d+1 times and interpolate

nodes.name: Sandwiched sequential measurement
nodes.statement: (Pasting): Let $x_1, \ldots, x_{d+1} \in \mathbb F_q$. We will define an initial ``sandwiched" measurement as follows: \begin{equation*} \widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_{d+1}}_{g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1}} = G^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdot G^{x_2}_{g_2} \cdots G^{x_{d+1}}_{g_{d+1}} \cdots G^{x_2}_{g_2} \cdot G^{x_1}_{g_1}. \end{equation*} $\widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_{d+1}}$ has a natural interpretation as the sub-measurement in which one performs the sub-measurements $G^{x_1}, G^{x_2}, \ldots, G^{x_{d+1}}$ one after another and outputs their results.

nodes.name: Interpolate outcomes into a global polynomial
nodes.statement: (Interpolation) Next, let $(x_1, \ldots, x_{d+1}) \in \distinct{d+1}$. We define the interpolated measurement \begin{equation*} H^{x_1, \ldots, x_{d+1}}_{h} = \widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_{d+1}}_{h|_{x_1}, \ldots, h|_{x_{d+1}}}. \end{equation*} This performs the $\widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_{d+1}}$ measurement and outputs the~$h$ which is consistent with the outcomes~$g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1}$ if one exists. (We note that this is not necessarily a sub-measurement if $(x_1, \ldots, x_{d+1}) \notin \distinct{d+1}$. This is because there may exist $h \neq h'$ for which $h|_{x_i} = (h')|_{x_i}$ for all $1 \leq i \leq d+1$.)
nodes.statement_short: Interpolate outcomes into a global polynomial

nodes.name: Average over distinct points
nodes.statement: (Averaging): Finally, we randomize over the choice of $(x_1, \ldots, x_{d+1})$. In other words, we define \begin{equation*} H_{h} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{({\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{d+1}) \sim \distinct{d+1}} H^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{d+1}}_h. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Announce the sketch
nodes.statement: We now sketch the argument that shows this holds, at least for constant~$d$.

nodes.name: One more G measurement changes little
nodes.statement: To do this, it is first possible to show that \begin{equation} \bra{\psi} G^{d+2} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{\Delta} \bra{\psi} G^{d+1} \otimes I \ket{\psi}, \end{equation} where $\Delta = \mathrm{poly}(m) \cdot \mathrm{poly}(\epsilon, \delta, \gamma, \zeta, d/q)$ is small. Intuitively, this is because after performing $(d+1)$ $G$ measurements, the outcome of another $G$ measurement is essentially determined due to interpolation. (The proof is of this fact is slightly subtle and involves the $Z$-boundedness condition.)
nodes.statement_short: One more G measurement changes little

nodes.name: Eigenvalue distribution mu of G
nodes.statement: From here, it is possible to derive \Cref{eq:subtract-a-G} as follows. Write the eigendecomposition $G = \sum_i \lambda_i \ket{v_i}\bra{v_i}$ of~$G$. This defines a probability distribution $\mu$ over eigenvectors, where eigenvector~$i$ occurs with probability $\mu(i) = \bra{\psi} (\ket{v_i}\bra{v_i} \otimes I) \ket{\psi}$. In this language, for any power~$k$ we can write \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} G^k \otimes I \ket{\psi} = \bra{\psi} \Big(\sum_i \lambda_i^k \ket{v_i}\bra{v_i}\Big) \otimes I \ket{\psi} = \sum_i \lambda_i^k \cdot \mu(i) = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim \mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^k]. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Rewrite the step in terms of mu
nodes.statement: Thus, \Cref{eq:step-one-of-grand-plan} is equivalent to the statement that \begin{equation} \Delta \geq \bra{\psi} G^{d+1} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \bra{\psi} G^{d+2} \otimes I \ket{\psi} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim \mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^{d+1}] - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim \mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^{d+2}] = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim\mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^{d+1}(1-\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}})]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the step in terms of mu

nodes.name: State the goal
nodes.statement: By \Cref{eq:subtract-a-G}, our goal is to bound \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi} G \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \bra{\psi} G^{d+1} \otimes I \ket{\psi} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim \mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}] - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim \mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^{d+1}] = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim\mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}(1-\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^d)]. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Scalar inequality lemma
nodes.statement: To do so, we will use the following lemma. \begin{lemma} For any real number $0 \leq \lambda \leq 1$, \begin{equation*} \lambda (1-\lambda^d) \leq 2 \cdot \Big(\lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda)\Big)^{1/(d+1)}. \end{equation*} \end{lemma} \begin{proof} The lemma is trivial for $\lambda = 1$, and so we will assume that $\lambda \neq 1$. We note that \begin{align*} \lambda^{d+1} (1-\lambda^d)^{d+1} \leq \lambda^{d+1} (1-\lambda^d) &= \lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda) \cdot \left(\frac{1-\lambda^d}{1-\lambda}\right)\\ &= \lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda) \cdot (1 + \lambda + \cdots + \lambda^{d-1}) \leq d \cdot \lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda). \end{align*} The lemma now follows by taking the $(d+1)$-st root of both sides and noting that $d^{1/(d+1)} \leq 2$ for all integers $d \geq 1$. \end{proof}

nodes.name: Apply the lemma and concavity
nodes.statement: Then \Cref{lem:looks-easy-but-took-me-a-while} implies that \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim\mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}(1-\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^d)] &\leq 2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim\mu}\Big[\Big(\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^{d+1}(1-\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}})\Big)^{1/(d+1)}\Big]\\ &\leq2\cdot \Big(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{i} \sim\mu}[\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}}^{d+1}(1-\lambda_{\boldsymbol{i}})]\Big)^{1/(d+1)} \tag{because $a \mapsto a^{1/(d+1)}$ is concave}\\ &\leq 2 \cdot \Delta^{1/(d+1)}. \tag{by \Cref{eq:equivalent-way-of-writing-grand-plan}} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Conclude the bound
nodes.statement: Thus, we have established the bound \begin{equation*} \bra{\psi}G \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \bra{\psi}G^{d+1} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \leq 2\cdot \Delta^{1/{d+1}} = 2\cdot ( \mathrm{poly}(m) \cdot \mathrm{poly}(\epsilon, \delta, \gamma, \zeta,d/q))^{1/{d+1}}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Assume lambda < 1 and bound via the geometric sum
nodes.statement: The lemma is trivial for $\lambda = 1$, and so we will assume that $\lambda \neq 1$. We note that \begin{align*} \lambda^{d+1} (1-\lambda^d)^{d+1} \leq \lambda^{d+1} (1-\lambda^d) &= \lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda) \cdot \left(\frac{1-\lambda^d}{1-\lambda}\right)\\ &= \lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda) \cdot (1 + \lambda + \cdots + \lambda^{d-1}) \leq d \cdot \lambda^{d+1}(1-\lambda). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Assume lambda < 1 and bound via the geometric sum

nodes.name: Take (d+1)-st roots
nodes.statement: The lemma now follows by taking the $(d+1)$-st root of both sides and noting that $d^{1/(d+1)} \leq 2$ for all integers $d \geq 1$.

nodes.name: Fix k >= d+1
nodes.statement: Let $k \geq d+1$ be an integer.

nodes.name: Sandwiched sequential G-hat measurement
nodes.statement: (Pasting): Let $x_1, \ldots, x_k \in \mathbb F_q$. We will define an initial ``sandwiched" measurement as follows: \begin{equation*} \widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_{k}}_{g_1, \ldots, g_{k}} = \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdot \widehat{G}^{x_2}_{g_2} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_{k}}_{g_{k}} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_2}_{g_2} \cdot \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Sum over patterns with at least d+1 polynomial outcomes
nodes.statement: (Interpolation): Next, let $(x_1, \ldots, x_{k}) \in \distinct{k}$. For any string $w \in \{0, 1\}^k$ and polynomial $h \in \polyfunc{m+1}{q}{d}$, we define $h_w$ to be the tuple $(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathcal{P}^+(m, q, d)^k$ where $g_i = \bot$ if $w_i = 0$ and $g_i = h|_{x_i}$ otherwise. We define the interpolated measurement \begin{equation*} H^{x_1, \ldots, x_{k}}_{h} = \sum_{w : |w| \geq d+1} \widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_{k}}_{h_w}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Sum over patterns with at least d+1 polynomial outcomes

nodes.name: Average over distinct points
nodes.statement: (Averaging): Finally, we randomize over the choice of $(x_1, \ldots, x_{k})$. In other words, we define \begin{equation*} H_{h} = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{({\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{k}) \sim \distinct{k}} H^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_{k}}_h. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Agreement form of strong self-consistency
nodes.statement: Because~$G$ is a projective measurement, \Cref{prop:two-notions-of-self-consistency} implies that the strong self-consistency of~$G$ from \Cref{item:ld-pasting-self-consistency} is equivalent to \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \ket{\psi} \geq \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes I\ket{\psi} - \frac{1}{2}\cdot \zeta. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Expand the squared distance
nodes.statement: Our goal is to bound \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \Vert (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2\\ =~&2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \ket{\psi}\\ =~&2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g_1} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g, h} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{h} \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes I \ket{\psi} - 2\cdot \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \ket{\psi}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: But this is at most~$\zeta$ by \Cref{eq:ld-g-self-consistency}.

nodes.name: Expand into four terms
nodes.statement: The error we wish to bound is \begin{align} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_o \Vert (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\nonumber\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}})^2 M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} + \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o)^2 G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ & \qquad - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} - \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_g \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Goal: each term near <G tensor M>
nodes.statement: We will show that all four terms in \Cref{eq:g-commute-with-gg-error} are close to $\bra{\psi} G \otimes M \ket{\psi}$, where $M = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o$.
nodes.statement_short: Goal: each term near <G tensor M>

nodes.name: First term via switching sandwiches
nodes.statement: For the first term in \Cref{eq:g-commute-with-gg-error}, we have \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}})^2 M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o\otimes I \ket{\psi} &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o\otimes I \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$G$ is projective}\\ &= \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}}\sum_o \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi}\\ &\approx_{2\sqrt{\omega}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}}\sum_o \bra{\psi} G \otimes M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \ket{\psi} \tag{by \Cref{prop:switch-sandwich} and \Cref{eq:M-self-consistent}}\\ &= \bra{\psi} G \otimes M \ket{\psi}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Second term via switching sandwiches
nodes.statement: Similarly, for the second term in \Cref{eq:g-commute-with-gg-error}, we have \begin{align*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o)^2 G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi} &=\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$M$ is projective}\\ &=\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi}\\ &\approx_{2\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \bra{\psi} M \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \ket{\psi} \tag{by \Cref{prop:switch-sandwich} and \Cref{lem:g-complete-self-consistency}}\\ &= \bra{\psi} M \otimes G \ket{\psi}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Split G^x and commute with M
nodes.statement: For the third term in \Cref{eq:g-commute-with-gg-error}, we begin by claiming that \begin{align} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi}\nonumber\\ & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} \tag{because~$G$ is projective}\\ & \approx_{\sqrt{\chi}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{align} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline*} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I) \cdot ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g}) \otimes I)\ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes I\ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g - G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g}) \otimes I) \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*} The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements. The expression inside the second square root is at most $\chi$ by \Cref{eq:M-commutes-with-G}.
nodes.statement_short: Split G^x and commute with M

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline*} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I) \cdot ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g}) \otimes I)\ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes I\ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g - G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g}) \otimes I) \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: First factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements.

nodes.name: Second factor at most chi
nodes.statement: The expression inside the second square root is at most $\chi$ by \Cref{eq:M-commutes-with-G}.

nodes.name: Move G^x_g to the other side
nodes.statement: Next, we claim that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:split-G-and-commute} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g\ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big| \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I) \cdot ((M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I) \cdot(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g))\ket{\psi}\Big|\\ &\leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}\\ &\quad \cdot \sqrt{ \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g)) \ket{\psi}}. \end{align*} The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements. The expression inside the second square root is \begin{align*} & \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_g \bra{\psi}(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot\Big(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I\Big) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_g \bra{\psi}(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g)^2 \ket{\psi}. \tag{because~$M$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*} This is at most~$\zeta$ by \Cref{item:ld-pasting-self-consistency}.
nodes.statement_short: Move G^x_g to the other side

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big| \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I) \cdot ((M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I) \cdot(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g))\ket{\psi}\Big|\\ &\leq \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}\\ &\quad \cdot \sqrt{ \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g)) \ket{\psi}}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: First factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The expression inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements.

nodes.name: Second factor
nodes.statement: The expression inside the second square root is \begin{align*} & \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_g \bra{\psi}(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot\Big(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I\Big) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}}\sum_g \bra{\psi}(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g)^2 \ket{\psi}. \tag{because~$M$ is a sub-measurement} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Bounded by zeta
nodes.statement: This is at most~$\zeta$ by \Cref{item:ld-pasting-self-consistency}.

nodes.name: Move G^x_g back
nodes.statement: Next, we claim that \begin{equation} \eqref{eq:move-G-for-great-justice} \approx_{\sqrt{\zeta}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I\ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big| \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I)) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ &\leq \sqrt{ \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g))\ket{\psi}}\\ &\quad \cdot \sqrt{ \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}. \end{align*} The expression inside the first square root is \begin{align*} & \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot \Big(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I\Big) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g))\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g)^2\ket{\psi}. \tag{because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements} \end{align*} This is at most~$\zeta$ by \Cref{item:ld-pasting-self-consistency}. The expression inside the second square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{align*} &\Big| \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I)) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ &\leq \sqrt{ \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g))\ket{\psi}}\\ &\quad \cdot \sqrt{ \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: First factor
nodes.statement: The expression inside the first square root is \begin{align*} & \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot \Big(\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I\Big) \cdot (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g))\ket{\psi}\\ \leq~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \bra{\psi} (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g)^2\ket{\psi}. \tag{because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Bounded by zeta
nodes.statement: This is at most~$\zeta$ by \Cref{item:ld-pasting-self-consistency}.

nodes.name: Second factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The expression inside the second square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements.

nodes.name: Commute G^x_g past M again
nodes.statement: Next, we claim that \begin{align} \eqref{eq:move-G-for-even-greater-justice} & = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I\ket{\psi} \tag{because~$G$ is projective}\\ & \approx_{\sqrt{\chi}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o,g} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I\ket{\psi}. \end{align} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline*} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I) \cdot(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I ) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq\sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} - G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o) \otimes I)\ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*} The expression inside the first square root is at most $\chi$ by \Cref{eq:M-commutes-with-G}. The expression inside the second square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement: To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference. \begin{multline*} \Big|\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I) \cdot(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I ) \ket{\psi}\Big|\\ \leq\sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} ((G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o - M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \cdot (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{g} - G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o) \otimes I)\ket{\psi}}\\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} (M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*}

nodes.name: First factor at most chi
nodes.statement: The expression inside the first square root is at most $\chi$ by \Cref{eq:M-commutes-with-G}.

nodes.name: Second factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The expression inside the second square root is at most~$1$ because~$G$ and~$M$ are sub-measurements.

nodes.name: Reduce to <G tensor M>
nodes.statement: Finally, \begin{align*} \eqref{eq:commute-the-G-yet-again} &=\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{o, g} \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I\ket{\psi} \tag{because~$G$ is projective}\\ &=\mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} G M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{o} \otimes I \ket{\psi}\\ &\approx_{2\sqrt{\omega}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G \otimes M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \ket{\psi} \tag{by \Cref{prop:switch-sandwich} and \Cref{eq:M-self-consistent}}\\ &= \bra{\psi} G \otimes M \ket{\psi}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Third term near <G tensor M>
nodes.statement: In total, this shows that \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{2 \sqrt{\zeta} + 2 \sqrt{\omega} + 2 \sqrt{\chi}} \bra{\psi} G \otimes M \ket{\psi}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Fourth term is the conjugate
nodes.statement: The fourth term in \Cref{eq:g-commute-with-gg-error} is the Hermitian conjugate of the third term. As a result, \Cref{eq:term-three-for-use-right-now} implies that \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_o \bra{\psi} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} M^{\boldsymbol{y}}_o G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \approx_{2 \sqrt{\zeta} + 2 \sqrt{\omega} + 2 \sqrt{\chi}} \bra{\psi} G \otimes M \ket{\psi} \end{equation*} as well.

nodes.name: Combine the errors
nodes.statement: In total, this gives an error of \begin{equation*} 2\sqrt{\omega} + 2\sqrt{\zeta} + 2 \cdot\left(2 \sqrt{\zeta} + 2 \sqrt{\omega} + 2 \sqrt{\chi}\right) = 6 \sqrt{\zeta} + 6 \sqrt{\omega} + 4 \sqrt{\chi}. \end{equation*} This proves the claimed bound.

nodes.name: Recall commutativity of G
nodes.statement: By \Cref{eq:quote-com-main}, \begin{equation} G^x_g G^y_h \otimes I \approx_{\nu_{\mathrm{commute}}} G^y_h G^x_g \otimes I. \end{equation}

nodes.name: First application of the switcheroo lemma
nodes.statement: Now we apply \Cref{lem:commutativity-switcheroo} to \Cref{eq:com-main-copy}. To do so, we set the ``$\{M^y_o\}$" sub-measurement to be $\{G^x_g\}$, and therefore $\mathcal{O} = \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$. This implies that \begin{equation} G^x_g G^y \otimes I \approx_{\theta_1} G^y G^x_g \otimes I \end{equation} for $\theta_1 = 12 \sqrt{\zeta} + 4 \sqrt{\nu_{\mathrm{commute}}}$.
nodes.statement_short: First application of the switcheroo lemma

nodes.name: Second application of the switcheroo lemma
nodes.statement: Next, we apply \Cref{lem:commutativity-switcheroo} to \Cref{eq:applied-the-lemma-to-com-main-copy}. This time, we let $\mathcal{O}$ be a set containing a single outcome, and for this outcome~$o$, we set $M^y_o = G^y$. This implies that \begin{equation*} G^x G^y \otimes I \approx_{\theta_2} G^y G^x \otimes I \end{equation*} for $\theta_2 = 12 \sqrt{\zeta} + 4 \sqrt{\theta_1}$. This uses \Cref{lem:g-complete-self-consistency} for the strong self-consistency of $\{M^y_o\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Second application of the switcheroo lemma

nodes.statement:
We now show that $

nodes.statement_short: Bound theta_1 and theta_2 by nu_2

nodes.name: Bound theta_1
nodes.statement: First, using $\sqrt{30} \leq 6$, we have \begin{align*} \theta_1 = 12 \sqrt{\zeta} + 4 \sqrt{\nu_{\mathrm{commute}}} &= 12 \sqrt{\zeta} + 4 \sqrt{30 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/4} + \zeta^{1/4} + (d/q)^{1/4}\right)}\\ &\leq 12 \zeta^{1/8} + 24m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/8} +\zeta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\right)\\ &\leq 36 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/8} + \zeta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\right). \end{align*} This is clearly less than $\nu_2$.

nodes.name: Bound theta_2
nodes.statement: Next, we have \begin{align*} \theta_2 = 12 \sqrt{\zeta} + 4 \sqrt{\theta_1} &\leq 12 \sqrt{\zeta} + 4 \sqrt{36 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/8} + \zeta^{1/8} + (d/q)^{1/8}\right)}\\ &\leq 12 \zeta^{1/16} + 24m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right)\\ &\leq 36 m \cdot \left( \gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right). \end{align*} This is equal to $\nu_2$, which completes the proof.

nodes.name: Commutator with G^y_bot
nodes.statement: First, we note that \begin{equation*} G^x_g G^y_{\bot} - G^y_{\bot} G^x_g = G^x_g \cdot (I - G^y) - (I- G^y)\cdot G^x_g = G^y G^x_g - G^x_g G^y. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Bound it by nu_2
nodes.statement: Hence, by \Cref{cor:commuting-with-G-complete}, \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}}\sum_g \Vert (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}}\sum_g \Vert (G^{\boldsymbol{y}} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g - G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 \leq \nu_2. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Commutator of two incomplete parts
nodes.statement: Next, we note that \begin{align*} G^x_{\bot} G^y_{\bot} - G^y_{\bot} G^x_{\bot} &= (I - G^x) \cdot (I - G^y) - (I - G^y) \cdot (I - G^x)\\ & = (I - G^x - G^y + G^x G^y) - (I - G^y - G^x + G^y G^x)\\ &= G^x G^y - G^y G^x. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Bound it by nu_2
nodes.statement: As a result, by \Cref{cor:commuting-with-G-complete}, \begin{equation*} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \Vert (G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot}) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 = \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \Vert (G^{\boldsymbol{y}} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} - G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}) \otimes I \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 \leq \nu_2.\qedhere \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Self-consistency of G-hat
nodes.statement: We begin with \Cref{eq:gselfconall}. To prove this, we wish to bound \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g} \Vert(\widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \sum_{g \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2 + \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}} \Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot} \otimes I - I \otimes G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot}) \ket{\psi} \Vert^2\\ \leq~& \zeta + \zeta = 2\zeta, \end{align*} by \Cref{item:ld-pasting-self-consistency} and \Cref{cor:g-bot-self-consistency}.

nodes.name: Commutation of G-hat
nodes.statement:
Next, we show \Cref{eq:gcomall}. To prove this, we wish to bound  egin{align*} &\mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h} \Vert(\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g \widehat{G}^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h - \widehat{G}^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\ =~&\mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h - G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 + \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{ ot} - G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{ ot} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\ & \quad + \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g\in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{ ot} - G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_{ ot} G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 + \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}},  oldsymbol{y}} \sum_{h\in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot} G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h - G^{ oldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{ oldsymbol{x}}}_{ ot}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\ \leq~& 
u_{\mathrm{commute}} + 3
u_2, \end{align*} by \Cref{eq:quote-com-main} and \Cref{cor:commuting-with-G-incomplete}. We can therefore bound this by  egin{align*} 
u_{\mathrm{commute}} + 3
u_2 &= 30 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/4} +\zeta^{1/4} + (d/q)^{1/4}ight) + 3 \cdot 36 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}ight)\ &\leq 30 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}ight) + 3 \cdot 36 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}ight)\ &= 138 m \cdot \left( \gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} +(d/q)^{1/16}ight). \end{align*} This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Split into four commutator terms
nodes.statement: To prove this, we wish to bound \begin{align*} &\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h} \Vert(\widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g \widehat{G}^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h - \widehat{G}^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\\ =~&\mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g, h \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 + \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\\ & \quad + \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{g\in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_{\bot} G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_g) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2 + \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}, \boldsymbol{y}} \sum_{h\in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}} \Vert(G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot} G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h - G^{\boldsymbol{y}}_h G^{{\boldsymbol{x}}}_{\bot}) \otimes I \ket{\psi}\Vert^2\\ \leq~& \nu_{\mathrm{commute}} + 3\nu_2, \end{align*} by \Cref{eq:quote-com-main} and \Cref{cor:commuting-with-G-incomplete}.

nodes.name: Bound by nu_3
nodes.statement: We can therefore bound this by \begin{align*} \nu_{\mathrm{commute}} + 3\nu_2 &= 30 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/4} +\zeta^{1/4} + (d/q)^{1/4}\right) + 3 \cdot 36 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right)\\ &\leq 30 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right) + 3 \cdot 36 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right)\\ &= 138 m \cdot \left( \gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} +(d/q)^{1/16}\right). \end{align*} This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Chain of applications
Count the applications
nodes.statement: In total, we have $(k-2) + (k-2) \leq 2k$ applications of \Cref{eq:gselfconall} with error $2\zeta$ each and $(k-1) \leq k$ applications of \Cref{eq:gcomall} with error $\nu_3$ each.

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement: By \Cref{prop:triangle-inequality-for-approx_delta}, this implies that \begin{equation*} G^{x_1}_{g_1} G^{x_2}_{g_2} \cdots G^{x_k}_{g_k} \otimes I \approx_{3k \cdot (4k \zeta + k\nu_3)} G^{x_2}_{g_2}\cdots G^{x_{k-1}}_{g_{k-1}} G^{x_k}_{g_k} G^{x_1}_{g_1} \otimes I, \end{equation*} as claimed.

nodes.name: Bound by nu_4
nodes.statement: We can bound this as follows. \begin{align*} 3k \cdot (4k \zeta + k\nu_3) & = 12k^2 \zeta + 3k^2 \nu_3\\ &= 12k^2 \zeta + 3 k^2 \cdot 138 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right)\\ &\leq 12k^2 \zeta^{1/16} + 414 k^2 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right)\\ &\leq 426 k^2 m \cdot \left(\gamma^{1/16} + \zeta^{1/16} + (d/q)^{1/16}\right). \end{align*} This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Sum out later outcomes
nodes.statement: To begin, we note that \begin{align*} \sum_{g_{i+1}, \ldots, g_k} \widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} & = \sum_{g_{i+1}, \ldots, g_k} \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_k}_{g_k} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1}\\ & = \sum_{g_{i+1}, \ldots, g_{k-1}} \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdots \Big(\sum_{g_k} \widehat{G}^{x_k}_{g_k} \Big)\cdots \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1}\\ & = \sum_{g_{i+1}, \ldots, g_{k-1}} \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_{k-1}}_{g_{k-1}} \cdot I \cdot \widehat{G}^{x_{k-1}}_{g_{k-1}}\cdots \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \tag{because $\widehat{G}^{x_k}$ is a measurement}\\ & = \sum_{g_{i+1}, \ldots, g_{k-1}} \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_{k-1}}_{g_{k-1}} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \tag{because $\widehat{G}^{x_{k-1}}$ is projective}\\ & \cdots \\ & = \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_{i}}_{g_{i}} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_1}_{g_1}\\ & = \widehat{H}^{x_1, \ldots, x_i}_{g_1, \ldots, g_i}. \end{align*}

Abbreviate the first i-1 factors

eq  ot}  ra{\psi}\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i}\cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} )^\dagger \otimes (I - B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{[f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})]}) \ket{\psi}. \end{align} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference.  egin{multline*} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, { oldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i: g_i 
eq  ot}  ra{\psi} ((\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} - \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}}) \otimes I) \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} )^\dagger \otimes (I - B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{[f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})]})) \ket{\psi}\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, { oldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i: g_i 
eq  ot}  ra{\psi} ((\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} - \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}}) \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i}\cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}})^\dagger - (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}})^\dagger \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i})) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, { oldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i: g_i 
eq  ot}  ra{\psi} (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} )^\dagger) \otimes (I - B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{[f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})]})^2 \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*} The term inside the first square root is at most  egin{equation} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, { oldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i}  ra{\psi} ((\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} - \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}}) \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i}\cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}})^\dagger - (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}})^\dagger \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i})) \otimes I \ket{\psi}, \end{equation} which is at most~$
u_4$ by \Cref{lem:commute-g-half-sandwich}. The term inside the second square root is at most~$1$ because~$B$ and~$\widehat{G}$ are measurements.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement:
To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference.  egin{multline*} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, { oldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i: g_i 
eq  ot}  ra{\psi} ((\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} - \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}}) \otimes I) \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} )^\dagger \otimes (I - B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{[f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})]})) \ket{\psi}\ \leq \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, { oldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i: g_i 
eq  ot}  ra{\psi} ((\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} - \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}}) \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i}\cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}})^\dagger - (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}})^\dagger \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i})) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}\ \cdot \sqrt{\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, { oldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i: g_i

nodes.name: First factor at most nu_4
nodes.statement: The term inside the first square root is at most \begin{equation} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{\boldsymbol{u}} \mathop{\bf E\/}_{{\boldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, {\boldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i} \bra{\psi} ((\widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} - \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}}) \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i}\cdot (\widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}})^\dagger - (\widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}})^\dagger \cdot \widehat{G}^{{\boldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i})) \otimes I \ket{\psi}, \end{equation} which is at most~$\nu_4$ by \Cref{lem:commute-g-half-sandwich}.

nodes.name: Second factor at most 1
nodes.statement: The term inside the second square root is at most~$1$ because~$B$ and~$\widehat{G}$ are measurements.

nodes.statement:
Next, we claim that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:gonna-need-a-bigger-cauchy-schwarz} \approx_{\sqrt{
u_4}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, { oldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i: g_i 
eq  ot}  ra{\psi}\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} )^\dagger \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i}\otimes (I - B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_{[f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})]}) \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we bound the magnitude of the difference.  egin{multline*} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \dots, { oldsymbol{x}}_i} \sum_{g_1, \dots, g_i: g_i

eq  ot}  ra{\psi} ((\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} - \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}}) \cdot ((\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}})^\dagger \cdot \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} - \widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_i}_{g_i} \cdot (\widehat{G}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_{<i}}_{g_{<i}}))^\dagger) \otimes I \ket{\psi}}. \end{multline*} The term inside the first square root is at most~$1$ because~$B$ and $\widehat{G}$ are measurements. nodes.statement:
In particular, we claim that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:sum-restricted-to-global-polynomial} \approx_{ rac{k^2}{q} + k \cdot
u_5 +  rac{md}{q}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{	au}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi}. \end{equation} To show this, we note that $\eqref{eq:remove-the-restriction} \geq \eqref{eq:sum-restricted-to-global-polynomial}$. onumber\ &= \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi}, \end{align} because~$B$ is a measurement. Next, we claim that  egin{equation} \eqref{eq:B-appears-out-of-thin-air} \approx_{ rac{k^2}{q} + k \cdot
u_5} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[ orall i\in 	au, f( oldsymbol{y}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})]. \end{equation} To show this, we note that $\eqref{eq:B-appears-out-of-thin-air} \geq \eqref{eq:add-in-indicator-for-f-and-g}$. Thus, it suffices to upper bound their difference $\eqref{eq:B-appears-out-of-thin-air} - \eqref{eq:add-in-indicator-for-f-and-g}$. This is given by  egin{equation} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au: |	au|\geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\exists i \in 	au, f( oldsymbol{y}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]. \end{equation} Recall that ${ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k \sim \mathbb F_q$ are sampled independently and uniformly at random. Then \Cref{prop:ld-dnoteq} implies that \Cref{eq:about-to-swap-x-for-y} is $(k^2/q)$-close to  egin{align*} &\mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{	au: |	au|\geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}({ oldsymbol{x}})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\exists i \in 	au, f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]\ \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au| \geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{	au}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\exists i \in 	au, f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]\ \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{	au} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{	au}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\exists i \in 	au, f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]\ \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{	au} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathsf{Outcomes}_{	au}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot \Big(\sum_{i\in 	au}  oldsymbol{1}[f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})]\Big)\ =~& \sum_i \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{g_1, \ldots, g_k : g_i 
eq  ot} \sum_{f: f({ oldsymbol{x}}_i) 
eq g_i( oldsymbol{u})}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi}\ =~& \sum_i \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{{ oldsymbol{x}}_1, \ldots, { oldsymbol{x}}_k} \sum_{g_1, \ldots, g_k : g_i 
eq  ot} \sum_{a

u_5) 	ag{by \Cref{lem:ld-sandwich-line-one-point}}\ =~& k \cdot 
u_5. \end{align*} Returning to \Cref{eq:add-in-indicator-for-f-and-g}, we introduce the notation $\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g,  oldsymbol{y},  oldsymbol{u})$ to indicate whether there is a consistent degree-$d$ polynomial interpolating the $g_i$'s along the line in direction~$u$. In other words,  egin{equation*} \mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g,  oldsymbol{y},  oldsymbol{u}) = \left\{ egin{array}{rl} 1 & 	ext{if $\exists f$ such that $f( oldsymbol{y}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})$ for all $i \in 	au$,}\ 0 & 	ext{otherwise.} \end{array}ight. \end{equation*} Clearly, for any $f$,  egin{equation*}  oldsymbol{1}[ orall i\in 	au, f( oldsymbol{y}_i) = g_i( oldsymbol{u})] \leq  oldsymbol{1}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g,  oldsymbol{y},  oldsymbol{u})] \end{equation*} because the left-hand side indicates whether~$f$ is the consistent degree-$d$ polynomial interpolating along direction~$u$. As a result,  egin{align} \eqref{eq:add-in-indicator-for-f-and-g} \leq~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au|\geq d+1} \sum_f \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, oldsymbol{y}, oldsymbol{u})]
onumber\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au|\geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes \Big(\sum_f B^{ oldsymbol{u}}_f\Big) \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, oldsymbol{y}, oldsymbol{u})]
onumber\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{u}} \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au|\geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \cdot  oldsymbol{1}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, oldsymbol{y}, oldsymbol{u})]
onumber\ =~& \mathop{ f E/}_{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k} \sum_{	au:|	au|\geq d+1} \sum_{(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}( oldsymbol{y})}}  ra{\psi} \widehat{H}^{ oldsymbol{y}_1, \ldots,  oldsymbol{y}_k}_{g_1, \ldots, g_k} \otimes I \ket{\psi} \cdot \mathop{ f Pr/}_{ oldsymbol{u}}[\mathsf{Consistent}_{	au}(g, oldsymbol{y}, oldsymbol{u})]. \end{align} Let us now fix $(y_1, \ldots, y_k) \in \mathsf{Distinct}_k$, a type $	au$ such that $|	au| \geq d+1$, and $(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \overline{\mathsf{Global}_{	au}(y)}$. Suppose without loss of generality that $	au_1 = \cdots = 	au_{d+1} = 1$, so that $g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1} \in \polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$. Then there is a unique polynomial $h^* \in \polyfunc{m+1}{q}{d}$ which interpolates $g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1}$. Then there is a unique polynomial $h^* \in \polyfunc{m+1}{q}{d}$ which interpolates $g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1}$. In other words, for all $1 \leq i \leq d+1$, \begin{equation*} h^*(u, y_i) = g_i(u). \end{equation*} In addition, for any $u$, $(h^*)|_u$ is the unique degree-$d$ polynomial which interpolates $g_1, \ldots, g_{d+1}$ along the line in direction~$u$. nodes.name: Notation for prefixes and suffixes of types and outcomes
nodes.statement: We begin by introducing some notation that we will use throughout the proof. Let $\tau \in \{0, 1\}^k$ be a type. Then we define \begin{equation*} \tau_{< \ell} = (\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_{\ell-1}) \in \{0, 1\}^{\ell-1}, \quad \tau_{> \ell} = (\tau_{\ell+1}, \ldots, \tau_{k}) \in \{0,1\}^{k-\ell}, \end{equation*} and we define $\tau_{\leq \ell}$ and $\tau_{\geq \ell}$ similarly. In addition, given $(g_1, \ldots, g_k) \in \mathcal{P}^+(m, q, d)^{k}$, we define \begin{equation*} g_{< \ell} = (g_1, \ldots, g_{\ell-1}) \in \mathcal{P}^+(m, q, d)^{\ell-1}, \quad g_{> \ell} = (g_{\ell+1}, \ldots, g_{k}) \in \mathcal{P}^+(m, q, d)^{k-\ell} \end{equation*} and we define $g_{\leq \ell}$ and $g_{\geq \ell}$ similarly. Using this notation, we can write \begin{equation*} \widehat{H}^{x_{\geq \ell}}_{g_{\geq \ell}} = \widehat{H}^{x_{\ell}, \ldots, x_k}_{g_{\ell}, \ldots, g_k}. \end{equation*} Next, we introduce the notation \begin{equation*} \widehat{G}^{x_{\geq \ell}}_{g_{\geq \ell}} = \widehat{G}^{x_{\ell}}_{g_{\ell}} \cdots \widehat{G}^{x_k}_{g_k}. \end{equation*} This satisfies the recurrence relation \begin{equation} \widehat{G}^{x_{\geq \ell}}_{g_{\geq \ell}} = \widehat{G}^{x_{\ell}}_{g_{\ell}} \cdot \widehat{G}^{x_{> \ell}}_{g_{> \ell}}. \end{equation} Furthermore, we can write \begin{equation} \widehat{H}^{x_{\geq \ell}}_{g_{\geq \ell}} = (\widehat{G}^{x_{\geq \ell}}_{g_{\geq \ell}}) \cdot (\widehat{G}^{x_{\geq \ell}}_{g_{\geq \ell}})^\dagger. \end{equation} Finally, we will write $\mathsf{O}_{\tau}$ as shorthand for $\mathsf{Outcomes}_{\tau}$.
